- [x] TODO-5640: String heap hot paths: O(1) frees, chunk index, region cache
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-02
  - phase: Strings and slices (docs/spec/strings-and-views.md, Parity with `std::string`), speed
  - parallel_track: string-quality
  - scope: Profiling `short_strings` (110 to 140x `std::string`) showed about 90% of its time in the linear `std::find` over a chunk's free list that `VmTextHeap::release` used to detect a double free, plus a linear scan of all chunks in `chunkWithFreeBlock`, a full recount of empty chunks on every chunk-emptying free, and a `std::map` search in `VmHeapCore::byteAt` for every byte access. Fix them in `VmTextHeapBody.inc` and `VmHeapCoreBody.inc` (shared by the VM and the optimized C++ runtime): a per-block free flag, a per-size-class ordered set of chunks with free blocks (lowest chunk first, as the scan was), an empty-chunk counter, and a one-entry last-region cache in `byteAt` that `releaseByteRegion` clears. Behavior and error messages stay the same; a free in the unused tail of a chunk becomes an invalid-address error.
  - acceptance:
    - the text-heap unit suite passes with new cases (tail free rejected, lowest chunk first with exact chunk accounting, randomized allocate/free cycles with every double free rejected); the TODO-5628 conformance suite and benchmarks pass with lowered budgets; `short_strings` is under 15x `std::string`; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the string heap and the byte-region lookup; byte loops are TODO-5629.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-02
  - result: Heap hot paths fixed in VmTextHeapBody.inc and VmHeapCoreBody.inc: O(1) double-free flag per block, per-class ordered set of chunks with free blocks, empty-chunk counter, one-entry last-region cache in byteAt; a free in a chunk tail is now an invalid-address error. short_strings 110-140x -> 5-9x std::string; insert_front 43-61x -> 32-48x; copy_text 15-35x -> 17-24x. Three new text-heap cases; conformance suite and budgets updated. Full release gate green (1876 of 1876, AppKit drivers skipped).

- [x] TODO-5639: A binding whose declared type is an imported short name skipped the Copy helper
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-02
  - phase: Strings and slices (docs/spec/strings-and-views.md), found by the TODO-5628 suite
  - parallel_track: lifecycle-strings
  - scope: `[String mut] s{stringFrom("hello")}` then `[String mut] c{s}` shared one heap block: `c.append("!!")` grew the text in place while `s.count()` stayed 5, and at scope end the VM stopped with `string heap block freed twice` (size 1 to 31) or `invalid string heap free address` (32 and up); `optexe` aborted the same way. Spelling the type `/std/text/String` worked, and so did a user struct with `Copy`. Cause: the struct-binding branch of the lowerer (`IrLowererLowerStatementsBindingsContinued.h`) resolved the slot layout from `info.structTypeName` (the full path) but looked up the `Copy` helper, and the disarm of a temporary source, with the raw type-transform name `structTypeName` (`String`, the imported short name), so `defMap.find("String/Copy")` missed and the struct was only bit-copied. Fix: use `info.structTypeName` for those three lookups. Tests: bindings of every spelling copy and free once; a copy in a 300-iteration loop; the TODO-5628 suite now uses the binding form.
  - acceptance:
    - the repro programs copy instead of aliasing (counts differ after appending to one side) and never fault; `Copy` also runs for a user struct; the TODO-5628 conformance suite uses `[String] copy{s}`; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the three lookups in the struct-binding branch; no new move/use-after-move checking.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-02
  - result: Fixed in IrLowererLowerStatementsBindingsContinued.h: the struct-binding branch used the raw type-transform name (the imported short name String) for the Copy helper lookup and the temporary-source disarm while the layout used the resolved path, so a binding from a binding only bit-copied and the block was freed twice. Three lookups now use info.structTypeName. New tests: bindings of every spelling copy and free once; a 300-iteration copy loop; the conformance suite uses the binding form. Full release gate green (1876 of 1876, AppKit drivers skipped).

- [x] TODO-5540: `StringView`: a borrowed view of literals and Strings
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-10-08
  - phase: Strings and slices (docs/spec/strings-and-views.md), first of six leaves for the text view
  - parallel_track: string-view
  - scope: A borrowed read-only view of text in any byte region: the stdlib struct `StringView` (pointer and byte count, `/std/text`), made from a String with `s.view()` and from a string literal with `textOf("...")`. A literal's bytes get an address through the new `__pstext_literal([string] text) -> Pointer<u8>` text host function, answered by the VM and the optimized C++ runtime (a NUL-terminated byte region made on first use and kept for the run; `VmTextHeap::literal`), so there is no new opcode and no PSIR change. Operations of this leaf: `count`, `empty`, `byteAt` (faults out of range), `equals(StringView)`, `equalsText(string)`. The existing `string` stays the static literal type for now (print, map keys, `File` paths, host parameters and every current program are unchanged); `StringView` is the type for text that is not a literal, and unifying the two spellings is TODO-5621. Native backends reject `__pstext_literal` until TODO-5622 follow-ups.
  - acceptance:
    - VM and `optexe` tests: view of a String and of a literal, empty text (a literal and an empty String), `byteAt` ends and out of range, `equals` and `equalsText` for equal, different and shorter text, a view after the String grew; the existing suite passes unchanged; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the view type, literals and Strings as sources, and the operations above on the VM and optexe; borrowing rules, slicing, search and parsing are TODO-5618 to TODO-5620.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-02
  - result: StringView (stdlib struct, pointer+count) made by s.view() or textOf("literal"); a literal gets an address from the new __pstext_literal text host function (VM and optexe; no opcode, no PSIR change); count/empty/byteAt/equals/equalsText. string stays the static literal type; unifying is TODO-5621. Release gate green (1876 of 1876 once the vm_string_lookups lint was satisfied via vmStringCount).

Both had one cause: `inferBaseSetupSemanticFieldAccessKind` (`src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerInferenceBaseKindInternal.h`) looked the receiver's recorded type text up as a struct path, and the receiver of an inlined method is recorded as `Reference<Type>`; the failed lookup also left a layout error behind. It now unwraps `Reference<T>` and `Pointer<T>` before building the candidate paths. With that, `StringView.find(needle)`, `rfind(needle)`, `parseI32()`, `first()` and `last()` return `Maybe` (`Maybe<i32>`, `Maybe<u8>`), and `Maybe` gains `unwrapOr(fallback)` to read a value out. (`pick`, `plus` and other builtin names are not usable as user function or method names: they capture the builtin.)
  - acceptance:
    - VM and `optexe` tests: 170 search cases and 27 integer texts where the `Maybe` forms agree with `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`/`parseI32Or`, and `first`/`last` on empty and non-empty text; every existing test passes; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the unwrap in the field-access kind inference and the `Maybe` forms; no change to sum lowering.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-03
  - result: Reference/Pointer receiver unwrap in field-access kind inference; Maybe-valued StringView find/rfind/parseI32/first/last and Maybe.unwrapOr, VM and optexe differential tests

- [x] TODO-5655: Callee-reachable receiver addresses so `mut` methods can be real calls
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-03
  - phase: Strings and slices (docs/spec/strings-and-views.md), split from TODO-5645
  - parallel_track: lowering-gaps
  - scope: Measured 2026-11-03: the 8-call `StringMap<i32>` sample still takes 3.2 s end to end under `primevm` and `--emit=ir` writes 33 MB for it, because `insert`, `erase` and the other `mut` methods are inlined at every call site and the read-only slice of TODO-5645 does not reach them. A local address is an index into the current frame (`indirectSlot` in `src/runtime/VmFastKernel.cpp`, `AddressOfLocal` in `VmExecutionKernel.cpp`), so a callee cannot write through a caller's address. Choose one model and apply it in every consumer of the IR: (a) a copy-in/copy-out receiver (the callee returns its modified receiver slots through a result area that the call site stores back), or (b) frame-qualified addresses (a call-depth or frame-base tag that `AddressOfLocal`/`LoadIndirect`/`StoreIndirect` honor in the VM kernels, the simple and optimizing C++ emitters, the arm64 backend and the GLSL/Wasm validators). Then let `computeRealCallEligibleDefinitionPaths` accept `mut` receivers and struct parameters, including `/std/collections/` receivers once their collection-record metadata survives the call.
  - findings (2026-11-03): copy-out through the operand stack (the callee pushes its receiver slots below the result and the call site pops them back into the receiver) needs no VM change, since `Call`/`Return` share one operand stack, but it makes a function leave more than its result behind. The optimizing C++ emitter and the native backends compile each IR function to a function that returns only its result, and virtual-register lowering assumes a `Call` consumes its parameters and yields at most one value, so the trick works in the VM only. A portable copy-out needs a result area that survives the frame (the heap, or a frame-qualified address), which is the work this block scopes.
  - result (2026-11-03): for the VM target a `mut` method is a real call that receives the address of a heap copy of its receiver (`HeapAlloc`, copy in, call, copy back, `HeapFree`; `IrLowererLowerInlineCalls.cpp`), and a struct passed by value is its slots on the operand stack, rebuilt in a block of the callee's frame (`IrLowererLowerStatementsCallsStage.cpp`). The heap address is valid in every frame, so no kernel or backend changed. Eligibility (`computeRealCallEligibleDefinitionPaths(..., allowMutReceivers)`) takes these only for the VM target and keeps structs with `Copy`/`Move`/`Destroy` helpers, `/std/collections/` receivers and definitions with a generated tail value inline. Measured with the 8-call `StringMap<i32>` sample under `primevm`: 3.2 s before, 1.9 to 2.0 s after (a program that only constructs the map takes 1.0 s). The serialized `--emit=ir` module stays inlined (33 MB) because that target is backend-neutral.
  - acceptance:
    - the 8-call `StringMap` sample lowers in under 2 s and its IR is under a quarter of today's size; every existing test passes with identical output; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the addressing model and the eligibility extension; no inliner tuning.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-03
  - result: mut methods and by-value struct parameters are real calls on the VM target via a heap copy of the receiver; sample 3.2 s to 1.9 s

- [x] TODO-5645: Real calls for struct-receiver methods (library code is inlined at every call site)
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-02
  - phase: Strings and slices (docs/spec/strings-and-views.md), found building TODO-5625
  - parallel_track: lowering-gaps
  - scope: Only definitions whose parameters and result are all plain scalars can be lowered as real `Call`s (`computeRealCallEligibleDefinitionPaths` in `src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererRecursionAnalysis.h`); a method with a struct receiver, a pointer or a view is inlined at every call site. For stdlib types built from small methods this multiplies: lowering a program that makes one `StringMap<i32>` and calls it eight times took about 5 s before TODO-5653 and takes 2.4 s after it (one `insert` 1.5 s), and `vector<i32>` alone costs 0.8 s. Extend real-call emission to definitions with struct and pointer parameters (pass the address of the receiver, as the inline path does for `mut` parameters), starting with the non-recursive library methods that are called from more than one site.
  - first slice done (2026-11-03): read-only (`mut`-free) struct helper methods with scalar parameters and a scalar or void result, outside `/std/collections/`, are now real calls when they have two or more call sites (`computeRealCallEligibleDefinitionPaths`, `IrLowererLowerStatementsCallsStage.cpp`, `IrLowererLowerInlineCalls.cpp`). A local address is an index into the current frame (`VmFastKernel.cpp` `indirectSlot`), so a callee cannot read through the address of a caller's struct; the receiver therefore goes as a copy of its slots on the operand stack, rebuilt in a block of the callee's frame. Measured: the 8-call `StringMap` sample still lowers in 2.4 s because its methods are `mut` or called once. Still open: `mut` receivers and struct parameters (they need a write-back or an addressing model where a callee can reach a caller's frame, in the VM, the C++ runtime and the native emitters), the `copy`/`move` lifecycle, and the collection records whose locals carry element and key/value kinds.
  - remaining work (2026-11-03): the `mut` receiver and struct parameter part is split out as TODO-5655; this block closes with it.
  - design notes (2026-11-03): the pieces exist but are not joined. (1) Eligibility (`computeRealCallEligibleDefinitionPaths`) rejects `takesImplicitThis` helpers, `mut` parameters and any non-scalar parameter; the call site (`IrLowererLowerInlineCalls.cpp`, the `realCallReservationIndex` branch) pushes `emitExpr` values, and `IrLowererLowerStatementsCallsStage.cpp` pops them into scalar `Value` locals 0..N-1. (2) The inline path binds a struct parameter without copying when the argument is a struct local (`LoadLocal` of the struct local is its address, stored in the parameter's local; a `mut` struct parameter becomes `Kind::Reference` the same way) and copies slots only for other arguments (`emitInlineDefinitionCallParameters`, `IrLowererInlineParamHelpers.cpp`). (3) `buildCallableDefinitionCallContext` (`IrLowererStatementCallHelpers.cpp`) already builds the locals of a definition lowered as its own function, including the implicit `this`, struct layouts and bare struct names, from `inferCallParameterLocalInfo`; the real-call body loop should reuse it instead of the scalar-only loop. (4) Open questions: the `copy`/`move` parameter lifecycle (drop flags are released at the call site today), argument shapes that need a temporary, and `isStructParamMatch` aliases for bare imported names (TODO-5650). A first slice could take only struct receivers (`this`) of non-`mut`-free methods with scalar or void results.
  - acceptance:
    - the 8-call `StringMap` sample lowers in under 2 s; the IR of programs that call a method from several sites shrinks; every existing test passes with identical output; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: eligibility and emission for struct/pointer parameters; no inliner tuning beyond that.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-03
  - result: Struct-receiver methods are real calls: read-only ones by slot copy, mut ones through TODO-5655; sample 3.2 s to 1.9 s on the VM

- [x] TODO-5638: Shared immutable strings (`SharedString`)

  - status: done

  - parallel_track: strings
  - scope: `/std/text/shared` (`stdlib/std/text/shared.prime`, a lazy module): a `SharedString` is an immutable, reference-counted text. Copying it shares the bytes and adds one to the count, `view()` is a `StringView` over the shared bytes, `owners()` reports the count, and the last owner's `Destroy` frees the block. - [x] TODO-5670: A `[ref]`-captured vector of `Function`-holding structs passes to a parameter correctly
  - owner: ai

  - phase: Web server blockers (found probing closures for a request router)
  - parallel_track: closures-ref-captures
  - scope: With `[struct] Route { [i32] code  [Function<i32, i32> mut] handler }`, a local `[vector<Route> mut] routes{...}` holding two routes, `call_all([vector<Route> mut] routes, [i32] input)` that sums `routes[i].handler(input)`, and `[mut] app{[ref routes]([i32] x) { return(call_all(routes, x)) }}`, `app(10i32)` compiles but faults on VM and optexe with `VM error: unaligned indirect address in IR: 68`. Add a `BytePointer` host kind: semantics requires each `Pointer<u8>` host parameter to be followed by a `u64` length; `src/backend/IrToOptCppEmitter.cpp` passes `uint8_t *` resolved with `rt.heap.byteSpan(address, length)` and faults with `invalid byte pointer passed to host function` on a bad span (address 0 with length 0 passes `nullptr`). `hostCType`, the IR serializer and printer, and `VmHost`/`Script::bind` (which reject the kind with a clear message) follow. Socket `recv`/`send` and any other byte-buffer host function need this.
  - acceptance:
    - an optexe test with a small C++ shim that fills and sums a `vector<u8>` buffer through `sliceMut`/`data`; a length past the buffer faults instead of reading; IR dump shows the new kind; docs/spec/host-and-core-library.md describes the convention
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the host kind and its pairing rule; no socket code.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-06
  - result: IrHostValueKind::BytePointer (PSIR v32, printed `bytes`): a `Pointer<u8>` host parameter outside `__pstext_*` lowers to it and must be followed by a `u64` length; optexe passes `uint8_t *` from `rt.heap.byteSpan` and faults with `invalid byte pointer passed to host function` (nullptr for 0/0); the VM, Script::bind, the simple C++ emitter and native reject it by name; fixtures tests/fixtures/host_calls/bytes_host{,_overrun}.prime + bytes_impl.cpp, tests in primestruct.backend.cpp_strings and primestruct.ir.module_printer; spec in docs/spec/host-and-core-library.md (Byte buffers)

  - scope: Add `stdlib/std/http/server.prime` (`import /std/http/server/*`) with `ServerConfig` (port, backlog, maxRequestBytes, accept/read/write timeouts, loopbackOnly, announce), `ServeError` (a `/std/net` code with `why()`), `serve<Handler>(handler, config)` (until `stopRequested()`) and `serveUntil<Handler, Stop>(handler, config, stop)`, each returning `Result<ServeError>`. Rejected requests get a bare status, and connection errors close that connection. -4 (EINTR) and accept timeouts re-check the stop condition, and only a failed `listen` returns an error. `announce` prints `listening on <port>` to stderr.   - result: stdlib/std/http/server.prime (/std/http/server): ServerConfig, ServeError, serve (until stopRequested) and serveUntil; single-threaded accept/read/parse/handle/write/close with a read deadline, bare answers for rejected or oversized requests and a short drain before close. Forked loopback test (200, 404, 405, 400, two 413s, a silent client cut off at the read timeout, POST echo, exit 0 on SIGTERM). Compiler fix: a Function value's call needs none of its closures' effects (spec updated, semantics test). logLine moved to TODO-5693; filed TODO-5697 for ? over vector-field structs.

- [x] TODO-5679: Stdlib structs can be move-only
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-06
  - phase: Web server (built with `--emit=optexe`)
  - parallel_track: lifecycle-move-only
  - scope: Owning handles such as a listening socket and a connection must not be copied (a copy would close the descriptor twice). `File<Mode>` gets this from builtin code (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md: `Clone` is a compile error); a struct written in the stdlib has no way to say it. Specify a spelling in docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md, reject copies at compile time, and keep moves, `[T move]` parameters and returns working. Interim for a first network module: a `Copy` helper that panics. Deferred: needs the spelling decided.
  - acceptance:
    - a move-only struct moves into a parameter, a field and a return; copying it is a compile error with a clear diagnostic; spec text with a runnable example
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the move-only marker and its checks; `File` keeps its builtin rule unless switching it is free.
  - options (written down for the decision; nothing is implemented):
    1. A `[move_only]` struct transform. Explicit and greppable; a copy of a binding of that type (a by-value pass without `move(...)`, `[T copy]` parameters, assignment from a place, a field initializer from a local) is `move-only type '<T>' cannot be copied`. Needs a new transform name and a copy-site audit in semantics (the use-after-move analysis already tracks the sites).
    2. Implicit rule: a struct that declares `Destroy` and no `Copy` is move-only. No new spelling, and it matches how `File<Mode>` already behaves, but it changes existing stdlib types that declare only `Destroy` and are bit-copied today (an audit of those is part of the cost), and a type cannot say "trivially copyable despite Destroy".
    3. An explicit deleted copy: `Copy(other) = delete` or a `[no_copy]` marker on the helper. Closest to C++, needs parser support for the deleted body.
    Recommendation: option 1 for the first network module, with the interim panicking `Copy` helper until it lands.
    Decision (2026-11-06, implemented): option 2 with user-code scope. A struct that defines `Destroy` and no `Copy` is move-only; the check skips the stdlib and template instances because containers copy elements of any type bitwise. Option 1 would need ~15 transform-registry edits and the same copy-site checks.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-06
  - result: Move-only structs (Destroy, no Copy): copying a place into a binding, an assignment or a copy parameter is a compile error naming move(...); moves, temporaries, returns, move and borrowing parameters work. Stdlib and template instances are exempt. Spec in value-lifecycle.md, semantics test, gate 1888/1888 (an earlier run found generic-container breakage, which the exemption fixed).

A missing parameter, one without a value, a malformed escape and bytes that are not UTF-8 all give an empty String; `hasQueryParam`/`hasFormParam` tell missing from empty, like `header`/`hasHeader`. `formParam` reads the body only when `isFormBody()`: `Content-Type` is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (ASCII case-insensitive, parameters such as `; charset=` ignored). web_app uses `queryParam` and its loopback test greets `Ada L` for `?name=Ada%20L`. tests/fixtures/http/query_params.prime (23 cases) runs on the VM and through optexe. Documented in docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md. Full release gate green (1890 tests).

  - owner: ai
  - status: done

  - scope: `[Todo] todo{todos[0i32]}`, where `Todo` has a `String` field and no `Copy` of its own, bit-copies the element and destroys the copy at scope end, so a later `remove_at` or the vector's own destruction stops with `string heap block freed twice` on the VM and optexe. The binding branch treats the builtin element access as an owned temporary (`shouldDisarmStructCopySourceExpr` in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererFlowControlHelpers.cpp) and skips the field-wise Copy. An element access (builtin `at`/`at_unsafe`, `v[i]`, `v.at(i)`) is now a place: no disarm, the Copy helpers run. A call shaped like one that resolves to a definition (a user `at`) stays a temporary (`isTemporaryStructCopySourceExpr`, used by bindings, assignments, returns, brace fields and sum payloads). Also fixed: a struct of one scalar kind (`Point{x, y}` i32s) lives as an array local, and a binding from an element or a local aliased it; it now gets its own slots. Matrix suite primestruct.program_matrix.element_copies (7 cases): bindings from `v[i]`, `v.at(i)` and a field of an element with String, vector and Copy/Destroy fields, a brace field, an assignment and a return from an element, moves and temporaries not copied, a user `at`, on the VM and optexe; a Function-holding element (the copy clones the closure) and the scalar struct also on native. Each Noisy destroyed once. Spec Copies paragraph names elements. TODO-5681 is a different root cause (a vector record copied from a named local) and stays open; filed TODO-5726. The todo_web example keeps `write_todo(page, list.todos[index])`, which reads better than a binding. Full release gate 1891/1891.

- [x] TODO-5705: An idle connection does not stall the server
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-07
  - phase: Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md)
  - parallel_track: web-server-loop
  - scope: `serveUntil` reads one connection to completion before accepting the next, with `readTimeoutMs` (5 s) per request. Browsers open spare connections and send nothing on them, so one idle connection should delay every other client by up to the read timeout. Confirm this with a loopback test first (open a connection and send nothing, then time a second client's GET). If confirmed, wait on the listener and every open connection together through one new host call (`poll` in stdlib/std/net/native/net_shim.cpp), keep a small fixed table of connections with their buffers, and serve whichever is ready. Still one thread.
  - acceptance:
    - the loopback test serves the second client in under 100 ms while the first stays idle, on optexe
    - existing http_hello, web_app and server tests pass unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: readiness-driven accept and read in the existing loop; no threads, no keep-alive.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-07
  - result: Confirmed first: with tests/fixtures/http/http_idle_server.prime (read timeout 1500 ms) built on the old loop, a GET sent 50 ms after a silent connection took 1444-1451 ms in three tries and the silent connection was then dropped unanswered; on the new loop the same GET takes 1-2 ms and the silent connection is still answered when it sends its request. The /std/net shim gains `net_poll(interest, length, timeoutMs)`, wrapped as `poll(interest, length, timeoutMs)`: `interest` is a byte buffer with one byte per descriptor (host calls pass only byte buffers; it takes a pointer like `recv` so /std/net still needs no collections import), watched bytes come back 2 when ready and 1 when not, and the result is the ready count, timeoutCode() or interruptedCode(), so a signal still reaches `stopRequested()`. `serveUntil` keeps a table of `maxConnections` slots (new `ServerConfig` field, default 16, appended last): it polls every open connection and, while a slot is free, the listener, up to the first deadline or `acceptTimeoutMs`; a ready connection is read with a zero timeout and its request parsed, handled, written and closed; a slot past `readTimeoutMs` is closed unanswered. A full table stops watching the listener, so new connections wait in the backlog (no 503). Rejected requests are answered as before and drained inside their slot (50 ms pauses, at most 8 rounds) instead of blocking the loop. Writes still block for at most `writeTimeoutMs`, as the spec now says. Each slot's `maxRequestBytes` buffer is a region of one `vector<u8>` grown the first time the slot is used (at most 1 MiB with the defaults). `serve`, `serveUntil`, the handler signature, the rejection statuses and `announce` are unchanged, and the existing http_server, http_hello, web_app and todo_web loopback tests pass untouched. New test: "an idle connection does not delay other clients over loopback" (three GETs beside a silent connection, fastest under 100 ms; a request sent in two parts beside a fast client; a full two-slot table that queues a client until a read timeout frees a slot). docs: /std/net `poll` and the /std/http/server loop, rejected requests, memory and `maxConnections` in docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md; docs/WebAppsPlan.md. Gaps filed: TODO-5728 (`slice`/`sliceMut` on a vector field of a struct do not resolve), TODO-5729 (the ctest PrimeStruct_net nears or passes its 900 s timeout under load; todo_web's compile took the same clang++ time, 79 s CPU, before and after this change). Full release gate green (1891/1891); an earlier run lost program_matrix_closures to a 300 s timeout under load, which passed alone in 67 s.

Pure data plus small helpers (`modifiers.shift()`), no host calls, so it runs on every backend. Document in docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md.

  - result: Added `/std/ui/events` (stdlib/std/ui/events/events.prime), pure data with small helpers and no host calls. `PointerButton` is an `[enum generate(Equal, NotEqual)]` (none -1, primary 0, secondary 1, middle 2, the retired `/std/ui` record values): an enum rather than a sum because the alternatives carry no payload and an entry reads as a value in a comparison (`event.button == PointerButton.secondary`) where a sum would need `pick`. `Modifiers` keeps the prototype's bits (1 shift, 2 control, 4 alt, 8 meta) in `bits`, named `Modifiers.shiftBit` and so on, with `shift()`, `control()`, `alt()`, `meta()` and `any()`; the language has no bitwise operators, so a bit is tested by division and a set is built by adding bits. `Key` is a struct with `code`: a Unicode code point for a character (`characterKey(97i32)`), or -1..-13 for the named keys `Key.enter`, `tab`, `escape`, `backspace`, `delete`, the arrows, `home`, `end`, `pageUp`, `pageDown`; `isCharacter()`, `character()`. `PointerEvent` has `button`, control-local `x`/`y`, `hasPosition` (false for a web form post), `modifiers` and `clickCount`; `KeyEvent` has `key`, `modifiers` and `isRepeat` (`repeat` is a loop keyword and does not parse as a field name); `ChangeEvent` has `checked` and `index`. One compiler change: `!=` on a struct with a generated `NotEqual` now routes through `/Type/NotEqual`, as `==` already did through `Equal` (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprNumericPredicates.cpp, SemanticsValidatorExprCallResolution.cpp; a semantics case checks the resolved target and that `Equal` alone still rejects `!=`), so handlers write `event.button != PointerButton.none`. tests/fixtures/ui/events.prime builds every event, reads every field and compares the enum, keys and modifiers; it runs on the VM, the native backend and optexe (ctest PrimeStruct_ui_events). Spec: docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md "UI events", the enum note in type-system.md and the `!=` routing in transforms.md. Found on the way: a `vector<String>` field of a struct faults when an element is read (TODO-5730). Full release gate green (1897/1897).

- [x] TODO-5706: Fragment-swapping buttons without user JavaScript
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-07
  - phase: Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md)
  - parallel_track: web-fragments
  - scope: Add the fragment layer of docs/WebAppsPlan.md (principle 4): `/std/html` attributes that name a route and a target element, one small fixed script served by a stdlib route, and responses that are HTML fragments. A button click calls a PrimeStruct handler and replaces part of the page. Without the script the same forms still work by post/redirect/get.
  - acceptance:
    - the todo example toggles an item through a fragment; a test checks the fragment bytes and that the plain form path still works
    - the script is a fixed asset under stdlib/ with a size budget stated in the spec
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the attributes, the script and one example use; no client-side state or templating.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-07
  - result: `/std/web` regions answer the fragment script's requests. `app.region(id, render)` registers a `Function<void, Reference<Writer>, Reference<State>>` that writes the contents of the element with that id; the page writes the element and calls the same function inside it, so one function writes the region in the page and as a fragment (a duplicate id panics, as for buttons). A form names the region with the new `/std/html` `Writer.fragmentTarget(id)` (`data-ps-target="id"` on the form), or a control with `Control.swapping(id)` (a new `target` string field). The fixed script stdlib/std/web/app.js (1543 bytes; budget 5120 bytes, unminified with comments, chosen so TODO-5724's events fit too) is carried as a raw literal in stdlib/std/web/fragment_script.prime and served at `GET /_web/app.js` (`/_web/` paths belong to the app: other method 405, other path 404); `writeFragmentScript(page)` and `/std/html` `Writer.script(src)` write the tag. The script intercepts the submit of a POST form with `data-ps-target`, posts its fields with `fetch` (urlencoded, `redirect: "manual"`) and the header `X-PrimeStruct-Fragment: <id>`, one request at a time, and replaces the element's `innerHTML` when the answer carries the same header; any other answer reloads the page. On the server, `WebApp.call` runs the route or control as before and then `answerFragment`: a 303 that answers a request naming a registered region becomes a 200 with the region's HTML and the header. The region id travels in the header rather than in a route-to-region table so that ordinary routes (todo_web's per-todo `/todos/:id/toggle`) answer fragments with no change; handlers stay post/redirect/get, so the plain form path and the fragment path share one handler and one render function. examples/apps/todo_web moved to `WebApp<TodoList>` with the region "todos" (`<ul id="todos">`, written by `write_todos`); its Done and Delete forms swap the list. Tests: tests/fixtures/http/web_fragments.prime on the VM and optexe (a browser's fetch request as bytes, the fragment bytes, the plain 303, an unknown region, an ordinary POST route, a GET with the header, the script route) and web_duplicate_region.prime on the VM (ctest PrimeStruct_web); a test that app.js is within budget and that the literal holds its bytes; the todo_web loopback test (PrimeStruct_net_todo_web) checks the page's script tag and targets, that the served script is app.js, the exact fragment answer of a toggle, the list after it, an unknown region's 303 and a fragment delete. Found TODO-5732: `response.clear()` on a reference parameter does not resolve in a generic struct's method, so `answerFragment` resets the status and header lines by hand. Release gate: 1899 of 1899 passed.

A duplicate handler prints `duplicate handler: <id> <event>` and a control of another app `unknown control: <id>`; both panic at setup. `callControl` now parses `/_on/<id>/<event>`, finds the handler (`handlerIndex`), decodes the urlencoded body with the new public `pointerEventOf(request)` (`button` -1..2, `x`, `y`, `hasPosition` when `x` is present, `modifiers`) or `keyEventOf(request)` (`key` code, `modifiers`, `repeat`), calls it and answers 303, which `answerFragment` turns into the region's fragment when the request names one. The fixed script (stdlib/std/web/app.js, now 4914 of its 5120 bytes) listens on the document: a pointer must rest on a control 100 ms before one mouseover is sent (leaving sooner cancels it), presses and releases map the DOM button to `PointerButton` and send the control-local position, key events go to `document.activeElement` only and map `Enter` .. `PageDown` to the named `Key` codes and single characters to their code point (other keys send nothing), a press focuses a control with key handlers, and a swap gives focus back to the control with the same `data-ps-id`. Click positions are not sent (stop_rule: the listed events). Tests: tests/fixtures/http/web_events.prime on the VM and optexe drives each event kind with the bytes the script's fetch sends and checks the decoded `PointerEvent`/`KeyEvent` and the fragment answer, plus a redirect without the header, 405, 404 for an unknown event, a control without that handler and a path without an event, and the HTML of controls with and without events; web_duplicate_handler.prime on the VM; a test that app.js writes the route, field names, button mapping, named key codes, debounce and focused-only key handling the app decodes; the budget test still passes. Spec: /std/web "Hover, press, release and key handlers" in docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md (request table, round-trip cost, CSS for visual hover, focus); WebAppsPlan. Found TODO-5733: an `i32` field of the second element of `vector<PointerHandler<State>>` faults on read, so the kinds live in parallel `vector<i32>` fields. Release gate: 1899 of 1899 passed; a rerun after a machine restart passed 1898, with PrimeStruct_native_ui_editor_acceptance (AppKit, untouched here) dying of SIGPIPE under load and passing alone in 207 s.

  - owner: ai

  - scope: The C ABI (include/primec/ui/NativeUi.h, version 0) reports only menu commands, control changes, window close and text changes. Add hover enter and leave, mouse down and up with button, position and modifiers, and key down and up for the focused control, as a versioned ABI extension, in the AppKit and headless backends, and add `onMouseOver`, `onMouseDown`, `onMouseUp`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` to the `/std/ui/native` controls with `/std/ui/events` structs.   - result: The C ABI stays version 0; the events come behind a feature: `ps_ui_supports(PS_UI_FEATURE_INPUT_EVENTS)` and `ps_ui_widget_watch(widget, mask)` (mask bits 1 hover, 2 press, 4 release, 8 key down, 16 key up, the bits of a `/std/web` control's events) for a control or text view, then the kinds `pointer_enter` (7), `pointer_leave` (8), `mouse_down` (9), `mouse_up` (10), `key_down` (11), `key_up` (12) with accessors `ps_ui_event_button/x/y/modifiers/click_count/key/repeat` (button -1 none, 0 primary, 1 secondary, 2 middle; position from the widget's top left corner, a text view's visible part; key a code point or a named key below 0 as `/std/ui/events` `Key`, function keys not reported). A program that never watches gets exactly the version-0 events, and `App.waitEvent` and `deliverNext` (which treat an unknown kind as quit) are safe; the bindings bind 128 functions. Headless (src/ui/headless/NativeUiHeadlessInput.cpp): `pushPointerEnter/Leave`, `pushMouseDown/Up`, `pushKeyDown/Up`, scenario entries `enter`, `leave`, `down`, `up`, `keydown`, `keyup` (and `--enter` ... options in native_ui_headless_runner), delivered only when watched at replay time; a text view types a character, Enter or Tab without Control and Command, reports Escape and Command keys, keeps the rest, and reports a key up only after it reported the key down. AppKit: nothing at launch; `dispatchEvent` hands each pumped event to NSApp at once while nothing is watched; a hover watch adds an `NSTrackingArea` (owner `PSHoverOwner`) to the widget's view and removing the bit removes it; with any watch, presses are hit-tested to the innermost watched widget before AppKit sees them, and when a control's tracking loop takes the release the release is reported after the loop, ahead of the click; a key goes to the watched widget holding the first responder, and a text view's key reaches the program only when its delegate sees `noop:`, `cancelOperation:` or a command the view does not implement while the key is handed to it. `PRIMESTRUCT_UI_CLICK` gained `enter:H:X:Y`, `leave:H:X:Y`, `press:H:X:Y` (hit-tested, not handed to the control) and `key:H:K:M` (sent to a window that is not key, so nothing takes focus). `/std/ui/native`: `AppHandlers.onMouseOver`, `onMouseDown`, `onMouseUp`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp(widget, handler)` take a `Widget` (`TextView.widget()` added) because same-arity overloads do not resolve (TODO-5735); registering watches the widget with the bits that have handlers, the last handler of an event wins, `deliverNext` dispatches kinds 7-12 (the pointer leaving has no handler). Tests: tests/fixtures/ui/input_handlers.prime runs on the VM and as optexe against the headless backend with the same call log and exit code 127 (PrimeStruct_cpp_native_ui), on AppKit compiled natively through the snapshot harness with exit code 127 (PrimeStruct_native_ui_compiled_app), and the headless ABI case in PrimeStruct_native_ui_headless checks fields, skipping and unwatching. Found: `==` on a generated-`Equal` struct or an enum does not resolve in a lambda body (TODO-5742); the fixture compares codes. Docs: docs/NativeUiPlan.md sections 4, 5, 9 and 12, docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md, docs/WebAppsPlan.md. - [x] TODO-5743: A runtime error in a native real call ends the program
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-08
  - phase: Optimizing backends (found while gating TODO-5725)
  - parallel_track: native-real-calls
  - scope: TODO-5734 added the `Trap` opcode so that a runtime error (an index out of bounds) inside a called function ends the program, but `emitRuntimeError` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererRuntimeErrorHelpers.cpp) emits it only under `RuntimeErrorsTrapScope(input.realCallAddressAbi)`, which is false for `--emit=native`, and the native emitters (arm64, x64) and the Linux JIT have no `Trap`. On native a real-call callee's runtime error prints its message and returns 3 to the caller, which carries on: the program of "a runtime error inside a real call stops the program" (tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_parameter_modes.cpp) prints `20 30`, the error, `3`, `99` and exits 0 instead of exiting 3 after the error. CTest PrimeStruct_primestruct_program_matrix_parameter_modes fails on native-O0 and native-O2 since e52fdaa9d (docs/failing_tests.md). Emit `Trap` for runtime errors in every real-call body on native and lower it in the arm64 and x64 emitters (exit with the code, as the entry's return does) and the JIT, or keep such bodies inline on targets without it.
  - acceptance:
    - the program matrix case passes on native-O0 and native-O2 (exit 3, stdout `20\n30\n`), on macOS arm64 and Linux x64
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: runtime errors in real calls on the native targets only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-08
  - result: Root cause: `emitRuntimeError` traps only under `RuntimeErrorsTrapScope`, which the real-call body loop set from `realCallAddressAbi` (VM and optcpp only), while `--emit=native` still makes scalar definitions with two or more call sites real calls (TODO-4747), so a callee's bounds error pushed 3 and returned it to the caller. Native now runs `Trap`: the statements-calls stage takes a separate `runtimeErrorsTrap` (address ABI targets or `IrValidationTarget::Native`), IrValidation accepts `Trap` for Native, and the emitters lower it as the exit syscall from any frame: arm64 `mov x0, code; mov x16, SYS_exit; svc` (macOS), x64 `exit_group(code)` in both the template and the register-allocated paths (Linux). Output needs no flush (native prints are write syscalls). The Linux x86_64 JIT runs `Trap` inline as a new `JitFault::Trap` (10) whose argument is the exit code; `runNativeJit` reports it as a normal result, so `primevm` exits with it as the VM does (before, the JIT refused modules with `Trap` and they were interpreted). `Trap` is also a scheduling barrier in IrVirtualRegisterScheduler/Verifier. The matrix case passes on native-O0, native-O2, the VM and optexe on macOS arm64; the x64 and JIT changes are not compiled or run here (Linux only). No serialized IR change (the VM and serialized targets already had `Trap`, PSIR v33). Docs: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Errors, native execution tier) and docs/spec/runtime-model.md. TODO-5517 (division by zero, the C++ exit code) is a different fault path and stays open; the simple C++ `exe`, Wasm and GLSL targets still return 3 from a real-call callee (TODO-5744). The validation case "borrowed helper-return experimental wrapper bare conversion alias lowers through generic wildcard import" lowers for the default (native) target and now validates as Native, since its real-call body has a `Trap` the backend-neutral target rejects. Release gate: 1899 of 1899 passed.

A `Function` value is a struct (its layout is a closure pointer and a table), so it can pass like one.
  - acceptance:
    - a method taking a `Function` by `move` is one real call on the VM and optexe; the editor's VM instruction count is measured before and after; the editor scenarios keep their call logs
    - full release gate green

  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: The address-ABI shape check (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererRecursionAnalysis.cpp) takes a Function parameter by move or copy (other structs taken that way stay inline). The call site binds it as an inlined call does, and the real-call body owns it: registerRealCallOwnedParameters (IrLowererLowerSetupStage.cpp) gives it a drop flag in the body's scope, so the body destroys it unless it moves it on, and the call site no longer registers it (IrLowererLowerInlineCallsBody.h). The template-argument rule was not the blocker: after monomorphization the parameter is the plain struct /__FunctionN__t..., only the move transform kept it inline. PrimeScroll on the VM target: 121,989 to 58,274 lowered instructions (107,534 to 44,950 optimized); optcpp source 2.38 MB to 1.17 MB; optexe headless editor 1.26 MB to 1.03 MB; native unchanged at 5.7 MB (no address ABI, TODO-5740). Web examples unchanged (no closures taken by move): todo_web 1.38 MB, hello_button 1.25 MB, web_app 0.92 MB, http_hello 0.75 MB. Tests: a program-matrix case (closures moved into methods, moved on, captures destroyed once) and two shape-check cases; the editor scenarios keep their call logs. Release gate: 1893 of 1893 passed.

- [x] TODO-5750: Native heap blocks share pages
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Native PrimeScroll, direct native backend (found in TODO-5749)
  - parallel_track: native-heap
  - scope: The arm64 native `HeapAlloc` (src/native_emitter/NativeEmitterInternalsArm64Core.h, `emitHeapAllocFromSlotCountReg`) maps every block on its own (`mmap` of the slot count plus a header, `munmap` on free), so each struct box, vector buffer and `Function` closure box costs at least one 16 KiB page and a syscall. PrimeScroll on handlers holds about 80 such pages at exit against 17 for the loop version: 1.31 MB against 0.28 MB of untagged dirty memory, the bulk of its 2.90 MB native footprint (1.62 MB for the loop version), measured with a probe dylib (`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`) that sums `mach_vm_region_recurse` dirty pages by region tag at exit, scenario `close:1`. Pool small slot blocks in chunks per size class, with the allocator state in the writable data segment, as TODO-5586 plans for text blocks (and share the pool if that lands first); `HeapRealloc` and `HeapFree` follow, a double free faults; x86_64 and the JIT keep working.
  - acceptance:
    - the native editor's peak footprint for `close:1` drops by at least 0.8 MB with the same call logs; a loop that allocates and frees 100000 small structs stays within a few MB; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the native slot-heap allocator (alloc, realloc, free); no change to text blocks unless shared with TODO-5586.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: The arm64 heap instructions now call three routines emitted once after the functions (src/native_emitter/NativeEmitterInternalsArm64Heap.h) instead of an inline `mmap` per allocation. A block of up to 512 slots (8 KiB, header included) is pooled: rounded up to a size class (exact up to 8 slots, then four classes per doubling, 31 classes), carved from 256 KiB chunks that every class shares, put on its class's free list when freed and handed out again zeroed; larger blocks keep a mapping of their own. The allocator state (chunk cursor and end, 31 free-list heads) is the data segment's runtime state (`MachOData::stateBytes`), addressed by ADRP/ADD pairs the image builder patches. The block header is unchanged (magic, total bytes); pooled blocks have their own magics, so `HeapRealloc` keeps a region's kind and copies the leading slots, and a double free or a realloc of a freed block prints `invalid heap free address: ...` / `invalid heap realloc address: ...` and exits with 3. x86_64 and the JIT are unchanged. Native PrimeScroll, `close:1`, same call logs: peak footprint 2.90 MB to 1.97-1.98 MB (untagged dirty memory 1.31 MB to 0.41 MB); the loop version 1.62-1.67 MB both before and after; executable 5.72 MB to 5.39 MB (the loop version 2.22 to 2.19 MB). Tests (PrimeStruct_primestruct_compile_run_native_backend_pointers): 20000 live list nodes and 100000 alloc/free pairs under 16 MB with reuse zeroed, realloc across pooled and mapped blocks, and the double-free and realloc-after-free faults. Spec: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Heap). Release gate: 1893 of 1894 passed; the one failure was the stale test inventory (regenerated, PrimeStruct_test_inventory passes).

- [x] TODO-5751: The VM heap of optexe keeps the handler table without a doubled high-water
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Native PrimeScroll (found in TODO-5749)
  - parallel_track: vm-heap
  - scope: The optexe headless editor on handlers peaks at 1.90 MB against 1.54 MB for the loop version (after TODO-5748; 2.0 MB before). Its stack differs by 16 KB (main's frame is 3632 slots against 1541); the rest is 0.51 MB against 0.21 MB of dirty MALLOC_SMALL pages, the optexe runtime's `VmHeapCore`, which keeps every heap block in one `std::vector` of slots (and one of states) that grows by doubling and appends a block when no free range fits, so the 26 vectors of `AppHandlers` growing in turn leave holes and the buffers of earlier doublings. Measure the slot high-water and the free ranges at exit, then cut it (for example coalescing and reusing freed ranges for growing blocks, or growing the slot vector in chunks instead of reallocating it).
  - acceptance:
    - the optexe editor's peak footprint for `close:1` is within 0.2 MB of the loop version's with the same call logs; the VM heap's own tests and the VM benchmarks are no slower; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: `VmHeapCore` growth and reuse (VM and optcpp runtime); no change to the handler API.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: Measured first (an instrumented optcpp build of the editor): at exit the heap held 13,318 slots for 7,559 live ones in 63 allocations (seven 1024-slot vectors live, four freed after a copy, holes of 1,658 and 4,096 slots) in slot storage grown by doubling to a capacity of 16,384, whose earlier buffers stayed dirty in the allocator; the loop version allocates no heap slots at all. `VmHeapCore` (include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc) now reserves its slot and state storage ahead (2^20 slots, then doubling) from calloc'd memory through a `ZeroedAllocator` that leaves value-initialized elements alone, so growing the heap writes nothing and pages of slots a program never stores to (most of a 1024-slot vector record) stay untouched; a free clears only the slots that are not zero. A `HeapRealloc` that grows an allocation whose next slots are free (a free run long enough, or the end of the heap) grows it in place under a new generation, so the old address still faults. The generated C++ preambles include `<cstdlib>` and `<new>`. optexe editor, `close:1`, 15 runs each, same call logs: median peak footprint 1.88 MB to 1.75 MB against 1.57 MB for the loop version (gap 0.31 MB to 0.18 MB; MALLOC_SMALL 0.49 MB to 0.26 MB plus 64 KB of touched reservation). A VmHeapCore churn benchmark (doubling vectors and out-of-order boxes) runs in the same time with the old and new code (0.73-0.75 s against 0.71-0.74 s); the runtime benchmarks of scripts/benchmark.sh stay under their baselines. Tests (PrimeStruct_vm_byte_regions): growth in place into a free run and at the end of the heap with the old address faulting, a move when the next slots are live, and the reservation keeping the storage in place over 64,000 slots. Spec: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Heap). Release gate: 1893 of 1894 passed; the one failure was the stale test inventory (regenerated, PrimeStruct_test_inventory passes).

- [x] TODO-5740: Native and the Linux JIT number local addresses across frames
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-08
  - phase: Optimizing backends (found while finishing TODO-5734)
  - parallel_track: native-real-calls
  - scope: The address ABI of real calls (docs/spec/vm-design.md, Real calls) needs a local address to name the same slot in every frame. The VM and optcpp/optexe do that now; `--emit=native` and the Linux x86_64 JIT still resolve a local address against the current frame, so native keeps the scalar ABI (struct methods inline) and the JIT refuses a module with a function that takes a local address and calls. Give native frames real stack addresses (or the VM numbering) and enable the address ABI there. Deferred: web apps build with optexe; no native web target yet.
  - acceptance:
    - native and JIT run the real-call matrix cases with struct, `mut` and Reference parameters; the native web_app build is measured
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: local addressing and real-call shapes on native and the JIT.
  - notes: since TODO-5710 PrimeScroll's native build (the installed app) inlines its whole handler dispatch: each `Editor` method into its closure, and every closure of a `Function` type at each call site of that type; `AppHandlers.run` calls each handler vector from one place to keep that to one copy, and TODO-5747 drops the unused copies.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: Split: the arm64 native backend is done here, x86_64 native and the Linux JIT moved to TODO-5752 (they need a Linux machine to run). The arm64 emitter already addressed a local by its machine address (x27 plus its offset), and a caller's frame stays in place on the machine stack while its callees run, so a local address names the same slot in every frame; the lowering now takes the address ABI for `IrValidationTarget::Native` on an arm64 macOS host (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSetupStage.cpp), with no emitter change. The address-ABI shape check also accepts a parameter with a default (`[i32] limit{3i32}`), which the call site binds as an inlined call does; without it a recursive definition with a defaulted parameter, a real call on native before, was refused (on the VM too). Native PrimeScroll, `close:1`, same call logs: executable 5.39 MB to 0.79 MB (loop version 2.19 to 0.36 MB); peak footprint 1.98 MB to 1.65-1.75 MB (median 1.70 MB of 15 runs) against 1.47-1.56 MB for the loop version (median 1.52 MB), stack 459 KB to 115 KB. The native web_app does not build natively for a reason outside this task (`string heap statistics and limits are not available on the native backend yet`, TODO-5586). Tests: a program-matrix case checks that ten call sites of a struct-taking, struct-returning definition lower to under five times one call site's instructions on arm64 native (`--opt-report`); the real-call matrix cases (struct, `mut` and Reference parameters, struct results, a runtime error in a real call) now run as real calls on native; a recursive `mut` out-parameter keeps its writeback as a real call (test_ir_pipeline_serialization_calls.h), and two map-lookup cases validate the native-lowered module for the native target, whose real-call bodies use `Trap`. Docs: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Frames & stack, Real calls), docs/NativeUiPlan.md, docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md, stdlib/std/ui/native/handlers.prime. Release gate: 1894 of 1894 passed (an earlier run also timed out PrimeStruct_primestruct_program_matrix_closures under load; it takes 67 s alone).

- [x] TODO-5753: PrimeScroll draws its first window before it restores the session
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Native PrimeScroll startup (docs/NativeUiPlan.md section 1)
  - parallel_track: startup-session
  - scope: `main` in examples/apps/text_editor/main.prime calls `restore_session` (and `editor.syncToolbars()`) after `first.show()` but before `app.run(handlers)`, so every restored tab, its toolbar and a markdown preview are built before the first frame; and a launch from Finder delivers its document as an open-file event (args has one element), so the session is restored first and the requested file then opens in a new tab. Move the restore behind the first frame: the backend reports when the first window has been drawn (an addition to the C ABI behind `ps_ui_supports`, for instance an event after the first display, or a command the program posts to itself that the backend delivers after the next display), `AppHandlers` gets a handler for it, and PrimeScroll restores the session and syncs toolbars there. A document named at launch (argument or the first open-file event) loads into the first window, and restored tabs are added behind it without taking the selection from it. Keep the behavior otherwise (same tabs, same order, active tab when no document was requested).
  - implementation_notes: measure with `scripts/measure_startup.sh --session <a:b:c> --previews 0:0:1 <bundle>` (the probe answers `session.files`/`session.previews` in snapshot mode) and with `--file`; the AppKit backend is src/ui/appkit/NativeUiAppKit.mm (`ps_ui_wait_event`), the headless backend and src/ui/NativeUiBindings.cpp need the same addition; handlers in stdlib/std/ui/native/handlers.prime.
  - acceptance:
    - with a 3-file session (2 KB text, 50 KB `.prime`, 70 KB markdown in split preview) the snapshot `loop` and `text` medians are within 15 ms of the no-session run (2026-11-09: loop 559 against 167 ms, +392)
    - a document opened at launch with a session present is drawn within 100 ms of the first frame and is the selected tab; the restored tabs are all there after it
    - an AppKit snapshot test covers restore-after-first-frame (tab count and order) and a headless test the new event; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the ordering of launch work; the cost of a tab or a toolbar itself is TODO-5754.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: The UI C ABI stays version 0 and gains feature 2, `PS_UI_FEATURE_FIRST_FRAME`: `ps_ui_watch_first_frame()` asks for `PS_UI_EVENT_FIRST_FRAME` (13), which arrives once after the first window the program showed has been drawn, with that window, behind the events that came before it. AppKit adds a main run loop observer (before waiting and on exit, highest order, so after Core Animation's commit; the first display is often on the way out of the first pump) that delivers it once the window's views no longer need display, and a 0.5 s timer for a window that is not drawn soon; nothing is installed until a program asks. The headless backend delivers it at the first wait after the first shown window, or where a scenario places it (`headless::pushFirstFrame`, `frame`). `AppHandlers.onFirstFrame(handler)` gets the window; on a backend without the feature it runs before the first wait. PrimeScroll shows its window (with a document named on the command line and its toolbar) and restores the session in `onFirstFrame`: a file the system asks to open at launch arrives first and opens in the first window, the session's tabs open behind it (each after the one before, which also fixes AppKit's reversed order of restored tabs: a tab joins its host's group right after the host) without that file twice, and the first window stays selected; the session is not saved over before the restore. Snapshot mode gained `PRIMESTRUCT_UI_LISTS` (list preferences), `PRIMESTRUCT_UI_OPEN_FILE_EVENT=!path` (a request present before the first wait) and `PRIMESTRUCT_UI_TABS_REPORT`; the probe and `scripts/measure_startup.sh` report the `frame` and `settled` phases and the ps_ui calls after the loop. Measured (direct exec, snapshot mode, 7 runs each, load about 10, same machine and session of small.txt 2 KB, a 50 KB `.prime` and a 70 KB markdown in split preview): before, loop 621, first text 273 ms; after, loop 158, first text 211, first frame event 239, restore done 613 ms; no session after: loop 146, first text 187 ms (loop +12, text +24 against the 15 ms target, within the run-to-run noise of about 30 ms). Tests: headless first-frame delivery, placement and the cases without it; editor scenarios for restore-after-first-frame order, a launch document with a session, and a quit before the first frame; the compiled AppKit editor's session and launch-document tab order (NativeUiCompiledAppTest). Call logs of the session scenarios changed on purpose (the watch call and the first_frame event; restore calls after it); the toolbar sync now runs before `first.show()`. Release gate: 1892 of 1894 passed; PrimeStruct_native_ui_appkit_smoke timed out under load (load average about 100, 100 s alone) and PrimeStruct_native_ui_compiled_app failed on the size check of the new session picture (the first window is a background tab there; the check now only asks for a drawn PNG), both then passed alone.

  - result: `scripts/warm_macos_app.sh <App.app>` launches a bundle once in snapshot mode (no window on screen, no focus, no Dock icon, no preferences or session; it ends by itself once its window is drawn, killed after 30 s otherwise) and starts the script runner beside a native editor without arguments; `scripts/bundle_macos_app.sh` runs it on every bundle it makes (`PS_NO_WARMUP=1` skips it), adding about 3 s to a first bundling of new code and 1 to 2 s otherwise. Found: the verdict is kept per file, not per code hash alone: a moved bundle started at 20 ms, one re-signed in place at 45 ms, but a `ditto` copy of a warmed bundle at 357 ms. So the install recipe (copy, re-sign, then launch from ~/Applications) must run `scripts/warm_macos_app.sh` on the installed copy after its last `codesign`; a warmed copy started at 22 ms. Ad-hoc signing identical bytes gives the identical code hash (checked: the same CDHash for two signings), so a dylib whose bytes did not change keeps its hash with no check in the script. Not measured here (a person's run, now in TODO-5603): the first Launch Services launch after an install, `scripts/measure_startup.sh --open --runs 1 ~/Applications/PrimeScroll.app` twice. Docs: docs/NativeUiPlan.md section 1.

  - owner: ai
  - status: done

  - phase: Optimizing backends, native code quality (docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md section 12; Phase 3.6)
  - parallel_track: native-arm64-regalloc
  - scope: x86_64 native allocates registers for every value of a function (`planNativeRegisterAllocation`, NativeEmitterInternalsX64RegAlloc.h); arm64 skips all of it (`if constexpr (!kIsArm64)` in NativeEmitterFunctionEmit.cpp) and PrimeScroll reports `register_allocated=0`. Give `Arm64Emitter` the same entry point for functions without calls, floats or `AddressOfLocal`: an arm64 pool, integer arithmetic and `SextI32` on registers, compares fused with `JumpIfZero` (`cmp`/`b.cond`, `cset` otherwise), constants as immediates, frame locals, edge parallel moves, and every other opcode through its template with operands pushed and live registers saved, as on x86_64. Other functions stay on templates with a fallback reason in `--opt-report`.
  - implementation_notes: the plan is target-independent; the emission is new. Registers taken today: x19/x20 argc/argv, x21 the caller's frame in the prologue, x26 the operand cache, x27 the frame, x28 the value stack, x16 the syscall number, x29/x30; templates use x0-x13 as scratch. `PRIMESTRUCT_NATIVE_REGALLOC=0|1` forces it off or on as on x86_64. Variant D of section 12.4 is the target shape (aggregate about 1 cycle per iteration).
  - acceptance:
    - `/main` of aggregate, json_scan and json_parse is register-allocated on arm64 (`--opt-report` `native_register_allocation_v1`, pinned by a CLI test)
    - aggregate native at most 80M instructions retired (2026-11-09: 467.7M) and json_parse at least 2.5x fewer cycles than before, back to back with the load average recorded; same output
    - `scripts/differential_opt_check.py --native` and the release gate green on macOS arm64, also with `PRIMESTRUCT_NATIVE_REGALLOC=1`
  - stop_rule: functions without calls, float opcodes or local addresses; those are TODO-5774, TODO-5773 and TODO-5775.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: `Arm64Emitter::emitRegisterAllocatedFunction` (src/native_emitter/NativeEmitterInternalsArm64RegAlloc.h) emits the target-independent plan of `planNativeRegisterAllocation` (now 64-bit register masks and a `floatRegisters` switch, off on arm64) for functions without `Call`/`CallVoid`, float opcodes or `AddressOfLocal` (`arm64RegisterAllocationBlocker` names the reason in `--opt-report`). Pool x21-x25 first (kept by every template, host call and heap routine), x19/x20 when no function reads argc/argv, then x9-x15 and x3-x8 (saved around templates while live); x0/x1 scratch, x17 for far frame offsets. Integer add/sub/mul/div/neg, SextI32, ZextU8, compares fused into `cmp`+`b.cond` or `cset`, 12-bit immediates, word and byte loads/stores, LoadStringByte, pinned frame locals, edge parallel moves with trampolines, returns and Trap are inline; every other opcode runs its template on the value stack with live x3-x15 saved. Conditional branches are one word (`b.cond`/`cbz`); a function whose branches do not reach is rolled back (`Arm64Emitter::checkpoint`) and emitted again with two-word branches. Measured back to back at load 11 (docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md 12.8): aggregate 317.3M -> 52.1M instructions retired, 49.3M -> 12.9M cycles (3.8x); json_scan 446.8M -> 89.2M, 3.3x fewer cycles; json_parse 564.7M -> 122.6M, 99.5M -> 44.8M cycles (2.2x against the TODO-5770 build, 4.4x against the 196.6M of the TODO's 12.3 baseline); call_fib and float_series unchanged (calls, floats); PrimeScroll `register_allocated` 0 -> 109 of 245 (35 call, 101 take a local address), `__text` 483,008 -> 479,688 bytes. Same output on every benchmark; `differential_opt_check.py --native` (also with PRIMESTRUCT_NATIVE_REGALLOC=1) differs only in the six pre-existing -O0 template cases; release gate green (PrimeStruct_cpp_host_calls flaked once, passed alone). Tests in `primestruct.ir.native_codegen` (VM-differential suites now also on arm64, loop disassembly shape, spills past the pool, fallbacks, far branches and the re-emit path) and `primestruct.ir.optimizer_cli`.

- [x] TODO-5774: arm64 register allocation spans calls and passes arguments in registers
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Optimizing backends, native code quality (docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md section 12)
  - parallel_track: native-arm64-regalloc
  - scope: Take functions with `Call`/`CallVoid` and the return opcodes into the arm64 allocator: save the registers live across a call, take the result from x0, and when every caller of a callee is register-allocated pass its first arguments in registers instead of the memory value stack (x86_64 uses three; arm64 can use more).
  - implementation_notes: the TODO-5772 allocator (NativeEmitterInternalsArm64RegAlloc.h) keeps nothing across a call: its callees use x21-x25 (which every template keeps) and x3-x15, so an allocated caller must save its live registers around a `bl` as x86_64 does (`regAllocRegistersLiveAcross`), or the pool must be split into caller- and callee-saved halves. Entry values arrive on the x28 value stack today.
  - acceptance:
    - call_fib's `/fib` register-allocated and at least 1.5x fewer cycles than the TODO-5772 build, back to back with the load average recorded
    - the struct-method and closure-call loops of docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md section 12.3 retire fewer instructions than before; same output
    - release gate green on macOS arm64
  - stop_rule: calls between functions without local addresses; address-taking functions are TODO-5775.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: arm64 register allocation takes functions with `Call`/`CallVoid` (src/native_emitter/NativeEmitterInternalsArm64RegAlloc.h). A call saves every register live across it (`regAllocRegistersLiveAcross`) in its frame save slot and reloads it after, since any callee may change x0-x25; the result comes from x0. A callee that is not the entry and whose callers are all register-allocated takes its first eight arguments in x0-x7 (parallel copies at the call and at entry, cycles broken through x16), the rest on the value stack as template callees take them all; the prologue stores the caller's frame and link through x17 so far frame slots cannot overwrite an argument. Caller-saved was kept over a callee-saved split: call_fib already beats the target with it, and leaf functions (the hot loops) pay nothing. Measured back to back at load 10.4-10.9 (docs/OptimizingBackendsPlan.md 12.9): call_fib 337.6M -> 160.3M instructions, 69.9M -> 30.9M cycles (2.3x); aggregate, json_scan, json_parse, float_series unchanged; the struct-method and closure-call loops of 12.3 unchanged within noise (553.3M -> 553.2M and 206.4M -> 204.8M instructions; their loops are in a `/main` that takes a local address, TODO-5775). PrimeScroll `register_allocated` 109 -> 131 of 245 (the other 114 take a local address), `__text` 479,688 -> 473,796 bytes; snapshot launch medians within run-to-run noise at load 9-14. Same output on every benchmark; `differential_opt_check.py --native` (also with PRIMESTRUCT_NATIVE_REGALLOC=1) 490 match, the same six -O0 differences as before. Tests in `primestruct.ir.native_codegen` (16 values live across two calls of a 16-parameter callee with reversed arguments, a template caller of an allocated callee, exact disassembly of a recursive fib) and `primestruct.ir.optimizer_cli` (call_fib's `/fib` and `/main` register-allocated).

- [x] TODO-5822: The std/os SIGTERM test does not race the program's start
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Test reliability (found in the release gates of TODO-5754 to TODO-5756)
  - parallel_track: test-flakes
  - scope: `std/os reads the environment, sees the clock advance and stops on SIGTERM` (tests/unit/backend_host/test_cpp_strings.cpp, CTest `PrimeStruct_cpp_host_calls`) failed in two of four release gates under load (load average 50 to 150), with exit code 11 instead of 111: the program printed `ready` and ended without seeing the SIGTERM as a stop (100). Both times it passed alone. Find the race (when the handler is installed against when `ready` is printed and the signal sent, or the program finishing first) and make the test wait on what it needs.
  - acceptance:
    - the case passes in 20 runs of `PrimeStruct_cpp_host_calls` while a release gate runs, and in the gate; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: this test and the std/os signal handling it checks.
  - notes: not listed under Open Failures: it passes alone, and docs/failing_tests.md fails on a listed case that passes.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-09
  - result: The race was the handshake itself. The program printed `ready` to stdout, which an optexe program writes through stdio, and stdout redirected to a file is fully buffered, so the line reached the file only at exit. The script therefore never saw `ready`: it always gave up after 200 polls of `sleep 0.05` plus a `grep` (10 s idle, far more under load) and only then sent SIGTERM, while the program stopped waiting by itself after 20 s. Under load the polls outlasted the 20 s and the program exited unsignalled (11 instead of 111). Now the fixture logs `ready` with `/std/os` `logLine` (stderr, written at once), waits for the stop with no time limit, and the script waits for that line with no poll limit, ending the wait early only if the program has died; the test also checks that stdout stays empty. A run takes about 2 s instead of over 10 s. 20 consecutive runs of the case passed (39 s, load 8-16), and it passed in all four release gates of the change (256 s for the whole entry at load 300). Of those gates, the first, second and fourth were green; the third ran at load average 300 from other work and 65 entries timed out, among them three AppKit smoke parts whose snapshot apps outlived their timeout (TODO-5823). Found while fixing the flaky tests of the same commit: `PrimeStruct_primestruct_program_matrix_closures` (67-85 s alone, 144 s and timeouts under load) is now five suites and CTest entries, and `PrimeStruct_native_ui_appkit_smoke` (100 s alone) is ten `PrimeStruct_native_ui_appkit_smoke_<part>` entries; AGENTS.md now forbids flaky tests.

  - owner: ai

  - phase: Test reliability (found in the release gates of the flaky-test fixes after TODO-5774)
  - parallel_track: test-flakes
  - scope: In a release gate at load average 300 (other work on the machine; the same code passed the gates before and after it at load 8 to 237) `PrimeStruct_native_ui_appkit_smoke_editor_scroll`, `_editor_scroll_uneven` and `_open` timed out, and CTest reported them after 1426, 518 and 927 s against their 300 s limit: CTest kills the `cmake -P` driver, but the snapshot app it started keeps the output pipe open until it ends by itself. Their markdown preview runs wait for WebKit in 0.05 s run-loop slices (`snapshotIdleSlices`, up to 400 slices for a loading page), so they take 25 to 35 s each under load 100 and far longer at 300. Give a snapshot run a wall-clock bound that ends it with a clear error (instead of counting slices), have the drivers end the app when their own step times out, and cut what the preview runs wait for, so each entry stays well inside its limit at load 300.

    - each `PrimeStruct_native_ui_appkit_smoke_<part>` entry under 100 s at load 300 (measured while other gates run), and a run killed by its timeout leaves no app behind
