- [x] TODO-5867: A string heap that alternates between block sizes keeps its chunks
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Multithreading and Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md, Concurrency; found measuring `serveWorkers`)
  - parallel_track: text-heap
  - scope: The string heap (`VmTextHeap`, include/primec/runtime/VmTextHeapBody.inc) keeps one chunk whose blocks are all free and returns any other at once. A thread that holds no other strings and builds one that grows through two block sizes (32 then 64 bytes: a `String` with four short `append`s) therefore empties two chunks per string, returns one and builds it again for the next string: a 256 KiB region, zeroed, with a free list of up to 8192 entries. Measured with `optexe` on arm64 (200000 strings, instructions retired): 279e9 on a spawned task against 2.2e9 on the main thread, where the program's other strings keep the chunks; with three strings of 20, 40 and 70 bytes alive in the task, 2.4e9. Every `serveWorkers` worker is such a thread: a small POST costs 157 us of user CPU per request with 1 worker against 37 us under `serve`, and 62 us when each worker keeps one string per block size alive (5751 against 12282 requests/s, `serve` 14224). Stop the rebuild without holding much more memory per thread: candidates are one free chunk kept per block size with small first chunks (as arenas have: 4 KiB, doubling), or a few free chunks kept regardless of size and re-cut for the size asked for.
  - implementation_notes: `releaseOwn` (the `emptyChunks_ > 1` branch) and `allocateOwn`; tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_text_heap.cpp pins today's policy ("an emptied chunk is returned except one kept for reuse") and the memory limit (`heldBytes`). Not measured yet: whether `parseRequest` of a small request (550000 instructions on the main thread) and the todo_web list page (21 us per item) pay the same cost.
  - acceptance:
    - a unit test counts chunk regions taken from the heap core: a thread's heap that builds and drops 1000 strings growing through 32, 64 and 128 bytes takes no new region after the first string (today it takes one or more per string)
    - the same loop as an `optexe` program on a spawned task retires at most 2x the instructions of the main-thread run (measured by hand, recorded in the result note)
    - the memory limit still refuses what it refused, and the result note records the bytes a heap holds after freeing everything, before and after
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the free-chunk policy of the string heap; the slot heap is unchanged.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: New free-chunk policy in include/primec/runtime/VmTextHeapBody.inc (VM and `optexe` share it). A size class's first chunk is 4 KiB (`FirstChunkBytes`; one block for a class with larger blocks) and each further chunk is as large as the class's chunks together, up to 256 KiB (4, 4, 8, 16 ... 256 KiB). Of the chunks whose blocks are all free each class keeps one, the smaller of two (the lower of two alike), and the heap keeps at most `FreeChunkLimit` = 1 MiB of them, returning the largest first (the first chunks of all 45 classes are 506 KiB together, so they all fit). Bound on retained memory: a heap whose blocks are all free holds at most one chunk per size class used and at most 1 MiB; before it held one 256 KiB chunk. After the acceptance loop (strings through 32, 64 and 128 bytes) it holds 12 KiB (three first chunks) where it held 256 KiB. The memory limit still counts the chunks and large blocks held and fails with `string memory limit exceeded`; under a limit the free chunks are now returned before an allocation is refused. Because chunks start small, a limit that refused a request only because the first small string had taken a whole 256 KiB chunk now grants it: `setStringMemoryLimit(300000)` with `tryReserve(200)` then `tryReserve(100000)` refused the second before (262144 + 100001) and grants it now (4096 + 100001); tests/unit/language/test_string_owned.cpp pins the same case with a limit of 102000, and that the large reserve alone fits. `TextHeapStats` gained `chunkBytes`, `freeChunkBytes` and `chunkRegions` (C++ only; `__pstext_stat` is unchanged). Tests (tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_text_heap.cpp): chunk sizes 4 KiB doubling to 256 KiB; one free chunk per class, the smaller of two; a class at a chunk boundary keeps the chunk it empties; the first chunks of all classes are kept together; free chunks beyond 1 MiB are returned largest first; a main-thread heap and a thread arena's heap that build and drop 1000 strings through 32, 64 and 128 bytes take 3 regions for the first string and none after; the limit counts a class's growing chunks and returns free chunks before refusing; the random cycle test and tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_heap_arenas.cpp pin the new bound in place of "at most one chunk". Measured by hand on arm64 (11 processors, load average 8 to 20), instructions retired by a loop of 200000 strings (a 3-byte text and four `append`s, 77 bytes), before -> after: `optexe` main thread 544.2e9 -> 3.19e9, `optexe` spawned task 553.2e9 -> 3.39e9 (1.06x the main thread; the scope's 2.2e9 for the main thread was a program that kept other strings alive, this one keeps none and rebuilt chunks on the main thread too); VM without tasks 554.8e9 -> 13.4e9, VM spawned task 694.7e9 -> 153.4e9, where the 140e9 that remain are not the heap: a VM program that uses tasks runs on the step kernel (TODO-5870). Guards: `optexe` instructions of benchmarks/strings before -> after: short_strings 4.623e9 -> 4.638e9, request_heap 5.325e9 -> 5.332e9, append_chunks 1.259e9 -> 1.245e9, request_arena 5.505e9 -> 5.501e9; peak resident bytes: short_strings 1,900,544 -> 1,835,008, request_heap 65,208,320 -> 65,437,696, append_chunks 56,262,656 -> 55,394,304, request_arena 2,113,536 -> 2,097,152, the loop on the main thread 3,670,016 -> 1,851,392 and on a task 2,752,512 -> 1,982,464. `scripts/benchmark.sh` with the baseline: every time check passes before and after and the 40 medians moved between 0.91x and 1.16x, the two largest moves in the C and Rust entries; it exits 1 before and after for the `primestruct_native` artifact sizes only (16538 bytes against 4300 or 8601 allowed). `scripts/benchmark_strings.py --budget` is over budget before and after under this load (short_strings 30.7x -> 32.1x of `std::string`, request_heap 16.4x -> 16.2x, append_chunks 7.1x -> 6.9x, append_bytes 6.7x -> 6.6x). Startup: no code was added to a startup path, and a program's first string of a class now takes and zeroes a 4 KiB region where it took 256 KiB. ThreadSanitizer, one manual run: an `optcpp` program with three tasks running the loop, two tasks returning a `String` the main thread frees and the loop on the main thread, built with `clang++ -std=c++23 -O1 -g -fsanitize=thread -pthread`: expected output, no report.

Now the walk gives each arm of a `pick` its payload binding (`pickArmPayloadBindings`, src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprPick.cpp, the binding the arm's validation uses), for a `pick` statement and a `pick` expression.
    - Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_subjects.cpp, 3 cases: a struct payload of `Maybe<Box>` and of a user sum, in a `pick` statement and a `pick` expression, on every backend of the matrix (VM, C++, `optexe`, native); a `String` payload (`line.byteAt(0i32)`, `line.count()`) of a sum local and of a call result and a struct payload of a call result on the VM and `optexe` with the heap statistics balanced; a method the struct does not have is still `unknown method: /Box/thrice`.

  - owner: ai

  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: With `get_values` returning a `Maybe<vector<i32>>` that holds two elements, `[Maybe<vector<i32>>] got{get_values(4i32)}` and `pick(got) { none { } some(values) { print_line(vectorCount<i32>(values)) } }` prints 896 (an address) on the VM and `optexe` instead of 2; `[vector<i32>] own{values}` then `own.count()` prints the same number and `own[1i32]` prints 2, the count.   - implementation_notes: The payload is stored as the specialized vector record (`resolveVectorPayloadStructPath`, src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpers.cpp) and `makePickPayloadLocalInfo` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickAndDiagnostics.cpp) binds it as a struct pointer, while the arm's uses are typed `vector<i32>`.

  - finished_at: 2026-11-11

A method call validated its receiver for target resolution and again as the first argument, so the second look at one `wait` expression was reported as a second wait; the same source position is now one wait. In the lowering, the collection receiver path emitted a vector-shaped receiver and then fell through to the ordinary call path, which emitted it again (a `wait` waited twice), and a method call or element read on an owning call result or a struct `wait` result read the receiver after the callee had destroyed its local (`make_values().count()` gave 0 and leaked). The receiver is now bound to a hidden local that lives to the end of the statement and is destroyed there, ahead of both paths, so it is evaluated once and read while alive. Tests: program-matrix `a method call on a wait result waits once` (VM seeds 1 to 8, optexe, heap balanced) and two semantics cases (one wait as a method receiver, a second wait still rejected).

  - owner: ai

  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: `pick(get(5i32)) { none { } some(line) { [String] owned{move(line)} } }` followed by a second `pick(get(6i32)) { none { } some(line) { [String] copied{line} } }` in the same function is rejected with `use-after-move: line was moved at ...`: the move is recorded for the name, not for the binding of the first arm. Naming the first binder differently compiles. End a payload binding's move state with its arm.
  - implementation_notes: The use-after-move check of src/semantics; compare with a `[String] line{...}` declared in two sibling `if` blocks, which is accepted.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the two picks compile and print both bytes on the VM; so do two arms of one `pick` that bind the same name and one of which moves it
    - negative: `move(line)` followed by a use of `line` in the same arm is still `use-after-move`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: move state of `pick` payload bindings.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: moves are recorded by name in `movedBindings`, and `pick` validation (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprPick.cpp) neither removed a payload binding's name when its arm ended nor tracked arms as separate paths, so a move in one arm poisoned the same name in a later arm or `pick`, and a move of an outer binding in one arm made a sibling arm's read a use-after-move. Each arm of a statement or expression `pick` now starts from the move state before the `pick`, the payload binding's entry is dropped at the arm's start and end, and after the `pick` a binding is moved when an arm that falls through moved it (as for `if` branches). Tests: three cases in tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_subjects.cpp (two picks and two arms binding `line` with one moving it, statement and expression form, an outer binding moved in one arm and read in the other, VM and optexe, heap balanced; use after the move in the same arm and use of an outer binding after the `pick` whose arm moved it are still rejected).

  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11

An arm value that is a place other than a local (a field, an element) must be copied with the type's `Copy` helpers.     - positive: both programs print the field's value on the VM and `optexe`, the holder's field stays readable, and the heap statistics are balanced
    - negative: a `String` field and an `i32` arm are still incompatible

  - stop_rule: field and element values of `pick` expression arms.

Fix: an arm value that is a place the arm does not end is copied with the type's `Copy` helpers (the same rule as TODO-5879, one root cause, one commit), and an arm whose kind is unknown takes the kind of its inferred binding type when that is a struct or a vector. - [x] TODO-5879: A `pick` expression's result owns a value of its own
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: A `pick` expression takes over whatever its arm names. `[vector<i32>] kept{pick(get_values(3i32)) { none { vector<i32>{} } some(values) { mine } }}` with `mine` a local of the enclosing scope leaves `mine` readable after `kept` freed its buffer, and the same for a `String` local. `pick(held) { none { label(0i32) } some(line) { line } }` with `held` a sum local clears the local's drop flag, so a later `pick(held)` reads a block the result freed; with `held` a parameter the caller destroys the payload too (`string heap block freed twice`). A `pick` expression of struct type passed as an argument is never destroyed (32 string-heap bytes a call). The result must own a value of its own: take over a fresh value and a local that ends with the arm, copy every other place, and destroy a result given as an argument after the call.
  - implementation_notes: found testing whether a discarded vector-yielding `pick` expression, or one whose arm yields a borrowed vector, leaks or frees twice; those do not (the callers of `isFreshBuiltinVectorExpr` copy a borrowed place in the arm and free a discarded result).
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the programs print the local's and the payload's value before and after the result ends, on the VM and `optexe`, with the heap statistics balanced
    - negative: covered by TODO-5877 (mismatched arms are still rejected)
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: what a `pick` expression arm's value does to the place it names.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: `tryEmitPickExpr` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickAndDiagnostics.cpp) treated an arm value that is a name as a local the arm may give away: it cleared the drop flag of whatever the name was (an outer local kept its buffer and its flag for a vector, a sum local lost its flag for a payload binding, a borrowed subject has no flag at all), so two owners freed one block or one owner read a freed one. `isOwnedTemporaryArgumentExpr` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererFlowControlHelpers.cpp) did not count a `pick` expression as a temporary, so a struct result given as an argument was never destroyed. Fix: one rule in `tryEmitPickExpr` for struct and vector results: a fresh value is taken over; a local declared in the arm, and the payload binding of a subject the `pick` itself owns (a call result), is taken over by clearing its flag; every other place is copied with the type's `Copy` helpers. A `pick` expression is an owned temporary argument. The risk that started it is tested and absent: a discarded vector-yielding `pick` expression and arms yielding a vector parameter, a vector local or an element are balanced. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp (8 cases, VM step and fast kernels and `optexe`, heap statistics in every one). Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md. Found and filed: TODO-5880 (a payload moved out of a sum local leaves it readable; a payload of a borrowed sum can be moved or returned) and TODO-5881 (`some<T>(...)` with a call to `some<T>` inside its argument is "recursive" on the VM).

- [x] TODO-5880: A payload moved out of a sum local leaves the local moved-from
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: In `pick(held) { none { } some(line) { [String] taken{move(line)} } }` with `[Maybe<String>] held`, the arm takes the payload's storage and `held` stays readable: a later `pick(held)` reads a block that `taken` freed. Passing `line` to a `[String move]` parameter does the same. With `held` a parameter or a field (a sum the definition only borrows), `move(line)` and `return(line)` end the program with `string heap block freed twice`: the owner destroys the payload as well. Moving a payload binding that owns resources out of a sum local must leave that local moved-from; a payload of a borrowed sum must not be moved or returned.
  - implementation_notes: the payload binding shares the subject's drop flag (`bindPickPayload`, src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickAndDiagnostics.cpp), so the lowering is right for an owned subject; the semantic validator (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprPick.cpp) erases the binder's moved state at the end of the arm without telling the subject.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: a payload moved out of a sum local and one passed to a `move` parameter print their value on the VM and `optexe` with the heap statistics balanced
    - negative: a `pick` on the sum local after the move is `use-after-move`; `move(line)` and `return(line)` of a payload of a sum parameter and of a sum field are rejected
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: moves and returns of `pick` payload bindings.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: the validator of a `pick` arm (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprPick.cpp) forgot the payload binding's moved state when the arm ended and never asked who owns the payload, so the sum local stayed readable after its payload's storage went to a new owner, and a payload of a sum the definition only borrows could be moved or returned although its owner destroys it too. A second cause hid half of it: `bindingOwnsResources` (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorStatementContainerHelpers.cpp) did not resolve a struct name the file imports, so outside `/std/text` a `String` (binding or payload) passed to a `move` parameter was not moved-from at all. Fix: `pickPayloadOwner` classifies the subject of a `pick` for a payload that owns resources: a local or a `copy`/`move` parameter is moved-from at the end of an arm that moved the payload out (`move(line)`, a `move` parameter), in `pick` statements and expressions; the payload binding of a read-only parameter, `this`, a `Reference`/`Pointer` local, a field, an element or another lent payload is lent, and `move(line)`, a `move` parameter and `return(line)` are rejected with `borrowed pick payload cannot be moved: line` / `borrowed pick payload escapes via return: line`. A fresh subject, a builtin `vector<T>` payload (its binding is a view that is copied) and `[unsafe]` bodies are untouched. `bindingOwnsResources` resolves imported struct names. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp, "a payload moved out of a sum local is destroyed by its new owner" (VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced), "a sum local whose payload was moved out is moved-from" and "the payload of a borrowed sum is not moved or returned". Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md.

- [x] TODO-5874: Assigning to a `mut` sum local destroys the payload it held
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: `[Maybe<String> mut] held{get(4i32)}` followed by `held = get(6i32)` and `held = none<String>()` leaves `stringHeapBytesInUse()` 64 higher at scope end on the VM and `optexe`: neither assignment destroys the payload the local held. The same with a `Maybe<vector<i32>>` leaves two heap blocks. `assign` of an owning struct value destroys the old value first (docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md); do the same for a sum local.
  - implementation_notes: Sum assignment is lowered in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersConstructEmit.cpp (`emitExistingSumValueIntoLocal` and the constructor paths write into the local's slots); `emitActiveSumPayloadDestroyFromSumPtr` destroys an active payload.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the block leaves the heap statistics unchanged on the VM and `optexe`, for a `String`, a struct with `Destroy` and a `vector<T>` payload
    - negative: `held = held` keeps the payload readable
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: assignment to sum locals.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: `assign` to a struct-shaped local goes through the owned-assign callback of src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerOperatorsConversionsAndCalls.h, which asks `structNeedsDestroyHelpers` about the target's type; a sum path is no struct with destroy helpers, so the new sum was copied slot by slot over the old one: the old payload leaked, and a sum assigned from another local shared that local's payload (`string heap block freed twice` when both were destroyed). Fix: the callback has a branch for a sum whose payloads need destroying: the new value is taken over from a temporary (a call, a constructor, `move(other)`) or, from a place, given a payload of its own by the new `SumHelpersContext::emitActiveSumPayloadCopyFromSumPtrs` (the payload's `Copy` helpers, a vector's buffer); then the payload the local held is destroyed if the local owned one, and the local owns the new value. The copy is made first, so `held = held` is valid. A `mut` sum local built from a place now has a drop flag that starts cleared, so an assignment can give it a value of its own, and a sum local initialized with `move(other)` takes over `other`'s drop flag (it leaked before). Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp, "assigning to a mut sum local destroys the payload it held" (`String`, `vector<i32>` and a struct with `Destroy`; `held = held`) and "a sum local assigned from a place gets a payload of its own", on the VM and `optexe` with the heap statistics balanced. Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md. Not covered: a target without a drop flag (a `mut` sum parameter, a `Reference` to a sum, a sum field) is still overwritten slot by slot.

- [x] TODO-5883: Assigning to a `mut` builtin vector local destroys what it held and copies a place
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: Found while reproducing TODO-5876 (assignment from a `pick` expression). `[vector<i32> mut] kept{make_values(1i32)}` followed by `kept = make_values(3i32)` leaves one heap block live at scope end on the VM and `optexe` (`heapLiveBlocks()`), and `kept = other` for a `[vector<i32>] other` ends with `VM error: invalid heap free address in IR`: the assignment stores the source's record pointer in the local, so the vector it held is never freed and a place assigned to it has two owners.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: assignment from a call, a constructor, a place, itself and in a loop leaves the heap statistics unchanged on the VM and `optexe`, for scalar and struct elements; the place keeps its own elements
    - negative: the source of `kept = other` is unchanged by a later `kept.push(...)`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: builtin `vector<T>` locals that own their record.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: `assign` to a name (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererOperatorCollectionMutationHelpers.cpp) handled struct-shaped locals with ownership and fell through to `emitExpr(rhs); StoreLocal` for everything else; a builtin vector local holds a pointer to its record, so the assignment repointed it at the source's record. Fix: a builtin vector local with a drop flag goes through the owned-assign callback (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerOperatorsConversionsAndCalls.h, `BuiltinVectorAssignPath`): the new record is slot-copied into a temporary, given a buffer of its own unless the right side is a fresh vector (`isFreshBuiltinVectorExpr`: a constructor, a user call, a `pick` expression), then the vector the local held is destroyed through its drop entry (the scope-end code, `emitBuiltinVectorDrop`), and the new record is installed in a record of the assignment's own, so a loop that assigns again does not overwrite the old record before it is destroyed. The drop entry carries the element copy path (`DropEntry::builtinVectorElementCopyPath`), set for a declared `vector<T>` local and an inferred vector of scalars. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_container_copies.cpp, "assigning to a mut vector local destroys what it held and copies a place" (VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced) and "a vector local assigned from another keeps its own elements on every backend". Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md. Left open as TODO-5884: a `mut` vector parameter and an inferred vector-of-struct local.

- [x] TODO-5876: `return(pick(...))` of a vector and assignment from a `pick` expression
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: In a definition with `return<vector<i32>>`, `return(pick(get_values(first)) { none { vector<i32>{} } some(values) { values } })` is rejected with `return type mismatch: expected vector`; binding the `pick` to a local and returning the local works, and so does the same `return` with `String` arms. And `kept = pick(get(3i32)) { none { label(0i32) } some(line) { line } }` for a `[String mut] kept` (the same for a `vector<i32>`) is rejected with `unable to infer implicit template arguments for /std/maybe/some`, though no `some` call is in the statement. Accept both; the returned or assigned value is the `pick`'s own (docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md), and the assignment destroys what the local held.
  - implementation_notes: The return check is in src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorStatementReturns.cpp (the return kind of a `pick` expression with collection arms); `pick` branch typing is in src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprPick.cpp. `tryEmitPickExpr` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickAndDiagnostics.cpp) builds the result.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: both programs print the picked value on the VM and `optexe` with the heap statistics balanced, for a `String` and a `vector<i32>`
    - negative: `return(pick(...))` with `i32` arms from a `return<vector<i32>>` definition is still a return type mismatch
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: `pick` expressions as return and assignment values.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Two root causes. (1) Return: the return check (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorStatementReturns.cpp) normalized the returned binding's whole type text to a collection path; for a `pick` expression the inferred binding names the collection with its element type in the type name (`vector<i32>`) and an empty template argument, so the text did not normalize and the value was not seen as a vector. The check now falls back to the binding's type name. (2) Assignment: the operator rewrite of the text filter (src/text_filter/TextFilterPipelineOperatorRewrite.cpp, `parsePrimaryExpression`) ended the right operand of `=` at the `)` of `pick(subject)`, because a `{` after a space is not a call suffix, so `kept = pick(x) { arms }` became `assign(kept, pick(x)) { arms }`: a `pick` call without arms followed by a block, which the implicit-template inference then reported against `/std/maybe/some`. A `pick(...)` operand now takes its arm block (on the same line) with it, and the arms are rewritten like any other body. The assigned value is the `pick`'s own (fresh), so the `String` path and the vector path of TODO-5883 take it over and destroy what the local held. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp, "a pick expression is returned as a vector and as a String", "a pick expression assigned to a mut local replaces what it held" (VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced) and "a returned pick expression with integer arms is not a vector". Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md. Found and left open as TODO-5885: a vector temporary used only as the receiver of `count()` or an index is not freed.

- [x] TODO-5875: `count()` on a local declared `Vector<T>` lowers
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: With `import /std/collections/*`, `[Vector<i32>] local{vector<i32>(1i32, 2i32)}` followed by `print_line(local.count())` stops with `VM lowering error: vm backend only supports entry argument indexing`; `vectorCount<i32>(local)` prints 2, and the same binding declared `vector<i32>` reads its count with `local.count()`. The payload binding of a `Maybe<Vector<i32>>` in a `pick` arm fails the same way. Make the method spelling resolve like the helper call.
  - implementation_notes: The error is the fallback of the entry-argument access path (src/ir_lowerer), reached when the `count` method call has no collection or method target; compare the facts published for the `vector<i32>` spelling with `--dump-stage`.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: `local.count()` and `local[1i32]` print 2 on the VM and `optexe` for the `Vector<i32>` local and for a `Maybe<Vector<i32>>` payload binding
    - negative: `local.missing()` is still `unknown method`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: method calls on bindings declared with the stdlib `Vector<T>` spelling.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: `tryEmitCountAccessCall` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererCountAccessHelpersEmit.cpp) takes every unqualified `count` call with one argument as a builtin count and rejected a receiver whose type text is neither a string nor a builtin collection with the entry-argument fallback error; the receiver of `local.count()` on a `Vector<i32>` local is the monomorphized stdlib struct (`/std/collections/vector/Vector__t...`), for which the semantic product has a resolved method target (`/std/collections/vector/count`). The rejection now applies only when no method target is resolved, so the call lowers as the ordinary method call it is. `local[1i32]` worked already. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp, "count and an index read a local and a pick payload declared Vector" (a local, the payload of a fresh `Maybe<Vector<i32>>` and of a sum local; VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced) and "a method a Vector local does not have is an unknown call target" (the diagnostic is `unknown call target: missing`, not `unknown method` as the acceptance guessed). Found and left open as TODO-5886: `push` on a `Vector<T>` local is `unknown call target: push`.

- [x] TODO-5878: A `[move name]` lambda capture compiles
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: `[i32 mut] n{4i32}` followed by `[mut] show{[move n]([i32] more) { return(n + more) }}` is rejected with `unable to infer implicit template arguments for /main__lambda0_make`; the same for a `String`, a `vector<i32>` and a `pick` payload binding. docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md lists `[move name]` as a capture form, and no test uses it. Make the capture move `name` into the closure, so that `name` is moved-from afterwards and the closure destroys the value.
  - implementation_notes: `desugarLambda` (src/semantics/SemanticsValidateLambdaClosures.cpp) passes `move(name)` to the closure's factory; the factory's template inference does not see through the `move` call.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the program prints 5 on the VM and `optexe`; a moved `String` and a moved `vector<i32>` print their value with the heap statistics balanced
    - negative: a use of `name` after the lambda is `use-after-move`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: `[move name]` captures.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: `desugarLambda` turns the lambda into a call of a generic factory and passes `move(name)` for a `[move name]` capture; `inferBindingTypeForMonomorph` (src/semantics/TemplateMonomorphImplicitTemplateInference.cpp), which gives the factory's type parameters their types from the arguments, knew `location(x)` (a `[ref x]` capture) and not `move(x)`, so no type was inferred for the capture. It now gives `move(x)` the type of `x`. The move itself, the moved-from state of the name and the closure's ownership of the value were already right once the factory was instantiated. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pick_values.cpp, "a move capture hands the value to the closure" (an `i32`, a `String`, a `vector<i32>`, the payload binding of a fresh and of a named sum; VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced) and "a name captured by move is moved-from after the lambda" (`use-after-move` for a `String` and a vector).

- [x] TODO-5884: Assigning to a `mut` vector parameter or an inferred vector-of-struct local keeps one owner
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: Two builtin `vector<T>` targets that `assign` still only repoints. (1) In `swap_in([vector<i32> mut] values) { values = make_values(8i32) ... }` called with a temporary, the assignment leaves two heap blocks live after the call on the VM (`heapLiveBlocks()`): the parameter's drop entry has no element copy path, so the vector it held is not destroyed and the new one has no owner. (2) `[mut] names{make_named(1i32)}` (the type inferred, the element a struct with a `String` field) leaves `stringHeapBytesInUse()` 32 higher per element at scope end even without an assignment: the drop entry of an inferred binding has no element struct path, so the buffer is freed and the elements are not destroyed; an assignment to it stores the source's record pointer (a second owner for a place, a leak for a temporary). A local declared `[vector<T> mut]` and an inferred vector of scalars are right.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: both shapes leave the heap statistics unchanged on the VM and `optexe`, with and without an assignment from a temporary and from a place
    - negative: a `[vector<i32> mut]` parameter that is not assigned still writes through to the caller's vector
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: builtin vector parameters and inferred builtin vector locals.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root causes, one per shape. (1) The owned assignment looked its target up among the drop entries by drop flag and needed the entry's element copy path; a parameter's entry had none and a `mut` parameter was skipped by the parameter loop altogether, so the assignment only repointed the callee's local. (2) The binding lowering read the element type from the binding's own `vector<T>` transform, which an inferred binding does not have, so the drop entry had no element path. Found on the way: a `[vector<T> copy mut]` parameter was not copied (the callee pushed into the caller's vector), a `[vector<T> move]` parameter was never freed, and a temporary vector of structs passed to any parameter destroyed only its first element (the entry's element stride was one slot). Fix: the element path now lives on the local (`LocalInfo::vectorElementLifecyclePath`), set where the element type is known - a declared or inferred binding (the type semantics inferred), a parameter - and the owned assignment (`BuiltinVectorAssignPath` in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerOperatorsConversionsAndCalls.h) reads it from the target instead of searching the drop entries. The parameter rule (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerInlineCallsBody.h): a `copy` parameter is copied unless the argument is a fresh vector or `move(x)`; a `move` parameter and a fresh vector given to any parameter belong to the callee (drop entry, element slots from the element's layout); a `mut` parameter given a place is a borrow, and assigning to it destroys the caller's vector and writes the new record over the caller's record, so the caller sees and later destroys the new one. An inferred `[mut] b{a}` of a vector of structs is now a copy, as the declared form was. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_vector_owners.cpp (new suite, 5 cases: scalar and struct `mut` parameters with temporary, place, field and nested-borrow arguments; write-through without assignment on every backend; inferred locals; `copy mut` and `move` parameters), heap statistics balanced on the VM and `optexe`.

  - parallel_track: pick-payloads

  - acceptance:

  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The operator rewrite skipped only spaces and tabs between `pick(subject)` and `{`, so arms that open on a later line were not part of the assigned operand. It now skips any whitespace, line breaks included. Tests: `an assigned pick keeps arms that open on a later line` (text_filters.pipeline.rewrites, the first text-filter test of `pick`; it also checks the same-line form) and `the arms of an assigned pick may open on the line after the subject` (program_matrix.sum_owners; assignment, an operand of `+`, a binding initializer and a statement, on the VM and `optexe`).

- [x] TODO-5881: A call takes a call to the same template instantiation as its argument on the VM
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: `some<String>(first_or(get(3i32)))`, where `get` itself returns `some<String>(...)` and is inlined into the argument, is rejected with `vm backend does not support recursive calls: /std/maybe/some__t...`; so is `some<vector<i32>>(pick(get_values(id)) { ... })`. The call is not recursive: one instantiation of `some` appears inside the argument of another call to it. Binding the argument to a local first works.

    - negative: a definition that calls itself is still rejected on the VM

  - stop_rule: calls to one definition inside an argument of a call to it.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The lowerer put the callee on its inline stack before it lowered the call's arguments, so a call to the same definition (or template instantiation) inlined into an argument looked like recursion. The non-struct call path now takes the callee off the stack while it lowers arguments written at the call site and puts it back before the body; default arguments and struct constructors keep the guard. `some<String>(first_or(get(3i32)))`, `some<vector<i32>>(pick(get_values(id)) { ... })` and `twice(twice(twice(3i32)))` run on the VM and `optexe` with the heap statistics balanced (tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_sum_owners.cpp), and `same(same(main()))` inside `main` is still rejected on the VM. Gate 2083/2083.

- [x] TODO-5888: An element of a vector temporary read as a struct or a String
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)
  - parallel_track: pick-payloads
  - scope: memory safety. With `make_rows` returning a `vector<Row>` (`Row` has an `i32` and a `String` field), `[Row] copy{make_rows(6i32)[1i32]}` and `first_byte(make_rows(4i32)[1i32].text)` read the wrong slots on the VM and `optexe` (`VM error: invalid text range` / `unaligned indirect address`): an index above 0 into a vector-of-struct temporary uses a stride of one slot. Index 0 reads the right element, and every such read leaves the vector live (one heap block and the elements' strings). A scalar result (`make_rows(5i32)[1i32].id`, `count()`) is right since TODO-5885; binding the vector to a local first is right.
  - implementation_notes: TODO-5885 lowers a read with a scalar result through a hidden local in a scope that spans the read (top of `emitExpr`, src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerEmitExpr.h). A struct, `String` or vector result points into the vector, so the vector must live until the end of the statement that consumes it (a binding initializer copies after `emitExpr` returns; a call argument is borrowed for the call). Either give the hidden local the lifetime of the enclosing statement, or copy the element into an owned temporary that the consumer takes over (`isOwnedTemporaryArgumentExpr` does not know an index expression).
  - acceptance:
    - positive: `[Row] copy{make_rows(6i32)[1i32]}`, `first_byte(make_rows(4i32)[1i32].text)` and `[String] text{make_rows(6i32)[0i32].text}` print the right values on the VM and `optexe` and leave the heap statistics unchanged
    - negative: the same reads from a named vector leave the vector usable
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: an element of a builtin vector temporary read as a struct, a `String` or a vector.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Root cause: only a read with a scalar result got the hidden local of TODO-5885; a struct, `String` or vector element was read from the bare call result, whose element type the access did not know (a stride of one slot), and nobody owned the vector. Fix: the same hidden, typed local now also serves an element read as a struct, a `String` or a vector (top of `emitExpr`, src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerEmitExpr.h), but in the current scope and until the end of the statement: the element stays a place, so every consumer (a binding, an argument, an assignment, `push`, a field read) copies from it exactly as from a named vector. `emitStatement` is wrapped (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerReturnEmitStage.cpp) and destroys the hidden locals its statement made once the statement is lowered (`LowerSetupStageState::statementTemporaryDrops`); a `return` leaves them to the scope, whose exit path runs after the value is copied out. Code that may not run or runs again inside one statement is a scope of its own (`emitScopedValueExpr`): a `while`/`for` condition and the right side of `and`/`or`. A read-only `vector<T>` binding, which stays a view of a named place, copies when the place is in such a temporary. The lowerer's old `struct parameter type mismatch` rejection of a one-argument call on such an element no longer applies to a builtin vector temporary. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_vector_owners.cpp, "an element of a vector temporary read as a struct or a String is copied out of it", "... read as a String, a vector or a field of those is copied", "... read where code may not run or runs again is destroyed each time" and "an element read from a named vector is a copy and leaves the vector usable" (VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced). Spec: docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md. Found and left open: TODO-5891 (a returned vector field or vector element of a local is not copied) and TODO-5892 (a block expression whose value is an owning local frees it twice).

- [x] TODO-5887: `remove_at` and `remove_swap` compile on a vector of sums
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Result and control flow (docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md)

- [x] TODO-5895: A spawned call with a `copy` or `move` scalar or struct parameter runs as a task
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Runtime Model)
  - parallel_track: mt-vm-tasks
  - scope: the first slice of TODO-5847. A spawned call with a `[T copy]`, `[T copy mut]` or `[T move]` parameter of a scalar or of a struct that is not a `Function` ran inline with an `--opt-report` note, and `[String copy mut]` is what the checker tells a user to write for a task that changes its argument. Give those shapes a real call on the address ABI and lower their spawns to `TaskSpawn`.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: tasks with `[i32 copy mut]`, `[String copy mut]`, `[Named copy mut]` and `[Named move]` parameters change their own copies on the VM (default schedule and seeds 1 to 8) and on `optexe`, the spawner's values unchanged, heap balanced; the same definitions called directly run as real calls with the lifecycle order of the inlined call
    - negative: a `copy` or `move` sum keeps its inline note
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: owned scalar and struct parameters of real calls and spawned calls; collections and sums stay in TODO-5847.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The address ABI took `copy`/`move` parameters only for a `Function`, so every other owned parameter kept its definition inline and its spawn inline. It now takes any scalar and any struct but a sum: the call site binds the copy (or the moved or temporary value) as before and passes the value or the copy's address, and the body owns it. A `copy mut` scalar in a real-call body was bound as the address of a caller's place (`unaligned indirect address` when a task passed the value); it is the body's own slot now. An owned sum stays inline: a `[Item move]` real call freed the payload twice on the VM (noted in TODO-5847). Tests: program-matrix `real calls own their copy and move parameters` (Copy and Destroy helper order as inlined, heap balanced) and tasks `a task owns its copy or move argument` (VM default and seeds 1 to 8, `optexe`, heap balanced through the arena probe); ir pipeline `address ABI takes any struct but a sum by move or copy`; the opt-report notes in the optexe and VM task tests name an owned sum and a `string` parameter instead.

  - owner: ai

  - parallel_track: closures-lifecycle
  - scope: With `[Function<i32, i32> mut] plain{[seven]([i32] x) { return(x + seven) }}` and a struct `Wrap` whose only field is `[Function<i32, i32> mut] run`, `[Wrap mut] wrap{Wrap{plain}}` followed by `print_line(plain(1i32))` prints 8 and then ends with `VM error: invalid heap free address in IR`: the field and the local share one closure block and both free it. Make the positional argument take the same copy path as the labeled one.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the `Wrap{plain}` and `Mutex<Function<i32, i32>>{plain}` programs print 8 and exit 0 on the VM and `optexe`, with the heap balanced

  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: A brace constructor with one positional argument parses it as `block() { value }`, and the copy classifier (`shouldDisarmStructCopySourceExpr`) took every block for a temporary, so a `Function` local was bound into the field without a copy and both freed one closure block. A block with one expression now classifies as that expression, so a place is copied exactly as the labeled form copies it (`Wrap{plain}`, `Mutex<Function<i32, i32>>{plain}`); `Wrap{move(plain)}` is still the use-after-move diagnostic.

  - owner: ai

    - negative: a lambda naming a type parameter that the definition does not have is still an unknown type

  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The lambda-closures pass lifts a lambda into a closure struct and factory that are templates over the capture types only, before monomorphization, so a type parameter of the enclosing definition written in the lambda (`[Reference<T>] item`) had no meaning in them.   - scope: Calling a closure with the result of a call that returns `Reference<T>` (`body(borrow_of(slot))`, `borrow_of` a `[return<Reference<T>>]` definition over `borrow(dereference(slot))`) hands the body a wrong address: the body reads and writes something other than the value.   - result: The inline-call lowering of a `Reference<T>` parameter (and of a `[T mut]` scalar parameter) passed an argument that is not a name or `location(...)` by storing its value in a temporary and borrowing the temporary. Such a call is now passed as it is (`isReferenceReturningCallExpr` in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererInlineParamHelpers.cpp), for plain definitions and for closure `call` methods alike; a value-returning call still borrows a temporary. `Mutex.locked` passes `mutexValueBorrow` directly. Using such a call as a value (`[i64] x{borrow_of(slot)}`) yields the address, which is TODO-5934.

  - parallel_track: diagnostics
  - scope: In benchmarks/http/bench_server.prime with `main` changed to `serve(bench_router(), config)?` (no `on_error`), or with its body changed to `print_line(nothing_here)` where `io_out` is not declared, `primec --emit-diagnostics --dump-stage ast-semantic` puts the primary span at `stdlib/std/http/http.prime:827:7` and the first related span at `definition: /std/http/AppRouter__t.../call`, with `definition: /main` second; the message is right (`missing on_error for ? usage`, `print_line requires io_out effect`) but the span is the stale position of the last definition the validator touched. A program with only `import /std/http/*` and an unknown identifier in `main` reports the right line (6:14), so it needs more imports (`/std/http/server`, `/std/os`, `/std/text`) or the generic `AppRouter<Bench>` instance. Report an expression diagnostic at the expression and name the definition it is in.
  - implementation_notes: `failExprDiagnostic` calls `captureExprContext(expr)` (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorDiagnostics.cpp); find why the expression's own position is not used for `try` and for the effect check of a call in `main` there. Reduce first: drop imports until the span is right.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the two programs above report their span in the user's file at the `?` and at `print_line`, with `/main` as the definition
    - negative: a diagnostic inside a stdlib definition still reports the stdlib position
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the primary span and definition of expression diagnostics in user definitions.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The validator infers the return type of the generic `/std/http` router by trying expressions that fail and are dropped (`inferDefinitionReturnBinding` clears `error_` and goes on; the failures are `unknown method target for routes` and the like in `AppRouter<Bench>`). Each failure ran `failExprDiagnostic`, whose `captureExprContext` sets the primary span only when none is set, and nothing cleared the span when the failure was dropped, so the first real diagnostic of a later definition (`main`) kept the old one. `SemanticValidationResultSink::clearContext` made it worse: it did nothing unless structured diagnostics were being collected, although the capture works in every mode. `failExprDiagnostic`, `failDefinitionDiagnostic` and `failExecutionDiagnostic` now start a failure with no context when `error_` is empty (a failure being passed up keeps the spans its scopes added), and `clearContext` clears in every mode. The span of `serve(bench_router(), config)?` is now `bench_server.prime` line 74 with `definition: /main`, and `print_line(nothing_here)` is reported at its line. Tests: text_filters `diagnostics_stdlib_span` (a mistake in `main` and one in a user helper of a program that imports the http server; both report the user's file and definition and no `http.prime`; the first fails without the change). The negative bullet "a diagnostic inside a stdlib definition still reports the stdlib position" has no user-reachable case (every error a user program causes is reported at the user's expression), so the helper-definition case stands in for it; the golden diagnostics suites pass unchanged.

- [x] TODO-5861: `SharedString` keeps its owner count inside the text block
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-10
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Heaps; docs/spec/strings-and-views.md, Beyond std::string)
  - parallel_track: string-concurrency
  - scope: The atomic owner count of a `SharedString` (stdlib/std/text/shared.prime) is one heap slot of its own beside the text block, because byte regions (`__pstext_alloc`) are not 8-byte aligned (large blocks, arena bumps) and the atomic opcodes (`__psatomic_*_i64`) take heap slot addresses only. So making a `SharedString` allocates and frees twice: an `optexe` loop of 1000000 `sharedFrom` plus destroy retires 4.67e9 instructions, against 3.01e9 with the old in-block plain count. Give the string heap an 8-aligned allocation (or align every block), let the atomic opcodes work on an aligned byte address on the VM and in the optimized C++ runtime, and put the count in the block again (before the text or after its padded 0 byte).
  - implementation_notes: `resolveIndirectAddress` of the VM and `ps_resolve` of src/backend/IrToOptCppEmitter.cpp reject byte addresses today; byte-region liveness (TODO-5793) already finds a region from an address. Measure with `/usr/bin/time -l` (instructions retired) on the two loops in the result note of the atomic count TODO in docs/todo_archive/2026-11.md.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: making a `SharedString` allocates one block (heap live blocks grow by 1 less than today); the create and destroy loop retires at most 3.2e9 instructions on `optexe` and the copy and destroy loop of 5000000 rounds no more than today's 4.5e9; the program-matrix `shared_strings` suite passes unchanged on the VM (all seeds) and `optexe`
    - negative: an atomic opcode on an unaligned byte address faults by name on the VM and on `optexe`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: where the count lives; native follows with TODO-5800.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: A `SharedString` kept its owner count in a heap slot of its own because the atomic opcodes took slot addresses only and byte regions were not 8-byte aligned, so making one allocated twice (4.67e9 instructions for 1000000 `sharedFrom` and destroy rounds on `optexe`). Byte regions of the heap (`VmHeapCore`, src: include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc, shared by the VM, the debugger and the generated `optexe` runtime) now occupy a multiple of 8 bytes each, so every region and every string block (all size classes are multiples of 8) starts at a multiple of 8; a region is still exactly as long as asked and the padding is not addressable. The atomic opcodes accept an 8-byte aligned byte-region address whose 8 bytes lie in one live region (`resolveAtomicAddress`, a new `VmKernelHost` hook with a default that keeps the old rule, in src/runtime/VmHeapHelpers.cpp; `ps_resolve_atomic` in src/backend/IrToOptCppRuntime.h); an unaligned address faults `unaligned atomic address in IR` and a cell outside one live region `invalid atomic address in IR`, on the VM (step kernel and debugger) and in `optexe`. The block of a `SharedString` is now the count (8 bytes) followed by the text and its 0 byte, `bytes` points at the text, and the count is `reinterpret<i64>(textAddress(bytes, -8))`; the struct lost its `ownerCount` field (3 slots instead of 4). Cost on `optexe` (instructions retired, `/usr/bin/time -l`): 1000000 `sharedFrom` and destroy rounds 4.67e9 before, 2.85e9 after (3.01e9 with the plain in-block count of TODO-5638); 5000000 copy and destroy rounds 4.49e9 before, 4.17e9 after. Making a `SharedString` takes one string block and no slot allocation. Tests: program matrix `shared_strings` "a SharedString is one string block that holds its text and its owner count" (VM step, seeds 1 and 2, `optexe`; the existing four-task, hand-over and channel cases pass unchanged and leave the heap empty), VM `atomics` (an aligned byte cell works and its bytes are the native-endian value; unaligned, partial and freed cells fault by name), `byte_regions` (every region starts at a multiple of 8 and keeps its exact length; the free-run test now uses multiples of 8), `optexe_tasks` (the same cells on `optexe` match the VM and fault with the same messages). Docs: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Atomics), docs/spec/strings-and-views.md, docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md. The arm64 native backend still has no atomics (TODO-5800).

- [x] TODO-5870: A VM program that uses tasks runs its string code on the fast kernel
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/spec/vm-design.md, Tasks; found measuring the string heap, TODO-5867)
  - parallel_track: vm-tasks
  - scope: A module with a `TaskSpawn` or `TaskWait` anywhere runs every function on the VM's step kernel under the task scheduler (src/runtime/VmFastKernelPrepare.cpp keeps tasks, atomics, mutexes and conditions off the fast kernel; `moduleUsesTasks` in src/runtime/VmExecutionKernel.cpp). Measured on arm64 with `primevm` (instructions retired): a loop that builds and drops 200000 `String`s (a 3-byte text and four `append`s, 77 bytes) retires 13.4e9 in a program without tasks and 153.4e9 when the same loop runs in a spawned task, and the same 153.4e9 on the main task of a program that spawns one unrelated `seven()` first. A loop of integer arithmetic costs the same either way (55e6 for 200000 rounds), so the cost is in calls or in the host calls of `String`, not in the scheduler's loop. Find which instructions cost 700000 host instructions per string on the step kernel and either run the functions that contain no switch point on the fast kernel between switch points or make those instructions cheap.
  - implementation_notes: the loop is the one in the result note of the string heap task (docs/todo_archive/); the heap itself takes no region per string any more, so the difference is all kernel. `optexe` runs the same loop in 3.2e9 (main) and 3.4e9 (task).
  - acceptance:
    - the string loop above on a spawned VM task retires at most 2x the instructions of the same loop in a program without tasks (measured by hand, recorded in the result note)
    - the deterministic schedule is unchanged: the seeded task tests print what they print today
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: VM execution speed of programs that use tasks; no new language surface.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: The step kernel's cost was never the scheduler: with tasks the whole module ran on the checked step kernel (one vector-backed frame and a bounds check per instruction, 11 to 14 times the host instructions of the flat loop on string code), because prepareModule declined every function that holds a task, atomic, mutex or condition opcode. Fix: the flat loop became resumable per call stack. `runVmFastTask` (src/runtime/VmFastKernel.cpp) runs a `VmFastTask` (operand stack, locals arena, frames, instruction pointer; src/runtime/VmFastKernelProgram.h) until its root function returns, a trap ends the program, or it reaches one of the 11 scheduler opcodes, where it hands the call stack back with `ip` at the opcode; `VmTaskScheduler` (src/runtime/VmTaskScheduler.cpp, split out of VmExecutionKernel.cpp for the file-size limit) gained a fast mode (`runFast`) that runs the opcode with the same spawn, wait, lock and condition code as the step mode (operands, advance and slot resolution go through `operands`, `advance` and `resolveSlot`; the atomics are `atomicStep`) and resumes the task the schedule picks, so the default and seeded schedules are unchanged. `prepareModule(module, functions, forTasks)` accepts the scheduler opcodes only for a run with tasks, a task's function may take parameters, and the dispatch table of the loop is filled once per process (the loop is `noinline`/`noclone`, since the table holds the addresses of one body). A run with a cancel flag, `PRIMEVM_KERNEL=step`, or a module the CFG analysis rejects keeps every task on the step kernel. Tests (tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_tasks.cpp): a counting test (`testing::vmFastTaskRunCount`, include/primec/testing/VmKernelSelection.h) shows a run with tasks is given to the flat loop once and not when the loop is off, both kernels agree on value and output for the default and seeds 1, 2 and 9 on two modules (one spawns and waits two frames deep with locals live across the switch and a write through the address of a caller's local), and faults read the same on both; the existing task, atomic, mutex and condition suites (37 cases) run on the flat loop. Measured on arm64 by `/usr/bin/time -l` (instructions retired, the `primec --emit=vm` compile step included, about 2.0e9 of each), a loop of 200000 `String`s (a 3-byte text and four `append`s, 77 bytes) in a spawned task: 87.8e9 before (`PRIMEVM_KERNEL=step` is the old path), 8.22e9 after, against 8.16e9 for the same loop in a program without tasks, so the task costs 1.01x the loop without tasks (acceptance: at most 2x); at 20000 rounds 10.37e9 before and 2.62e9 after against 2.62e9 without tasks.

- [x] TODO-5872: A thread reads the bytes of a block another thread allocated as fast as its own
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/spec/vm-design.md, heap arenas; found measuring `serveWorkers`)
  - parallel_track: mt-heap
  - scope: On `optexe` a byte load or store checks its address against the calling thread's arena in line (`byteAt` in include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc); an address of another thread's arena misses that check and goes through `byteAtEdge`, the out-of-line `byteAtSlow`, `ownerOf` and the owner's `byteAtOwn` for every byte. Measured with benchmarks/http: a `serveWorkers` worker that parsed a 32 KB form in the slot block the polling thread allocated spent 327 us of user time per request against 146 us for `serve`; parsing from a copy in a block of its own brought it to 160 us, which is what `work_slot` in stdlib/std/http/server.prime now does. Make the check of a remote byte region cheap (for example one more in-line compare against the last remote arena that answered), so shared read-only data needs no copy, and then drop the copy in `work_slot` if it no longer pays.
  - acceptance:
    - an `optexe` program in which a task sums the bytes of a 1 MiB `String` the main task built retires at most 1.2x the instructions of the main task summing it itself (measured by hand, recorded in the result note)
    - benchmarks/strings instruction counts do not rise by more than 1%
    - no gate test measures time; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: byte-region checks of another arena's addresses on `optexe`; slot regions and the VM are not included.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: A byte of another arena's block missed the in-line check of `VmHeapCore::byteAt` (its offset lies outside this arena's granule range) and went through `byteAtEdge` to the out-of-line `byteAtSlow`, `ownerOf` (an atomic table load) and the owner's `byteAtOwn` for every byte. Fix (include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc): a heap remembers the last other arena whose bytes it read (`remoteOwner_`, one relaxed-atomic pointer, set in `byteAtSlow`; an arena's storage is reserved once and lives as long as the arenas, so its offsets, bounds and storage never change, and one pointer cannot tear when threads share the last arena), and `byteAt` answers a granule of that arena which its region fills with the same one load and compare as for its own arena, after the own check fails. A granule a region only partly fills, a freed or stale address and the first read of an arena still take the slow path, which is exact. `slowByteReads()` counts slow-path accesses. Test (tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_heap_arenas.cpp): another thread reads all 100000 bytes of a block the main thread allocated and takes the slow path at most 129 times (the two edge granules and the first read; it was once per byte), reads one past the end as no byte, and reads the block as no byte after the owner freed it. Measured with `optexe` on arm64 (instructions retired of the program, a task summing a 1 MiB `String` the main task built, 16 passes, against the main task summing it): 3.8655e9 against 3.0367e9 before (1.27x), 3.6499e9 against 3.0586e9 after (1.19x; acceptance 1.2x); a task summing a `String` it built itself costs 3.107e9, so a remote byte still costs about 17% more than an own one (a second compare, the remote's base, bound and storage loads). `benchmarks/strings` on `optexe`, instructions before -> after (run-to-run noise of one binary is about 0.5%): short_strings 4.653e9 -> 4.661e9, request_heap 5.370e9 -> 5.369e9, append_chunks 1.2518e9 (three runs 1.2460 to 1.2572) -> 1.2611e9 (+0.75%), request_arena 5.518e9 -> 5.516e9, copy_text 664.4e6 -> 661.6e6, append_bytes 2.891e9 -> 2.908e9 (+0.6%). The copy in `work_slot` (stdlib/std/http/server.prime) stays: with the machine at a load average of 12 to 46 on 11 processors an `serveWorkers` run cannot show the difference between parsing the poller's block (about 1.17x the instructions per byte of an own block) and copying it first (one memcpy of the request), so dropping it is not claimed.

- [x] TODO-5871: `serveWorkers` answers more new connections a second than one thread can accept
  - owner: ai

  - parallel_track: mt-server

The 32 KB form with 4 workers (13,329, 2.41x `serve`) sits at nine tenths of that ceiling, which is why it misses 2.5x: 3 workers reach 12,585 and 4 only 13,167. What sets the ceiling was not measured (no sampling of the threads): the one thread that polls, accepts one connection per round and hands it over, the kernel's loopback connection setup, or the Python load generator. Measure which (per-thread CPU of the poller, or a load generator that keeps connections open against a server that allows it, TODO-5805), then raise it if it is the server's: accept in more than one thread, or hand over more than one connection per round (tried once here with no gain at this ceiling).

    - the measured cause of the ceiling is recorded in docs/WebAppsPlan.md (Measured)
    - if the cause is in `serveWorkers`: `python3 benchmarks/http/run_http_benchmarks.py` on an idle machine with at least 6 processors shows the 32 KB form at least 2.5x `serve` with 4 workers, and the table in docs/WebAppsPlan.md is replaced; if it is the load generator or the kernel, the target is restated against what the setup can show
    - no gate test measures time; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the connection-rate ceiling of `serveWorkers`; the list page waits for read-only handlers (TODO-5804).
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Measured, not changed: the ceiling is the load generator and the kernel's loopback connection setup, not `serveWorkers`, so there is nothing in the server to raise and no code changed. A reference server in C (scratch only, not committed: one blocking `accept`, one `recv` until the end of the headers, a fixed 2-byte response, `close`, 1 or 4 threads; no PrimeStruct code) was run against benchmarks/http's generator (scripts/http_load.py, 16 clients, a new connection per request, 5 s per run) on the 11-processor arm64 machine at a load average of 27 to 64 (other work was running, so only the comparison counts): 1 thread 10,299, 11,923 and 11,444 requests per second, 4 threads 11,426 and 11,255, and a PrimeStruct `serve` on `POST /form` of 8 bytes 9,372 in the same minutes. A server that spends 25 to 32 us of CPU per request (user and system, `getrusage` of its process) is held to the same rate as one that spends 130 us, and more accepting threads (the C server with 4, `serveWorkers` with 1 to 4 workers) do not move it. The generator costs about 200 us of CPU per request (71 us user, the rest system time of its 16 client processes in `connect`, `send` and `recv`). Recorded in docs/WebAppsPlan.md (Measured). Restated target: the form's 2.41x with 4 workers (13,329 requests per second at nine tenths of the ceiling) is what this generator can show; a 2.5x reading needs 13,900 requests per second, above what it shows for any server, so the 2.5x claim moves to TODO-5940 (a generator that costs less per connection). Not measured: the poller thread's own CPU (a sampling profile of the threads would say whether one accepting thread would limit a faster generator).

- [x] TODO-5840: A byte loop over one large region on `optexe` runs as fast as before the granule table
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-10
  - phase: Optimizing backends (found in TODO-5793)
  - parallel_track: optexe-bytes
  - scope: TODO-5793 replaced `VmHeapCore`'s last-region cache (three compares against members, but written on every miss) with a per-granule state table (one dependent load and compare, no write). On `optexe` `benchmarks/strings/append_chunks.prime` (43-byte appends into one String growing to 8.6 MB, byte by byte through `ps_store_u8`) takes 10% more CPU time (51.8 ms against 56.9 ms, median of 31 interleaved runs); every other string benchmark is within 4% and two_region_copy is 13% faster. With the check removed entirely both versions are within 2%, so the cost is the check in the hot loop: the generated program calls `VmHeapCore::byteAt` out of line, and forcing it inline (fast path inline, map search out of line) made append_chunks 15-20% slower, not faster. Find where the time goes (instruction count of the String.append loop in the generated code, the inlining of `textStore`) and win it back without a write on the read path.
  - implementation_notes: include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc (`byteAt`, `byteAtEdge`), src/backend/IrToOptCppRuntime.h (`ps_load_u8`, `ps_store_u8`); measure with CPU time of interleaved runs (wall time on a shared machine varied by 50%).
  - acceptance:
    - `append_chunks` on `optexe` within 2% of the pre-TODO-5793 build; the other string benchmarks and two_region_copy no slower than now
    - no write on the byte read path; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the optexe byte check; VM changes only if the shared heap code needs them.
  - notes: TODO-5794 (per-thread heap arenas) left this open: it has no per-thread region cache (a state-table read needs none), and append_chunks runs 0.7% more instructions than before it. Measured there again: the byte check inlined into the byte loops costs 8% more instructions on short_strings, so `ps_byte_at` (src/backend/IrToOptCppRuntime.h) keeps it out of line. The cycles of the same source move by 15% with `-falign-functions`/`-falign-loops`, so compare instruction counts and several layouts, not one CPU time.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: Where the time went: `String.append(text)` copied a literal one byte at a time (`textStore(this.data, this.fieldLength + i, convert<u8>(at(text, i)))`), about 145 instructions per byte on `optexe`, so the benchmark spent its time in a per-byte loop and the byte check was a tenth of it. Instead of shaving the check, the loop is gone: `append` (stdlib/std/text/string.prime) now makes one `__pstext_move` of `count` bytes from `__pstext_literal(text)`, the address of the literal's bytes (a byte region the heap copies once per literal and thread heap, both host functions already exist on the VM and `optexe`), so a literal costs one range check per call, not one per byte. No write was added to the byte read path (the check is unchanged). `replace` keeps its loop: for a few bytes the two host calls cost more than the loop (`insert_front` 70.4e6 -> 82.3e6 instructions with the bulk form). Tests (tests/unit/language/test_string_owned.cpp): appends of empty, 1-byte, 84-byte and 4-byte literals across block growth and 300 rounds of two appends (3300 bytes, byte sum checked) keep every byte in place; a structural test compiles a program that appends a literal, round-trips its bytecode and checks that no function holds `LoadStringByteDynamic` (the loop's instruction) and that the two bulk host calls are there. Measured with `optexe` on arm64 by `proc_pid_rusage`/`/usr/bin/time -l` (machine at a load average of 27 to 64 on 11 processors; instructions are exact, cycles move by 3 to 5% between runs), before -> after: `append_chunks` 1.26e9 instructions and 234e6 cycles -> 0.35e9 and 93e6 (the pre-granule-table build ran about 10% fewer cycles than the build before this change, so this is far inside the 2% acceptance), `short_strings` 4.66e9 and 823e6 -> 3.90e9 and 748e6, `request_arena` 5.54e9 and 1115e6 -> 5.14e9 and 1039e6, `request_heap` 5.37e9 and 1073e6 (minimum of three) -> 5.02e9 and 1049e6, `copy_text` 663.8e6 -> 662.2e6 instructions, `append_bytes` 2.903e9 -> 2.905e9, `two_region_copy` 804.1e6 -> 803.8e6, `replace_middle` 196.5e6 -> 197.0e6 and `insert_front` 71.3e6 -> 70.8e6 instructions (the loop stays). The residual, a `pushByte` or `textStore` loop whose every byte goes through the byte check, is unchanged: TODO-5938.

- [x] TODO-5952: arm64 native text blocks and 16 KiB blocks come from the pool
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Native allocator (found while closing the arm64 native threads TODOs)
  - parallel_track: mt-native
  - scope: On arm64 native a `String` or a `vector` literal created and dropped in a loop cost one page reclaim (about 1.4 us of system time) per iteration: `emitTextAlloc` mapped every text block with its own `mmap` (and `HeapFree` unmapped it), and a vector literal allocates 1025 slots (`kVectorLocalDynamicCapacityLimit`), above the pool's 512-slot limit, so it was mapped and unmapped each time. Text blocks take the pooled heap (their header keeps the VM block size, so `capacity()` is unchanged and a free rounds the size up to whole slots), and the pool takes blocks up to 2048 slots (32 KiB, 39 size classes).
  - acceptance:
    - a loop of 30000 `String` appends and 1025-slot allocations costs a few hundred page reclaims, not 30000 or more (a counting test, not wall time)
    - `capacity()` of a native `String` equals the VM's
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the arm64 native allocator; x86_64 native still maps every block.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-11
  - result: 1.6M `String` iterations 3.73 s (2.72 s system) to 0.32 s (0.00 s system), page reclaims 1,600,274 to 277; 1.2M `vector<i64>` iterations 2.82 s (2.03 s system) to 1.15 s (0.01 s system), 1,200,279 reclaims to 300 (the rest is zeroing the 16 KiB block on reuse).

  - scope: A definition with a `string` (module-table text) parameter stayed inline, because the inline binding records where the text comes from (`stringSource`) and the body indexes it statically. The VM and optcpp (which read a module string by a computed index) now take a `string` parameter on the address ABI when the body uses it only as `count()` or as the argument of `__pstext_literal` (`RealCallShapeContext::allowStringParams`): the call site's inline binding already stores the string's table index in the parameter local, the call passes it, and the body binds it as a runtime string (`StringSource::RuntimeIndex`). A body that indexes, compares, prints or forwards the parameter stays inline, since a runtime string expands to a branch per table string. Native keeps them inline (no dynamic string reads). `String.append` is the real call.

- [x] TODO-5953: `String.append` of a literal does not cost more as a real call on optexe
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-12
  - phase: Optimizing backends (found while finishing TODO-5741)
  - parallel_track: ir-real-calls
  - scope: TODO-5741 made `String.append([string] text)` a real call on the VM and optcpp: the length of `text` is read from the string table at run time and the bytes move with a general `__pstext_literal` move, where an inlined call knew both as constants. Measured with `scripts/benchmark_strings.py` workloads under `--emit=optexe` (instructions retired, 3 runs each, 33c23d4c3 against 721d535bf): `strings/append_chunks` 346.5e6 to 369.7e6 (+6.7%), `strings/append_bytes` 2,895e6 to 3,009e6 (+3.9%); the suite of `scripts/benchmark.sh` and native are within noise (+-2%). Get the cost back without losing todo_web's size (`--emit=optcpp` 1,849,712 to 1,668,906 bytes): for example emit the call with the literal's length as a second scalar argument so the callee skips the table lookup, or keep a call site inline when its argument is a literal of a few bytes inside a loop, and measure both.
  - acceptance:
    - `strings/append_chunks` and `strings/append_bytes` on optexe are within 2% of 33c23d4c3 and todo_web's optcpp output stays below 1.7 MB
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the call of a `string` parameter on the VM and optcpp only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: the +3.9% of append_bytes was not append at all. Making String.append a real call gave String.growFor a third C++ call site, so clang stopped inlining it into the pushByte byte loop (a call per byte); append_chunks paid the call of append plus ps_text_call, which compares the host function name against 19 names before reaching __pstext_move. Fix: String.growFor is one statement that is inlined into every caller (the grow check against capacity), the rest moved to growTo; optcpp/optexe emit __pstext_move as a direct ps_text_move call. Measured on optexe, instructions retired (3 runs), 33c23d4c3-equivalent (string parameters off) against now: strings/append_chunks 348.1e6 to 333.3e6 (-4.2%), strings/append_bytes 2,897e6 to 2,741e6 (-5.4%); the 721d535bf state was 368.8e6 and 3,014e6. todo_web --emit=optcpp 1,564,475 bytes (below 1.7 MB). Test: a bulk move past its region stops an optexe program and the C++ calls ps_text_move (test_string_conformance.cpp). Full release gate green.

- [x] TODO-5745: A labeled value that is a call parses in every position
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-08
  - phase: Language gaps found by native UI (TODO-5710)
  - parallel_track: parser-labeled-values
  - scope: Three shapes fail to parse although their parts parse alone. A labeled brace argument whose value is a call followed by an operator: `Pair{[a] five() + 1i32}` fails with "invalid character: '+'" (`Pair{[a] 4i32 + x}` parses). An assignment whose right side is a brace construction with a call as a labeled value: `window = Win{[handle] h()}` fails with "unexpected token in expression" at `=` (`[Win] w{Win{[handle] h()}}` and `p = Pair{[a] 2i32}` parse). An assignment whose right side passes a lambda whose body starts with a binding: `a = apply([]([i32] x) { [i32] y{x} ... })` fails the same way (a call statement or a binding initializer with that lambda parses). handlers.prime and the editor bind a local first.
  - acceptance:
    - the three shapes parse and run on the VM, with a parser test each
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the parser's labeled-value and assignment paths only.
  - findings: Measured 2026-11-12. None of the three is a parser bug: all three are the text filter. `applyPerEnvelopeFilterPass` (src/text_filter/TextFilterPipelineEnvelope.cpp) cuts the text into chunks around every envelope and rewrites operators per chunk, so an expression that contains an envelope never reaches `rewriteBinaryOperatorsWithPrecedence` whole. (1) `[a] five() + 1i32`: `scanEnvelopeAfterList` reads the label `[a]` plus `five()` as an execution envelope (`[transforms] name(args)`), so ` + 1i32}` is a chunk with no left operand and stays infix (`[a] x + 1i32`, `[a] a.b() + 1i32` and `[a] 1i32 + five()` are not envelopes and rewrite; `--dump-stage pre_ast` shows the difference). (2) `w = Win{[handle] h()}`: the same envelope splits the right side of the assignment from `w =`. (3) `a = apply([]([i32] x) { [i32] y{x} ... })`: a lambda is an envelope (`scanLambdaEnvelope`), so even `c = apply2([]([i32] x) { return(x) })` stays `c = ...` unrewritten (`a = 4i32` and `a = apply2(x)` become `assign`); a lambda in a call statement or a binding initializer needs no operator across the cut, which is why only the assignment and operator cases fail. The fix is in `findNextTransformListStart`/`findNextEnvelopeStart`: do not start an envelope for an argument label (`[ident]` directly in the braces of a `Type{...}` construction or the parentheses of a call, followed by a value and no `{` body) or for a lambda that sits inside the parentheses of a call. Not done in this pass: the change moves chunk boundaries for every program, needs its own pre_ast comparison over the stdlib and examples, and the gate budget of the pass was spent.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: the text filter cut the text at an argument label before a call and at a lambda inside call parentheses, so an operator or an assignment around them was never rewritten as one expression. Fix: findNextTransformListStart and findNextEnvelopeStart keep a single-identifier label in construction braces or call parentheses, and (where the lambda takes the active filters) a lambda inside call parentheses, in the call's text. The pre_ast of the 166 stdlib, example, benchmark and fixture files is unchanged.

  - owner: ai
  - status: done
