  - parallel_track: native-backend-strings
  - scope: The arm64 native String heap gives every text block its own mapping (a page or more each, a syscall per allocation and free). Pool small blocks in 256 KiB chunks per size class as the VM's `VmTextHeap` does, with state in the writable data segment of TODO-5582, and answer `__pstext_stat` and `__pstext_set_limit` ("string memory limit exceeded"); freed blocks are zeroed and a double free faults.
  - acceptance:
    - the string_heap program of tests/unit/backend_host/test_cpp_strings.cpp (reuse and figures) also runs through `--emit=native` with the VM's exit codes; a 100000-String loop uses no more than a few MB; full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the native String heap's allocator and its statistics.
  - notes: deferred to keep Ready Now at eight. PrimeScroll ships from the native build, so every String it makes takes a mapping of its own; the writable data segment this needs exists (`MachOData::stateBytes`), and since TODO-5750 slot blocks are pooled there (src/native_emitter/NativeEmitterInternalsArm64Heap.h: chunks shared by all size classes, free lists in the data segment), which text blocks could share. After TODO-5749 the text blocks are most of what native PrimeScroll on handlers still holds above its loop version (untagged dirty memory 0.41 MB in 11 regions against 0.28 MB in 5, of a 0.2 MB footprint gap).
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: The pooled blocks were already done (TODO-5952: text blocks come from the shared pool). Remaining: statistics and the limit. The native emitter now keeps six counters in the data segment's state (memory limit, bytes held by live text blocks, blocks handed out, live blocks above 64 KiB and their bytes, pool chunks mapped), updated with LSE adds by emitTextAlloc, emitTextFree and the heap's chunk mapping (NativeEmitterInternalsArm64Core.h, Heap.h), and only in a module that imports `__pstext_stat` or `__pstext_set_limit`. `__pstext_stat` answers 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 (arenas 6 and 7 read 0) and stops the program on the others; `__pstext_set_limit` sets the limit, over which `__pstext_try_alloc` answers null and `__pstext_alloc` stops with "string memory limit exceeded" (exit 3). Statistics match the VM (bytes in use, blocks, large blocks); the chunk count is the pool's. The string_heap program of test_cpp_strings.cpp runs natively with the VM's exit code, a 100000-String loop peaks at 1.2 MB, and three native tests cover the figures, the limit (try and fault) and an unsupported statistic. Not done: arenas and statistics 2 and 8 (TODO-5956).

  - owner: ai

Full release gate green.

    - negative: a block expression whose value is a local of an outer scope leaves that local usable

  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: a block expression's last value that is a local the block declared was loaded while the local kept its drop flag, so the block's scope destroyed it and the binding outside, which took the slots over as a temporary, destroyed it again (`string heap block freed twice`); as a call argument it was also not recognized as an owned temporary, and semantics inferred no struct type for it (`expected String got array`). Fix: the block expression emission releases the drop flag of such a local (IrLowererOperatorConversionsAndCallsControlHelpers.cpp), isOwnedTemporaryArgumentExpr treats a block that yields one of its own locals as an owned temporary, shouldDisarmStructCopySourceExpr copies instead of taking over when the block yields a local of an outer scope, a field or an element (the negative case: the outer local stays usable), and inferStructReturnPath reads the struct a block yields with the block's bindings in scope. Tests: vector_owners matrix case (VM and optexe, heap and string heap unchanged) for both bindings of the TODO, the argument form, a return form and an outer-local value, and semantics tests for the accepted and the mismatching block argument. A block that yields a vector (`[vector<i32>] v{block() { [vector<i32>] x{...} x }}`) is rejected earlier with `binding not allowed in expression context`, which this change does not touch. Full release gate green.

  - parallel_track: method-overloads
  - scope: docs/spec/language-core.md (Helper overloading) lets struct methods overload by parameter type, but a same-arity family declared in a struct body does not resolve. `evaluateRequirementOverloadViability` (src/semantics/TemplateMonomorphCoreUtilities.cpp) pairs the method's parameters, which have no implicit `this` yet, with the call's arguments, which start with the receiver, so `box.add("a", 3i32)` beside `add([string], [Tag])` is `no viable overload`; the struct-method path of `resolveMethodCallTemplateTarget` (src/semantics/TemplateMonomorphMethodTargets.cpp) passes no locals to `selectHelperOverloadPath`, so a struct-typed local is `unknown` and both candidates stay viable (`ambiguous`); a call argument is `unknown` too (as in TODO-5716), so `Menu.item([string], [string], [Command])` beside `item(..., [i32])` breaks the editor's `item(title, shortcut, command_save())`; and in a generic struct, `holder.on(tag, lambda)` with `on([Tag], [Function<...>])` beside `on([Other], [Function<...>])` is `unknown method: /Holder__t.../on`, and the lambda does not convert to the `Function` parameter. Skipping one argument when `expr.isMethodCall` and the call has one argument more than the method has parameters, and passing `&locals` at that `selectHelperOverloadPath`, resolved the non-generic local case in a trial. `/std/ui/native` uses separate names until then: `Menu.commandItem`, `Toolbar.commandButton`, `Menu.setCommandChecked`, `AppHandlers.onCheckBoxChange`, `onPopupChange`, `onListChange`.

    - same-arity struct method overloads resolve by a literal, a local, a parameter and a call with a declared return type, in a struct and in a generic struct, including a `Function` parameter given a lambda, on the VM and optexe; a no-viable and an ambiguous negative test
    - `Menu.item`, `Toolbar.button` and `AppHandlers.onChange` take a `Command` or a control as overloads, and the editor builds unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: overload selection of struct methods; no change to free-function overloads or to the specificity rule.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: three gaps in struct-method overload selection. (1) evaluateRequirementOverloadViability paired the method parameters (no implicit `this` yet) with the call arguments (which start with the receiver), so the first parameter met the receiver; a method call with one argument more than the method has parameters now skips the receiver. (2) The struct-method path of resolveMethodCallTemplateTarget passed no locals or parameters to selectHelperOverloadPath, so a local or parameter argument had no type; it passes them now. A call argument whose callee is one non-templated definition has its constructor or return<T> type. A path and a bare name of the same leaf match. (3) A generic struct had no overload families under its specialization: a call found no `/Holder__t.../on` ("unknown method"); each specialization now registers the families of its template. Menu.item, Toolbar.button, Menu.setChecked and AppHandlers.onChange are overloads on the command or control; the by-name spellings stay for a method-call argument (its type is not known to overload selection), and the editor builds unchanged. Tests: semantics struct_methods (no viable, ambiguous, positive) and program-matrix struct_methods (struct and generic struct, lambda to a Function parameter; VM, optexe, native); the native UI handlers scenario uses the overloads.

The module holds only templates, so with nothing instantiated the import check finds no definition under the path. An import of a module that exists is valid whether or not the program uses it.

Not traced further; the likely cause is that the import check runs after template monomorphization, which drops uninstantiated templates: check the path against the source definitions (the monomorph context's `sourceDefs`) or before the templates are dropped. Other template-only modules probably behave the same; test one.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the repro compiles and runs on the VM and `optexe`; a second template-only module imported and unused compiles too
    - negative: an import of a path no module defines is still `unknown import path`
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the import check for modules whose definitions are all templates; no change to lazy stdlib import.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: the import check runs after template monomorphization, which drops every template that nothing instantiated, so a wildcard import of a module that holds only templates (/std/tuple) found no definition under its path. Monomorphization now records the public templates it drops in Program::templateDefinitionPaths (sorted) and the check counts them as definitions of the module. An import of a path no module defines, and of a module whose templates are all private, is still an unknown import path. Tests: two semantics cases (user template-only module accepted, private-only rejected) and a program-matrix case importing /std/tuple/* and /std/maybe/* unused on the VM configs, optexe and native.

  - implementation_notes: the method target of `count` on the `Vector<T>` struct is published by the semantic method resolution (compare `--dump-stage semantic-product` for `grown.count()` and `grown.push(4i32)`); the mutating helpers of stdlib/std/collections/vector.prime are the rooted `/std/collections/vector/<name>` definitions at the end of the file.
  - findings (2026-11-11, tried and reverted): the rejection is deliberate and in three places. (1) src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprVectorHelpers.cpp rejects a bare or method mutator whose receiver classifies as the `Vector<T>` struct family (`unknown call target: <name>`); letting the method form through when `/std/collections/vector/<name>` is visible, plus adding the mutators to the `count`/`at` branch for that family in SemanticsValidatorExprMethodTargetResolutionGenericFallback.cpp, makes `push`, `pop`, `reserve` and `clear` run on the VM and `optexe` with the heap balanced. (2) `remove_at` and `remove_swap` are still rejected (`unknown call target: /std/collections/vector/remove_at`): they take the method branch of src/semantics/TemplateMonomorphExpressionRewritePhasesB.cpp, and exempting its `resolvesCollectionVectorValueReceiver` rejection the same way was not enough. (3) With (1), `push` on a `[Vector<i32>]` local without `mut` is accepted and changes it: the check of src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorMoveOnly.cpp (`push changes x, which is not mutable`) only knows the builtin `vector` base, and accepting the `Vector` base there did not fire. Do not land (1) without (3). tests/unit/semantics/calls_and_flow/test_semantics_calls_and_flow_collections_relocation_trivial_vector_elements.cpp (`canonical vector pop method requires visible canonical helper`) pins the rejection and turns positive. The explicit call `/std/collections/vector/push(grown, 4i32)` works today and checks `mut`. Also seen: `grown.at(0i32)` on such a local fails in lowering (`missing semantic-product method-call target: at`), while `grown[0i32]` works.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: `push`, `pop`, `reserve`, `clear`, `remove_at` and `remove_swap` as methods on a `[Vector<i32> mut]` local change it on the VM and `optexe`, heap statistics balanced
    - negative: `push` on a `[Vector<i32>]` local without `mut` is rejected
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: mutating method calls on bindings declared with the stdlib `Vector<T>` spelling.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: the method forms of the mutators were rejected for a receiver of the stdlib `Vector<T>` family in three places, by design of the earlier stdlib cutover. (1) The vector helper validation rejected `push`, `pop`, `reserve`, `clear`, `remove_at` and `remove_swap` as `unknown call target` for that family, and so did the template rewrite (`TemplateMonomorphExpressionRewritePhasesB`, the only place that rejected `remove_at` and `remove_swap`); both now let the method form through when the stdlib helper of that name is declared, and the bare call form `push(values, x)` stays rejected. (2) Method target resolution gave `count`, `capacity` and `at` a stdlib target for that family but not the mutators; it now does. (3) The mutability check (`push changes values, which is not mutable`) only knew the builtin `vector` base; it now knows the stdlib `Vector` specialization too, so a `[Vector<i32>]` local without `mut` is still rejected. Tests: semantics cases (the six methods validate on a `mut` local, rejection without `mut`, bare `push` still unknown, the old pop pin turned positive) and a vector_owners program-matrix case on the VM configs and optexe with balanced heap statistics. `grown.at(0i32)` on such a local lowers now. Found and filed: TODO-5978 (a `Vector<String>` leaks what `pop` and `clear` remove and faults after `remove_at`).

  - owner: ai

  - scope: `[n b] pair` and `[a b] wait(x, y)` are expanded only when they are statements of a definition's own body. Inside the block of an `if`, a loop or a lambda, `[n b] pair` fails with `duplicate binding name: pair` and `[a b] wait(x, y)` fails with `task handles cannot escape their spawning function: x` (or `unknown import path: /std/tuple/*`). Expand the destructuring statement in every statement list.
  - implementation_notes: found while fixing TODO-5849. The expansion is `makeTupleDestructuringBindingExpr` and its caller in src/semantics/TemplateMonomorphDefinitionRewrites.cpp, which walks `definition.statements` only; the split of a destructured multi-wait runs over the same list. Walk nested `bodyArguments` (blocks, loops, lambdas) the same way. The program-matrix case `a destructured multi-wait gives each binding its own result type` keeps its statements in a helper definition for this reason and can move them into a block once this is fixed.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: both forms inside an `if` block, a `for` body and a lambda body run on the VM (seeds 1 to 8 for the wait) and `optexe`, each name with its own element type, heap empty afterwards
    - negative: a name bound twice by one destructuring in a block is still a duplicate binding diagnostic
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: where the destructuring statement is expanded; no new destructuring forms.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-12
  - result: Root cause: `[n b] pair` and `[a b] wait(x, y)` were expanded only by rewriteDefinition, which walks `definition.statements`; the statements of an `if` block, a loop body or a lambda body went through rewriteExpr without that step, so a nested `[n b] pair` stayed a re-declaration (`duplicate binding name: pair`) and a nested multi-wait stayed an unsplit `wait` with a pattern. The expansion is now one function, expandDestructuringStatementAt (TemplateMonomorphDefinitionRewrites), called by the definition loop and by the two places that walk the statements of a block (rewriteExpr phase 8 for blocks and loops, and the lambda body); the hidden result tuples of multi-waits are numbered per definition by a counter in the monomorph context. A name bound twice by one destructuring in a block is still `duplicate tuple destructuring binding name`. Tests: a program-matrix case in the tasks suite with both forms in an `if` block, a `while` body and a lambda, each name with its own element type, heap empty afterwards, on the VM configs and seeds 1 to 8 and optexe, and a duplicate-name case. The language-core spec lists where a destructuring statement is expanded.

- [x] TODO-5992: A spawned call with a builtin `vector<T>` parameter or result runs as a task
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-16
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Runtime Model)
  - parallel_track: mt-vm-tasks
  - scope: the first slice of TODO-5847. A spawned call whose parameter or result was a builtin `vector<T>` ran inline with an `--opt-report` note. Give a vector parameter (borrowed, `copy`, `copy mut` or `move`) and a vector result a real call and lower the spawn to `TaskSpawn` through the task block.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: tasks that take a `vector<i32>`, `vector<String>` and `vector<Item>`, a `copy mut` and a `move` vector, and that return a `vector<String>` and a `vector<Item>` give the waiter the values on the VM (default schedule and seeds 1 to 8) and on `optexe`, the spawner's vectors unchanged, the heap balanced (heap statistics); `--opt-report` has no inline note for them
    - negative: a map parameter and a vector result that is not a `mut` local the task built keep their inline note
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: builtin `vector<T>` parameters and results of spawned calls; stdlib `Vector`, maps and owned sums stay in TODO-5847.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-16
  - result: A builtin vector is a pointer to a 5-slot record in the frame that made it plus a heap buffer, so a record cannot cross to another call stack. The spawner binds each vector argument in a hidden `mut` local of its scope (a copy of a name, a place or `move(name)`, or a fresh vector), copies the record into the task block and passes the block address; the hidden local's drop flag is off while the task runs (lent), or for a `copy`/`move` parameter for good, where the task's body owns the vector and destroys it (`registerRealCallOwnedParameters`). A vector result is returned by copying the returned local's record into the result block and giving up the buffer (`emitRealCallVectorReturn`), and the wait moves the record into a frame record of the waiter, whose binding owns it (`wait` of a task is a fresh vector, so `wait(t).count()` destroys the temporary too). Only a body whose every `return` names a `mut` vector local is taken (`vectorResultReturnsOwnedLocals`); a spawn whose vector argument is another expression stays inline. Tests: program-matrix tasks `a task takes and returns builtin vectors` (VM default and seeds 1 to 8, `optexe`, heap balanced; scalars, `String` and struct elements) and `a spawn that stays inline still returns its values`; optexe tasks `primec lowers a spawned call with String and struct values to a task` (notes for a map parameter and a non-local vector result).

- [x] TODO-5994: `wait(t).count()` of a stdlib `Vector` task result waits twice
  - owner: ai
  - created_at: 2026-11-16
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Runtime Model)
  - parallel_track: mt-vm-tasks
  - scope: Found with TODO-5993, which made a spawn whose result is a stdlib `Vector` a real task. `[i32] c{wait(w).count()}` on a `Task<Vector<i32>>` lowers `wait(w)` twice (the lowering copies the receiver into the callee's parameter record and then emits the argument expression again), so the VM stops with `task handle already waited` (and `optexe` faults the same way). The builtin `vector<T>` is handled by `isTaskVectorWait` (a hidden local that lives for the read); the stdlib struct has no such path, and `wait(t).get()` on a struct result is a semantic error (`task handle already waited`). Give the stdlib `Vector` and `Map` the same treatment: bind the waited struct to a hidden local that lives to the end of the statement, or diagnose a `wait` receiver that is not a binding at the semantic stage.
  - implementation_notes: src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerEmitExpr.h (the hidden-local read of a fresh builtin vector), `isTaskVectorWait` in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererReturnShapes.cpp, `validateTaskWaitExpr` in src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorTaskHandles.cpp. Repro: a `Task<Vector<i32>>` from a spawn of a function returning a `mut` `Vector<i32>` local, then `[i32] c{wait(w).count()}`; before TODO-5993 the spawn ran inline and the program printed the count.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: `wait(w).count()` and `wait(w)[i]` of a stdlib `Vector` task result give the value and leave the heap balanced on the VM (default schedule and seeds 1 to 8) and on `optexe`
    - negative: a second `wait` of the same handle stays a diagnostic
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: a method or index read of a waited stdlib `Vector` or `Map` result.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-16
  - result: Three causes. The collection receiver materializer emitted a vector-shaped receiver and only then gave up, so the ordinary call path emitted it a second time (the receiver ran twice, and a `wait` waited twice); it now decides before emitting. A method call validated its receiver for target resolution and again as the first argument, so the second look at one `wait` expression was reported as a second wait; the same source position is now one wait. A method call on an owning call result or a struct `wait` result read the receiver after the callee had destroyed its local (`make_values().count()` gave 0 and leaked); the receiver is now a hidden local that lives to the end of the statement and is destroyed there. Tests: program-matrix `a method call on a wait result waits once` (VM seeds 1 to 8, optexe, heap balanced) and two semantics cases (one wait as a method receiver, a second wait still rejected).

- [x] TODO-5841: `[namespace] name { ... }` is a definition
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-16
  - created_at: 2026-11-10
  - phase: AI workflow (docs/AiWorkflowPlan.md section 6.5)
  - parallel_track: namespace-envelope
  - scope: A definition body already works as a namespace: in `[return<void>] demo() { [return<i32>] one() { return(7i32) } }` the member is `/demo/one`, siblings call each other by bare name, `import /demo/*` works, and containers nest. But `/demo` is then a callable void function, it cannot be opened twice ("duplicate definition: /demo"), and `[namespace] demo() { ... }` fails with "expected transform identifier" because `namespace` is a keyword token. Add `namespace` as a definition transform: `[namespace] demo { ... }` (and `demo() { ... }`, a slash-path name, and a nested one) is a definition whose body holds only definitions. It takes no parameters, template list or `return`; a binding or statement in its body is a diagnostic; calling it or using it as a type is a diagnostic; its members get no implicit `this`. Definitions with `namespace` at one path are one namespace: the parser folds them into the first, in source order, with their transform lists joined. A `[namespace]` definition may share its path with a struct, enum or function (as `namespace P { ... }` next to `[struct] P` does today) only when its list is `namespace` alone. It lowers to nothing.
  - implementation_notes: `parseTransformList` must take the `KeywordNamespace` token as a transform name. Top-level definitions already accept a body without `()`; `tryParseNestedDefinition` (src/parser/ParserCoreDefinitionBodies.cpp) takes a nested `name { ... }` only for the `isNoReturnDefinitionTransform` names (struct-like and `sum`), so `namespace` joins that test. Members of a container are already flattened to slash paths with the container left as an empty definition (`--dump-stage ast`), so no AST type is added. Follow how field-less struct definitions are kept out of lowering. The keyword form (`Parser::parseNamespace`) is not touched here.
  - acceptance:
    - `[namespace] demo { ... }` with a function, a struct and a nested `[namespace]` runs on the VM; members resolve by path, by sibling bare name and through `import /demo/*`
    - two `[namespace] demo` blocks merge; `--dump-stage ast` shows one `[namespace] /demo` (golden test)
    - parameters, a template list, `return`, a statement in the body, a call of the namespace, and extra transforms on a path that is also a struct are diagnostics (one test each)
    - `--dump-stage ir-lowered` has no function for the namespace
    - docs/PrimeStruct_SyntaxSpec.md and docs/spec/transforms.md describe the transform with a runnable example
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the `namespace` transform only; the keyword form keeps its own parser path until TODO-5843, and no other transform gets a meaning for a namespace's members.
  - result: `namespace` is a definition transform. `parseTransformList` takes the keyword token as a transform name (`validateTransformName` allows it) and `namespace` joins `isNoReturnDefinitionTransform`, so `[namespace] demo { ... }`, `demo() { ... }`, slash paths and nested ones are definitions. The component `src/parser/ParserNamespaceDefinitions.{h,cpp}` holds the rules: `namespaceDefinitionShapeError` (no parameters, template list or `return`, only definitions in the body; run at the end of `parseDefinitionBody`) and `foldNamespaceDefinitions` (run once at the end of `Parser::parse`: blocks of one path fold into the first with transform lists joined, members stop being nested helpers so they get no implicit `this`, and a namespace sharing a path with another definition is dropped when its list is `namespace` alone and an error otherwise). The semantic predicates that read an empty untagged definition as a field-only struct (validator build, snapshot helpers, omitted-initializer and constructor passes, reflection and soa metadata, the template monomorphizer and the lowerer's struct test) treat `namespace` like a `return` transform, and a call of a namespace is `namespace is not callable: <path>` (src/semantics/SemanticsValidatorExprCallResolveRules.cpp); a type use falls out as an unsupported binding type. No semantic pass is added, so the pass manifest is unchanged. `--dump-stage ir-lowered` has no function for a namespace. Members are imported through `import /demo/*` only when `public`, as for any definition. Tests: tests/unit/compile_run/text_filters/test_compile_run_text_filters_namespace_definitions.cpp (VM run with function, struct, nested namespace and import, shared struct path, fold golden, no lowered function, one case per diagnostic). Docs: docs/PrimeStruct_SyntaxSpec.md section 3.3 and docs/spec/transforms.md. The keyword form is untouched.

  - phase: Result and control flow (found with the stdlib vector return fix)
  - parallel_track: vector-method-returns
  - scope: `isFreshBuiltinVectorExpr` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererFlowControlHelpers.cpp) returns false for every method call, so `[vector<i32>] v{maker.makeValues()}` gives the local no drop entry and leaks one slot-heap block per call (and a String block per element for `vector<String>`); a method-call temporary that is only read (`maker.makeValues().count()`) or discarded (`maker.makeValues()`) leaks too, as does a method result passed on through a Reference receiver. Measured with `heapLiveBlocks()` and `stringHeapBytesInUse()` on vm-O2 and optexe. Resolve a method call to its definition with the same resolver the free-function path uses and apply one shared rule: a callee declared `return<vector<T>>` hands over a vector of its own, whether a user method or a stdlib struct method (`StringView.splitOwned`); a method returning `Reference<vector<T>>` hands out a place and is not destroyed.

    - a method returning `Reference<vector<i32>>` leaves the field intact on every backend
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: builtin vector results of method calls only; no change to String or struct results.
  - notes: Same predicate as the free-function path; do not add a second copy of the rule.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - result: Method calls resolve through the receiver type in the fresh-vector predicate at every lowering site; a method result is freed as a local, temporary, discarded statement and argument; a Reference-returning method is not destroyed. Seven VM and optexe matrix cases.

- [x] TODO-6002: A method call on an element of a builtin vector of Strings frees the element twice
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: owner-fixes (worktree-agent-aae5f2ee5c789cf7f), 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by the build graph (stdlib/std/build/build.prime)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: Reported as "a by-value `vector<String>` parameter frees its strings twice (`string heap block freed twice`)". Reproduced 2026-11-17 on the VM and optexe in release, but the parameter is not the cause: with `import /std/collections/vector/*` (not `/std/collections/*`), `values[0i32].view().count()` on a `[vector<String>]` parameter or a plain `[vector<String> mut]` local binds the element to a hidden read-only struct binding whose drop flag is armed, so the shallow copy of the element is destroyed at the end of the statement and again by the vector. The lowerer's `isTemporaryStructCopySource` treats an element access as a temporary whenever the access resolves to a definition (meant for a user `at`), and the narrow import resolves `values[i]` to the stdlib `/std/collections/vector/at`, which `ownedTemporaryStructPath` already recognises as the builtin element place. Make the two agree through one shared predicate. Check the by-value parameter itself (a local, a field, a temporary as the argument) and the by-value forms that read an element and call a method on it.
  - implementation_notes: `src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerReturnEmitStage.cpp` (`isBuiltinVectorElementHelperCall`, `isTemporaryStructCopySource`), `src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererFlowControlHelpers.cpp` (`isTemporaryStructCopySourceExpr`). Tests go in a program matrix suite with heap and string-heap statistics.
  - acceptance:
    - the program matrix runs `values[i].view().count()`, `values[i].byteAt(0i32)` style reads and a by-value `vector<String>` parameter given a local, a field and a temporary, with `import /std/collections/vector/*` and with `import /std/collections/*`, on the VM and optexe, and ends with balanced heap and string-heap statistics
    - a negative case keeps a user-defined `at` returning a struct value treated as a temporary
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the element read of a builtin vector; the other defects of the build graph list have their own leaves.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - result: The by-value vector<String> parameter was not the cause. With only the vector module of the collections library imported, items[i] of a builtin vector is the stdlib at helper specialized for the element type (path plus __t<hash>); the element-access predicates know only the plain at name, so a method call on the element (values[i].view()) bound a shallow copy of the element to an armed hidden binding that was destroyed at the end of the statement and again by the vector, and an element passed to a struct parameter was disarmed (its strings emptied). Which receivers are builtin vectors is known only to the lowerer's locals, so the lowerer state now has isBuiltinVectorElementPlace (built on isBuiltinVectorElementHelperCall) and the temporary-argument, copy-source and inline struct-parameter decisions ask it before treating a call as a temporary; a stdlib Vector local's at still returns a copy that is destroyed. Program matrix suite element_receivers (4 cases, VM and optexe, balanced heap and string-heap statistics): local, by-value parameter given a local, a field and a temporary, the wide import, and a user at. Found while testing: a method named at that returns a String and is used as a receiver (bag.at(0i32).view()) leaks the returned String; not part of this leaf.

- [x] TODO-6005: A view of an indexed element dangles after the expression that made it
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: owner-fixes (worktree-agent-aae5f2ee5c789cf7f), 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by the build graph (stdlib/std/build/build.prime)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: `[StringView] a{values[i].view()}` and `nodes[i].id.view()` bind a view of an element; the element can change or move (a `push` that grows the vector) while the view is read. Decide with `docs/spec/strings-and-views.md` (slice and view lifetime, borrowed bindings): the binding is a borrow of `values` and a later `push` is already a `borrowed binding` diagnostic, or it is not diagnosed and must be. Diagnose where the language rule says a view must not outlive the statement for such receivers, otherwise fix it.
  - acceptance:
    - the rule is stated in `docs/spec/strings-and-views.md`; a negative test per diagnosed shape and a positive test per accepted shape, with balanced statistics for the accepted ones
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: views of vector elements and of their fields.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - result: Decided: a diagnostic, not a fix. The dangling view the build graph saw was the element copy of TODO-6002 (the view was made of a shallow copy that was destroyed at the end of the statement); that is fixed, so values[i].view() now views the element itself. What is left is the lifetime: the element can be destroyed by a pop, clear or assignment while the view is read. The slice-loan checker found the root of a view through field and method chains but stopped at an element read, so values[i].view() and nodes[i].id.view() were loans on nothing. Its place walk now follows element reads (v[i], at, at_unsafe, also as the specialized stdlib helper), so such a view is a loan on the vector until its last use: borrowed binding: values (root: values, sink: a). docs/spec/strings-and-views.md states the rule; test_string_owned has negative cases (clear, push, a field of an element) and a positive one (other elements read while the view lives, changes after its last use). The stdlib web and http routers stored a view of a route pattern (this.routes[index].pattern.view()) in a Request field through a named view; that is the existing escapes via field rule applied to a root that was now known, so they assign the view expression directly.

That is the ownership rule of `docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md` (a borrowed parameter cannot be stored); only the message is thin. Add the remedy to the message (take the parameter as `[T copy]` or `[T move]`) and state the rule where the diagnostic is listed.

  - result: Intended ownership rule, not a defect: a parameter without copy or move borrows the caller's value, so an owning one (a container, a type with Destroy, or one holding either) cannot be assigned, returned or moved (docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md, Parameter Passing); [Compiler] p assigned into a field is rejected and [Compiler copy] p is the way out. Only the message was thin. borrowedParameterEscapeMessage (SemanticsBorrowedParameterMessages) now builds both escape messages, via return and via assignment, and ends them with take it as [T copy] or [T move] to return it or keep it; the prefix tests still match. test_semantics_move checks both endings and that a move parameter may be stored. The spec names the remedy.

  - scope: A compile step's key is its compiler settings, the content hashes of the files `--emit-deps` listed for its last run, and the compiler version. The keys and the lists are kept in `ProjectRoot/.ps/cache/`, which is not committed. A step whose output exists and whose key and file hashes are unchanged is reported as up to date and not run.     - touching an imported file, changing a compiler setting, and deleting the output each re-run exactly the affected step
    - touching an unrelated file re-runs nothing
    - a build with the cache deleted gives byte-identical outputs
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: compile steps with file-hash keys; no interface-hash early cutoff (that comes with libraries, TODO-5929), no shared or remote cache.
  - resolution: `primec build` keeps `ProjectRoot/.ps/cache/<id>.cache` per step (hash scheme sha256 named in the file; key = compiler executable hash + step arguments; inputs = the `--emit-deps` list plus link-argument files, content-hashed; output hash recorded). Up-to-date steps print `up to date <id>`. Not covered: import-path shadowing, environment, and glob listings (TODO-5907 adds those as inputs when it lands).

  - parallel_track: build-glob
  - scope: `glob(base, pattern)` returns the paths under `base` that match, sorted bytewise: `*` (within a segment), `**` (any number of segments), `?`. A name that begins with a dot matches only a pattern segment that begins with a dot. Written in PrimeStruct over the listing of TODO-5906 (`listDirectory` of `/std/dir`) and the `/std/path` functions. The directory listings it read are what a build treats as inputs, so the function also returns them (or a second function does) for TODO-5915.
  - acceptance:
    - tests over a fixture tree for `*.prime`, `**/*.prime`, `?`, a dotted file, and no match
    - results are identical on the VM and with `--emit=optexe`
    - docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md documents it
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the three pattern forms; no bracket expressions, no negation.
  - notes: split on 2026-11-17. This leaf is the `glob` function in `/std/glob` (a module of its own, like `/std/dir`)
    that returns the matches and the directories it listed; TODO-6009 makes the build cache treat those directories as
    inputs.
  - resolution: `/std/glob` (stdlib/std/glob/glob.prime) gives `glob(base, pattern, matches, listed) -> Result<FileError>` over `listDirectory` and `join`; `matches` and `listed` are sorted bytewise and unique, and `listed` is the set of directories read, for TODO-6009. The tree is walked with an explicit task stack because the VM does not lower a recursive definition with vector parameters (TODO-6012); `vector<String>` is kept sorted by rebuilding it (TODO-6010, TODO-6011 are the defects found on the way). Entries of every kind match; a dotted name needs a dotted segment; `**` never enters a dotted directory; a bad pattern is EINVAL; a walk deeper than 64 is errno 40. Not covered: `b.files` and the cache inputs (TODO-6009), bracket expressions and negation, the native backends.

- [x] TODO-6009: A build step whose glob listing changes runs again
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Build system (docs/BuildSystemPlan.md, section 8)
  - parallel_track: build-glob
  - scope: A graph node may carry `inputDirs`, the directories its glob read (`Build.watch(id, dirs)`; written to the export only when non-empty). The cache entry of a step stores a hash of each such directory's listing (entry names and kinds, sorted); a step whose directory gained, lost or renamed an entry is not up to date. The listing hash is computed in C++ by the runner.
  - acceptance:
    - a graph with `inputDirs` exports them and `primec build` parses them
    - adding, removing and renaming a matched file re-runs the step; touching an unrelated directory does not
    - a missing watched directory is a change, not a crash
    - docs/spec/integration-and-tooling.md and docs/BuildSystemPlan.md state it
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: names and kinds of one directory level; no content hashing of matches (compile steps already hash what they read).
  - resolution: `Build.watch(targetId, dirs)` (stdlib/std/build/build.prime) stores the sorted, unique directories on the node; the export carries `inputDirs` only when there are any, and a watch of a missing target is a problem of the export. The runner parses them (`BuildStep.inputDirs`), the cache entry gets one `dir <hex> <path>` line each (sha256 of the one-level listing of names and kinds, `hashDirectoryListing` in src/pipeline/BuildCache.cpp, missing and unreadable are their own values), the entry is current only while every listing hash holds, and the sorted list of watched directories is part of the step key. `--profile build` now allows `/std/dir`, `/std/glob` and `/std/text` imports. Not covered: which entries matched (a non-matching new file in a watched directory also re-runs the step), file contents of matches (compile steps hash what they read), a glob inside a function step (TODO-5919).

- [x] TODO-6010: Shifting `vector<String>` elements with `items[at] = items[at - 1]` frees a string twice on the VM
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by glob (stdlib/std/glob/glob.prime; found while finishing TODO-5907)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: `insert_sorted([vector<String> mut] items, [String copy] item) { [i32 mut] slot{0i32}  items.push(item)  [i32 mut] at{items.count() - 1i32}  while(at > slot) { items[at] = items[at - 1i32]  at = at - 1i32 } }`, called six times with `stringFrom("hello world")` bound to a local, ends with `VM error: invalid string heap free address` (2026-11-17, release). The same loop with the assignment removed is clean, and `v[2i32] = v[1i32]` on a three-element vector of distinct literals is clean, so the fault needs the element-to-element assignment inside the loop on strings that were pushed as copies. Find which side drops or copies the slot twice. Workaround in glob: rebuild the vector with `push`.
  - acceptance:
    - a program matrix case that shifts the elements of a `vector<String>` up by one with an element-to-element assignment in a loop ends with balanced string-heap statistics on the VM and optexe
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: element assignment between two elements of one vector of a struct or `String`.
  - resolution: Not a double free in the shift: assigning to an element of a builtin vector of structs or Strings stepped by one slot instead of the element size and stored the source address into it, so the source element was read as moved and the target kept its old value. The `assign` of a vector element in IrLowererOperatorCollectionMutationHelpers.cpp now steps by the element slot count (from the local or from the field binding) and copies with ownership through `emitOwnedStructAssign` (place copied, temporary taken over, old element destroyed). Covered by the element_assign program matrix suite (shift loop with growth, place copy, self assign, scalar struct, vector field) with balanced heap and string-heap statistics on the VM and optexe. The glob workaround (rebuilding with push) is left in place.

- [x] TODO-6011: A name bound in one loop body and moved there is reported as moved in a sibling loop body
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by glob (stdlib/std/glob/glob.prime; found while finishing TODO-5907)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: Two `for` loops in one function each declare `[String] existing{items[i]}` and pass it to `merged.push(existing)`; the semantic pass reports `use-after-move: existing was moved at <line of the first loop>` on the second loop's use, although each binding is a new local of its own body. Moves should be tracked per binding, not per name in the function. Workaround in glob: distinct names per loop.
  - acceptance:
    - the two-loop shape compiles and runs; a use after a real move of the same binding is still a diagnostic
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: move tracking for same-named bindings in sibling scopes.
  - resolution: Moved state is now dropped when a binding goes out of scope: `LocalBindingScope` (SemanticsValidator.h) erases the names it inserted from `movedBindings` and `moveArgumentSites` along with the locals, so a same-named local of a sibling loop body or branch is a new binding. A real second use in the same scope is still `use-after-move`. Covered by "a name moved in one scope is a new binding in a sibling scope" (primestruct.semantics.move); docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md states it.

- [x] TODO-6012: A recursive definition with a vector or `Reference<vector<T>>` parameter does not lower on the VM
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by glob (stdlib/std/glob/glob.prime; found while finishing TODO-5907)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: `visit([StringView] base, [StringView] rel, [Reference<vector<DirEntry>>] entries, [Reference<vector<String>>] segments, ..., [vector<String> mut] matches)` that calls `walk`, which calls `visit` again, stops at lowering with `vm backend does not support recursive calls: /std/glob/visit` (2026-11-17). `isAddressAbiParameter` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererRecursionAnalysis.cpp) rejects a `Reference<vector<T>>` (the target text contains `<`) and a `StringView`-by-value mix, so the definition is inlined and the recursion is rejected. Either lower such definitions as real calls or make the diagnostic name the parameter that kept the definition inline. glob walks with an explicit stack instead.
  - acceptance:
    - a recursive definition with `[vector<i32> mut]` and `[Reference<vector<String>>]` parameters runs on the VM and optexe, or the diagnostic names the parameter and the rule
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the address-ABI parameter check for vectors and references to vectors.
  - resolution: Split: the recursion itself is judged too large for this leaf (the callee needs the element metadata of a vector parameter that a real-call body does not rebuild), filed as TODO-6015 with scope, acceptance and stop_rule. This leaf made the diagnostic name the cause: `realCallBlockerReason` (IrLowererRecursionAnalysis.cpp) returns the first parameter the address ABI does not take with its rule, and the recursion error appends it: `vm backend does not support recursive calls: /walk (it stays inline because parameter `out` is a `vector<i32>`: ...)`, and likewise for `Reference<vector<T>>`. Covered by the recursion program matrix suite; docs/spec/vm-design.md states the rule.

- [x] TODO-6014: A `primec build` spends 2.7 s compiling make.prime before it runs anything
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Build system (found while splitting the build_glob_cache tests, TODO-6013)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: `primec build` of a graph whose make.prime imports `/std/build/*` and builds one `ir` step takes 2.7 s of compile before the step runs (3.6 s with `/std/glob`, release, unloaded, 2026-11-17), and an up-to-date second run costs the same. Each build_glob_cache case needs two runs, so it takes about 7.7 s, above the 5 s doctest guardrail. Find where the time goes (import parsing, semantics of the build stdlib, lowering) and cut it, for example by making the build stdlib imports lazy or caching the compiled graph script.
  - acceptance:
    - an up-to-date `primec build` of a one-step graph takes 1 s or less in release, so every build_glob_cache CTest entry runs in 5 s or less
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the compile of make.prime; not the step runner.
  - findings: Measured 2026-11-17, release, one-step `ir` graph that imports `/std/build/*` (`primec build` runs `primec build --dry-run`, which compiles make.prime plus the appended `/std/build_runner/*` import, then runs it on the VM). Wall time of the compile (`--dump-stage`): parse and imports 0.04 s; semantic validation 0.5 s with 3,586 calls visited; semantic product 1.5 s cumulative (about 1.0 s of its own: `collectPilotRoutingSemanticProductFacts` re-infers 19,089 facts, a flat profile of method-target and path resolution with no single hot spot); lowering plus IR validation 1.1 s. A `sample` profile put 34% of the whole compile in `validateIrModule`, all of it in `validateNoOwnFrameAddressReturn` on `/std/build/Graph/export` (inlined to 33,737 instructions and 7,765 locals): the forward analysis copied a `vector<bool>` of locals per block and merged it bit by bit on every edge, 850 ms for that one function. Landed: (1) the frame-address and task-handle analyses keep the locals as 64-bit words (`LocalBits`), compile 2.64 s to 1.9 s; (2) the compiled script is cached (`BuildScriptCache`): an up-to-date `primec build` costs 0.21 s (hash of the compiler executable, load, VM run of the script, the step cache check) and `--dry-run` 0.13 s. Every build_glob_cache case now runs in at most about 5 s (the case that rewrites make.prime compiles twice) and the guardrail note is gone from the test source; the build_cache case with a deleted cache was split because it compiled three times. What a cache cannot fix is the 1.9 s of the first run of a script, TODO-6016.

(2) `inferQueryExprTypeText` inferred the receiver chain `a.b.c`, then `a.b`, then `a`, for every call that asks: inside the scope the type text of each sub-expression is memoized per expression and environment (`snapshotEnvironmentHash`, shared with the call snapshot memo). A fresh vector argument is still freed by the call site after the call. A `copy` or `move` vector stays inline at a direct call (TODO-6022 files it: the call site registers the copy's drop in its own scope, which a real-call body that owns the parameter would repeat). `primestruct.program_matrix.recursion` now holds four runnable programs (`mut` `vector<i32>` pushed past capacity through 20 levels, `Reference<vector<String>>`, a `vector<Named>` with `Destroy` plus a read-only `vector<Named>` summed recursively, a `mut` parameter replaced at each level), each with balanced `heapLiveBlocks` and `stringHeapBytesInUse` on `vm-step-O0`, `vm-O0`, `vm-O2` and `optexe-O2`; `vector_owners` gained a non-recursive case (a `mut`, a `Reference` and a read-only vector parameter with several call sites, and replacing a struct vector twice) and the existing `swap_place` and `swap_often` cases of that suite now run as real calls. Measured 2026-11-17 against the commit before: the glob program of `tests/unit/backend_host/test_glob.cpp` cut to ten cases, `--emit=optcpp`, 20,732 lines to 18,531 (`glob` and its vector-taking helpers are one function now); `tests/fixtures/build/build_graph.prime` 61,194 lines before and after (unchanged). `PrimeStruct_glob_optexe` 3.6 s to 3.1 to 3.8 s and `PrimeStruct_build_graph_optexe` 4.3 s to 4.1 to 4.25 s, three runs each, alone, in `PrimeStruct_cpp_host_call_tests`: within noise, since the C++ they compile barely changed (the build entries are dominated by TODO-6021, destruction repeated at every `return`).

- [x] TODO-6021: An early `return` repeats the destruction of every live local in optimized C++
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Build system (found by TODO-6020: the optexe build entries of the build graph and glob)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: The lowering expands the destruction of every live struct local at every `return` of a body, so a body that holds a `Graph` (a `vector<Node>` of nodes with `String` fields) and has seven `if(...) { return(n) }` checks holds eight copies of the destruction. Measured 2026-11-17 on `tests/fixtures/build/build_graph.prime` under `--emit=optcpp`: each such check added about 5,600 lines of C++ to `run_checks` (51,667 lines for the body; the host compiler took 5 s on the program), where the checks moved into a definition that owns no graph add a small fraction of that. The fixtures now work around it (TODO-6020), and `/std/glob` merged call sites for the same reason. Emit each live set's destruction once per scope (a shared cleanup block that the exits jump to, with the drop flags deciding what it destroys) in the IR lowerer, so the optimized backends, the VM and the arm64 backend all shrink; real calls already keep a callee's destruction in one place per exit.
  - acceptance:
    - the `run_checks` of the original `build_graph.prime` (graph and seven checks in one body, kept as a test fixture) lowers to under 15,000 lines of `--emit=optcpp` C++, and its output and heap statistics are unchanged on the VM and optexe
    - `--dump-stage ir` of programs with one `return` per body is unchanged; the dumps of programs with several exits differ only in the shared cleanup
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: destruction at early `return`; not `break`/`continue` exits and not real-call selection.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - evidence: A body with two or more `return` statements (counted syntactically) shares the destruction of its owning locals between its exits (`SharedReturnExits`, `src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererSharedReturnExits.cpp`; the hooks are `LowerReturnEmitStageState::emitSharedReturn` and `finishSharedReturnExits`, run by `emitEntryCallableExecutionWithCleanup`, which covers the entry and every real call). An exit whose live scope entries include a drop entry stores its value in a local of the body and jumps to a cleanup chain emitted once after the body: a trie over the live entries (last declared first), so exits with the same live prefix share the chain, and each node is the usual drop-flag-checked destruction of one entry; the drop flags still decide what runs, so each exit destroys exactly its live locals once, in the same order. Measured 2026-11-17 on `tests/fixtures/build/build_graph_one_body.prime` (the original one-body form, now a fixture): `run_checks` is 51,665 lines of `--emit=optcpp` C++ before and 10,967 after (the whole program 112,467 to 70,339 lines), the `--emit=vm` and optexe output equals the golden file and the heap and String heap checks (exit 0) pass on both. Unchanged by design: bodies with one `return`, exits with no drop entry live (file handles only, or nothing: `fib`-shaped bodies keep a direct return), inlined callees (they already jump to the call's exit), `break`/`continue` and the `?` exit; `--dump-stage ir` is the AST-level dump and does not change at all, and `ir-lowered` of one-return bodies is unchanged. Found while landing it: a `pick` statement lowered its arms in the enclosing scope, so the drop flag of an arm's local was read at exits and scope ends that never ran the arm, an uninitialized read on the arm64 native backend (frames are not zeroed): the old IR did it too, and only the stale stack values changed with the shared exits, which crashed `pick_return_owned_values` on native. Each arm of a `pick` statement is now its own scope: its owning locals are destroyed where the arm ends (an arm that ends in a `return` has left through its exit), so the `ir-lowered` IR of a `pick` statement whose arms hold owning locals changes (the destruction moves from the end of the enclosing scope to the end of the arm; arms without locals and all other programs are unchanged: 36 of 36 example programs compared byte-identical). The value form is TODO-6023. Tests: the `early_returns` program matrix suite (live sets at each exit, a loop with a return inside, nested scopes, a moved-from local, a void body, `String` and `vector<String>` locals, `Maybe` and `Result` returned early; heap and String heap balanced on the VM and optexe, and a native case) and three `build_graph` cases for the one-body fixture (VM golden, optcpp line count under 15,000, optexe golden with the heap checks).

- [x] TODO-6023: The arms of a value `pick` leave their owning locals in the enclosing scope
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Language defects found by TODO-6021 (shared exits of early `return`)
  - parallel_track: build-graph-defects
  - scope: A `pick` statement lowers each arm as a scope of its own since TODO-6021 (`SumHelpersContext`, `src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickAndDiagnostics.cpp`, the statement form), but the value form (`name = pick(...) { ... }`, `return(pick(...) { ... })`, the arms of `emitPickArmPrefixStatements`) still emits an arm's bindings into the enclosing scope. The drop flag of an arm's owning local is set only when that arm runs, so a cleanup of the enclosing scope (its end, or an exit of a later arm or of the body) reads the flag of an arm that never ran: zero on the VM (frames are zeroed) and stale stack memory on the arm64 native backend, which does not zero a frame (the symptom that TODO-6021 hit in `pick_returns`: a segmentation fault in `pick_return_owned_values` on native). Give each value arm its own scope too: the arm's value is computed first, the value a local ends the arm with is taken over (`releasedDropFlagLocal`), and the rest of the arm's locals are destroyed before the jump to the end of the `pick`. Write the failing program first (an owning `String` or struct local in a value arm, a body that returns after the `pick`, run on native).
  - acceptance:
    - a program with owning locals in the arms of a value `pick` runs on the VM, optexe and native with the same output and balanced heap statistics (VM and optexe), the locals destroyed where their arm ends
    - the arm-local value that ends the arm is still taken over, not copied or destroyed twice
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: value-form `pick` arms; not the statement form and not `match`.
  - notes: Done 2026-11-17. Each value arm is a file scope (pushFileScope/emitFileScopeCleanup), after the value is computed or copied into the result block and the local the arm ends with has its drop flag cleared; `tryEmitPickStatement` moved to IrLowererLowerSumHelpersPickStatement.cpp to stay under the file cap. Matrix suite `pick_value_arms` (4 cases, native included). The vector unit-arm shape found on the way is TODO-6024.

- [x] TODO-5896: `--vm-threads` runs each spawned task on its own OS thread
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: VM threads (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, VM Threads)
  - parallel_track: vm-threads
  - scope: The VM runs every task on one OS thread under `VmTaskScheduler` (src/runtime/VmExecutionKernel.cpp). Add a threads mode behind `--vm-threads` (`primevm` and `primec --emit=vm`; the default does not change): `TaskSpawn` starts a pthread with an 8 MiB stack as `optexe` does (`OptCppTaskRuntime`, src/backend/IrToOptCppRuntime.h); the VM allocates through `VmHeapArenas` (include/primec/runtime/VmHeapArenas.h), one arena per thread and arena 0 for the main task; handles and `TaskWait` follow docs/spec/vm-design.md, Tasks and Tasks on threads (a table of slots with generations behind one mutex). Every host call takes one global lock, and a print is one write, so lines never mix. A fault or `Trap` on any task flushes and leaves with exit code 3 the way `optexe` does; the embed API does not offer the mode until TODO-5899. A module that holds Atomic, Mutex or Channel opcodes is rejected in this mode with `--vm-threads does not support atomics, mutexes or channels yet` until TODO-5897.
  - implementation_notes: the step function `stepImpl` already runs one call stack; a task needs its own frames, operand stack and local counts (see `VmTaskScheduler::Task`). The heap functions of src/runtime/VmHeapHelpers.cpp (`vm_detail::storeHeapByte` and the others) take the one `heap_`; how many places assume a single heap was not counted.
  - acceptance:
    - a program that spawns four tasks of scalar callees prints the same output as under the default schedule, in a test that runs it 20 times
    - in this mode a block a task allocates carries a non-zero arena number (address bits 41 to 46); a single-task program's addresses are identical to today's (golden test)
    - a `String` or vector a task returns is freed by the waiter (a block freed by a thread other than its owner, no fault)
    - a module with atomic, mutex or channel opcodes gets the diagnostic above; without the flag every existing task test is unchanged
    - the wall time of a CPU-bound four-task program in this mode and by default is recorded in docs/todo_log.md (measured, not asserted by a test)
    - docs/spec/vm-design.md, Tasks, describes the mode
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: spawn, wait, heaps and the one host lock only; no sync primitives, no host-call refinement, no fast kernel, no default change.
  - notes: Done 2026-11-17. `Vm::setTaskThreads` / `--vm-threads` (primevm, `primec --emit=vm`) route a module with tasks to `VmThreadedTasks` (src/runtime/VmThreadedTasks.cpp): detached pthreads with 8 MiB stacks run the step kernel; the main task runs on the calling thread; slots with generations, results and the stop flag sit behind one mutex and condition variable. `RuntimeVmKernelHost` (src/runtime/VmExecution.cpp) allocates through `VmHeapArenas` with a thread-local arena binding (arena 0 for the main task, so single-task addresses are unchanged), and takes one host lock around prints, file operations and embedder host functions (not the VM's own `__pstext_*` functions, which use the calling thread's string heap). Deviation from the leaf text: a fault or Trap does not `_Exit`; it sets a stop flag that every task polls every 256 steps and that wakes waiters, the run joins every thread and returns the first outcome, so the process survives (most of TODO-5899; what remains there is the embed API and its cancel test). A wait that wakes after the run ended (a trap in the awaited task) does not return the result. The mode ignores the schedule seed and skips the native JIT. Atomic, mutex and condition opcodes are refused for any module in this mode. Tests: tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_threads.cpp (12 cases, each loop 20 times; the focused entry PrimeStruct_vm_threads ran 50 times in a row with no failure) and the `vm-O2-threads` config of the tasks program matrix (String, vector, Map, struct and closure tasks pass unchanged except the Atomic case, which is skipped until TODO-5897). Wall time of four tasks that each sum 10^8 integers (`while` loop of i64 adds): default schedule 1.14 s (flat loop), `--vm-threads` 12.5 s real and 46.3 s user, that is about 3.7 times parallel but each task about 10 times slower than the flat loop because threads mode uses the step kernel; TODO-5902 (fast kernel per task) is what closes that. Not found: a defect needing its own leaf, except that a program with thousands of live tasks is bounded by the operating system's thread limit (documented in docs/spec/vm-design.md).

- [x] TODO-5901: A threaded VM run records its synchronization order and replays it on the deterministic scheduler
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: VM threads (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, VM Threads)
  - parallel_track: vm-threads
  - scope: `--vm-record-sync <path>` writes, for a `--vm-threads` run, the order of the synchronization events across tasks (spawn, wait, lock, unlock, notify, every atomic operation, channel operations). `--vm-replay-sync <path>` runs the program on the deterministic scheduler following that order, so a run that was threaded can be repeated, stepped and inspected. Host input and output are not recorded; a program that reads from the outside is replayed only if the host calls return the same bytes.
  - acceptance:
    - a program with a mutex and a channel, run 20 times in threads mode with a record each, replays each record to the same stdout
    - a record from a different program or a changed program is refused with a diagnostic
    - the log format is versioned and documented in docs/spec/vm-design.md
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: record and replay of synchronization order; no per-instruction trace, no inspector work.
  - notes: Done 2026-11-17. `--vm-record-sync <path>` (needs `--vm-threads`) and `--vm-replay-sync <path>` (deterministic scheduler; no `--vm-threads`, no record, the seed is ignored) on primevm and primec; `Vm::setSyncRecordPath`/`setSyncReplayPath` and `RunOptions::syncRecord`/`syncReplay` for embedders. Format (version 1, little-endian, 24-byte header with the magic `PSSYNCLG`, the version and an FNV-1a fingerprint of the serialized IR; 8-byte event records of task number and kind; a trailer with the count), the ordering point (one record mutex: lock events after the take, unlock events before the release, condition and spawn events under the run's mutex, atomic operations under the record mutex across the operation) and the replay rules are in docs/spec/vm-design.md, Synchronization record and replay. Code: `src/runtime/VmSyncLog.{h,cpp}` (recorder, reader, fingerprint), the hooks in `VmThreadedSync.cpp` and `VmThreadedTasks.cpp` (a null-pointer test each when not recording), and the replay in `VmTaskScheduler.cpp` (`replayGate` parks a task that reaches a scheduler opcode out of turn, `completeReplayEvent` advances the record and releases the task whose turn it is; works on the flat loop and the step kernel). `Channel<T>` operations are the lock, condition and atomic events they are made of. Flag parsing moved to `src/support/OptionsVmFlags.{h,cpp}` (OptionsParser.cpp was at the file-size cap). Tests: tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_sync_replay.cpp (hand-built IR: 20 threaded runs each replayed, a forced lock order, conditions, the exact log bytes, changed and unusable records, divergence, deadlock replay), tests/unit/embed/test_embed_sync_replay.cpp (a Mutex and Channel program compiled once, 20 threaded runs each replayed to the same stdout; a changed program refused), tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_vm_sync_replay.cpp (primevm end to end) and the options cases; all are in tests/vm_threads_corpus.txt as `repeated`. Startup of a task-free program is unchanged by construction (no static state; one null-pointer test in `executeVmKernel`); the numbers are in docs/todo_log.md.

- [x] TODO-5919: A build step can be a PrimeStruct function that runs on a VM thread
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Build system (docs/BuildSystemPlan.md, section 4)
  - parallel_track: build-function-steps
  - scope: `b.step(name, inputs, outputs, function)` adds a step the runner executes in-process by running the function on a VM thread (TODO-5896), in parallel with other steps. The function's own effect declaration is its sandbox, and its file writes are confined to the build output directory by a path check in the host function. The export names the function and the files of its import closure and marks the graph as not self-contained. Large for one change: split it once it starts if the path confinement needs its own leaf.
  - acceptance:
    - a generator function step writes a `.prime` file that a compile step then builds
    - two function steps both produce their outputs (no timing assertion)
    - a step that writes outside the output directory faults with a diagnostic naming the path
    - the dry-run export marks the graph as not self-contained
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: function steps with declared inputs and outputs; no command steps, no network.
  - resolution: 2026-11-17. `b.step(name, inputs, outputs, source, function)` (the file is an argument too, because the runner cannot run a closure of the script and a definition in `make.prime` would run under the build profile) adds a `function` node. `primec` compiles each step with the embedding library in its own process, one at a time on the calling thread, and the runner runs the compiled definitions on its worker threads under `--jobs` (`BuildFunctionStepRunner`, `BuildFunctionSteps`, `BuildFunctionStepEmbed`). The sandbox is the effect list of the definition under a ceiling of heap_alloc, file_read, io_out, io_err and the task effects; writes go through `/std/build_step` `write_output`, whose host call uses `resolveStepOutputPath` (relative, inside the output directory, no link out of it) and faults with `build step <name> writes outside the output directory: <path>`; the path check was one function with a unit test, so it did not need a leaf. The export has `"selfContained":false` and the dry run adds `"closure"`. Function steps are cached in `.ps/cache` by key, closure and input hashes and a hash of all outputs, and an up-to-date step is not compiled. Tests: tests/unit/backend_host/test_build_function_steps.cpp. Follow-up: TODO-6029.

- [x] TODO-5922: `primevm --link` merges two serialized IR modules
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - finished_at: 2026-11-17
  - phase: Modules and libraries (docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md, sections 9 and 16)
  - parallel_track: lib-ir-link
  - scope: `IrFunction` (include/primec/ir/Ir.h) can be an import: no instructions, a flag and the name of the library that defines it; this is a schema bump with a migration note (IR stability rule, AGENTS.md). A new table classifies the operand of every opcode (function index: `Call`, `CallVoid`, `TaskSpawn`; host-import index: `CallHost`; string index: the string-printing and string-byte opcodes and string immediates; none; other), next to include/primec/ir/IrOpcodeTable.h and checked by a script in the style of scripts/check_ir_opcode_table.py, so a new opcode cannot be added without saying how it links. A merge function combines a consumer module with library modules by name: functions (an import resolves to the definition; a name defined twice is an error), struct layouts (equal layouts merge, unequal are an error), host imports (by name and signature), string tables (concatenated, every string operand remapped), instruction source maps and local debug slots (debug ids shifted). The result goes through `IrValidation`. `primevm <a> --link <b>` runs the merged module. Which opcodes carry which operand was not classified yet; read src/ir/IrValidation.cpp and the VM kernels for the ground truth.
  - acceptance:
    - two hand-built serialized modules, one calling an import the other defines, link and run on the VM with the expected result
    - one test per error: a name defined twice, unequal layouts of one name, an unresolved import (`undefined symbol <name> (library <lib>)`), a host import of one name with two signatures
    - string operands of every string opcode point at the right text after the merge (a test that prints strings from both modules)
    - the check script fails when an opcode has no operand class
    - the schema version bump has a loader test for the previous version
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the merge and the table only; no frontend, no archive, no optimizer or backend change beyond reading the merged module.
  - resolution: 2026-11-17. IR schema v38 (migration note in include/primec/ir/Ir.h and docs/spec/vm-design.md): `IrFunction::isImport` and `importLibrary`, written as a section after the host imports, and an entry index of `0xFFFFFFFF` for a module with no entry point; a v33 to v37 module loads with no imports. `include/primec/ir/IrOperandTable.h` classifies the immediate of every opcode (ground truth: src/ir/IrValidation.cpp and the VM kernels); `scripts/check_ir_opcode_table.py` fails for a missing row, a wrong order or an `Unclassified` row, and a `static_assert` ties the table to the opcode table. `linkIrModule` (src/ir/IrLinker.cpp, string pushes in src/ir/IrLinkStrings.cpp) merges functions, layouts, host imports, strings and source maps; `checkIrImportsResolved` gives `undefined symbol <name> (library <lib>)`; `validateIrModule` refuses a module that still has an import. `primevm <program> --link <module.psir>` (repeatable) runs the merge; a `.psir` program is now loaded and run without compiling. Tests: tests/unit/runtime/test_ir_link.cpp, test_ir_link_strings.cpp, test_ir_link_cli.cpp (ctest PrimeStruct_ir_link, PrimeStruct_ir_link_cli). Deviation: the opcodes carry no mark for a string literal (it is a `PushI32` or `PushI64`), so the linker follows a pushed string index to its consumer by a fixed pattern and refuses a library whose strings it would move but cannot follow; follow-up TODO-6031 (lowering marks string literal pushes).

  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-17
  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - phase: Modules and libraries (docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md, section 9; follow-up of TODO-5922)
  - parallel_track: lib-ir-link
  - scope: A string literal is a `PushI32` or `PushI64` of an index into the string table, so the IR cannot say which pushes are strings; `linkIrModule` (src/ir/IrLinker.cpp, src/ir/IrLinkStrings.cpp) finds them by the instruction that consumes them and refuses a library function whose string reaches a consumer through a local, a parameter or a return value (`cannot relocate the string operand of <opcode> in <function>`), and does not see a string that reaches no consumer in the library. Mark each literal push where lowering emits it (the `internString` call sites of src/ir_lowerer), for example a new opcode `PushString` that is class `String` in IrOperandTable.h or a flag on the instruction; a schema bump with a migration note and a loader test for the previous version, and the VM, the emitters and the optimizer treat the new form as the push it replaces. The linker then shifts exactly the marked pushes and the pattern match goes away. Which of these two encodings costs less in the VM kernels (the fast kernel fuses `PushI32` sequences, src/runtime/VmFastKernelPrepare.cpp) was not measured; measure startup and a VM benchmark before choosing.
  - acceptance:
    - a library function that prints a string it received as a parameter, and one that returns a literal, link into a program that has strings and print the right text
    - every backend that accepts the module before the change accepts it after (the corpus of the test suite), and the VM benchmark does not regress
    - the `cannot relocate` error and the pattern match are gone
    - docs/spec/vm-design.md (IR link) and docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md state the rule
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: marking literal pushes and removing the pattern match; no new link features.
  - result: Lowering marks each string literal push (`IrInstruction::isStringLiteral`, a flag in the padding of the 24-byte instruction, not a `PushString` opcode: the VM kernels, emitters and passes needed no change). PSIR v39 serializes the mark as opcode bytes 0xFE/0xFF and adds a module byte `stringPushesMarked`; a v33 to v38 module with strings loads unmarked and is refused as a library (`the library was written before IR schema v39 and does not mark its string literals; rebuild it`). The pattern match and `cannot relocate` are gone. VM startup and the VM benchmarks measured equal in an interleaved A/B against the previous commit.

- [x] TODO-5923: `primec --emit=interface` prints a module's interface and symbol table
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-11

  - phase: Modules and libraries (docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md, section 5)
  - parallel_track: lib-interface
  - scope: For a module root (a `[namespace]` or a file whose public definitions are the library, with no `main`), print the interface text in canonical PrimeStruct syntax and the symbol table as JSON. The text holds public structs and enums in full (fields with types and visibility, static fields), public non-generic functions as declarations with resolved parameter and return types, `[effects]` and `[summary]` and no body, and the `[namespace]` envelopes. The symbol table has one entry per symbol: path, kind, hash of the signature, hash of the content, hash of the closure of referenced symbols; hashes are SHA-256 (the stdlib manifest's FNV-1a 64 bit in include/primec/frontend/StdlibSymbolManifest.h only detects drift); the interface hash is the hash of the sorted table. A declaration printer is written for this; `--dump-stage ast` is a debug rendering and is not reused. Generic definitions are not included in this leaf (TODO-5926). Whether the repository has a SHA-256 to use was not checked. The pipeline may demand `/main`; emitting an interface needs no entry point.
  - acceptance:
    - golden tests of the text and the table for a module with a struct, an enum, a function, a nested namespace and a private function (absent from the output)
    - the printed text parses and validates as a program of declarations (parse-back test); if it does not, the printer is wrong
    - the same module printed twice gives byte-identical output; changing a function body changes its content hash and not its signature hash or the interface hash
    - inferred return types appear resolved (a function written without `return<...>` prints with its inferred one)
    - docs/spec/integration-and-tooling.md documents the emit kind
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: non-generic interface and the table; no archive, no library loading, no generics.
  - resolution: 2026-11-18. `primec --emit=interface` prints the interface text and `--emit=symbols` the symbol table (JSON) of a module; neither needs `/main` (a stub entry stands in for validation and is never printed). The declaration printer is src/pipeline/DeclarationText.cpp, the interface and table are src/pipeline/ModuleInterface.cpp (public API include/primec/pipeline/ModuleInterface.h), the name-based reference scan for the closure hash is src/pipeline/DefinitionReferences.cpp; SHA-256 is src/support/Sha256.cpp. Public non-generic structs, enums (printed in surface form, recognized by shape because validation keeps no mark of an enum) and functions are printed with resolved return types (an inferred return type appears resolved), resolved sorted effects (default effects included) and `[summary]`, inside `[namespace]` envelopes; stdlib definitions an import pulled in, private definitions and the entry are not printed. The table has path, kind, `signature`, `content` and `closure` SHA-256 hashes; the interface hash is the hash of the sorted `path kind signature` lines, so a body or summary change moves only `content` (and the `closure` of its dependents). Deviations: (1) the grammar has no declaration without a body, so a function declaration is printed with an empty body `{}` and parses only with `host` added (the `imported` marker of TODO-5925 gives declarations a grammar and validation); the parse-back test checks that, and struct and enum text is validated by printing it again (byte-identical). (2) The interface hash covers `path kind signature`, not the whole table, because the acceptance needs a body change to leave it alone. Tests: tests/unit/compile_run/text_filters/test_compile_run_text_filters_emit_interface.cpp (ctest `primestruct.compile.run.text_filters` shards `emit_interface`). Docs: docs/spec/integration-and-tooling.md, Module Interface.

Two things it left for this leaf: (1) the library code is lowered for the VM target, so every function has the address ABI (a struct, `mut` or string parameter is one slot holding an address or an index); a consumer lowered for a target with the scalar ABI (x86_64 native) calls it differently, so decide here whether the call site of an imported function always uses the address ABI or the archive records the ABI and the consumer target is refused when it differs. (2) The code holds the stdlib functions the library reached as real calls (for example `/std/collections/slice/Read`), and the consumer lowers the same functions under the same names, so the link must merge identical definitions of one name or the library must not hold them; the generic case is TODO-5926.
