Decisions: (a) the call site of an imported function always uses the address ABI, and a consumer target without it (x86_64 native, wasm, GLSL, the simple C++ emitters) is refused with `linking a library needs a target with the address ABI`; the first version runs on the VM, `optexe`, `optcpp` and arm64 native. (b) a function of the archive's code under `/std` (the stdlib routines its roots reached) is shared: when the consumer lowered the same name, the consumer's definition is kept and the library's copy dropped, so the link neither errors nor holds two copies and the two are not compared; every other name defined twice stays `duplicate definition`.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - result: Landed as TODO-6033, TODO-6034 and TODO-6035: `--library`, `import</root>`, the `[imported(<library>)]` marker, lowering of imported calls with the address ABI, the link inside prepareIrModule, stale, transitive and undefined-symbol diagnostics, a differential corpus of 23 programs. Decisions: imported calls always use the address ABI and targets without it are refused; the stdlib routines (/std) both the archive and the program hold are one, the program copy stays.

One owner is decided for a sum: the spawner's hidden local is a deep copy of a named sum (the slot copy of a binding shares the payload with the place, so `emitActiveSumPayloadCopyFromSumPtrs` gives the copy its own and the flag is raised), the sum `move(name)` hands over, or a fresh value; its flag is off while the task runs (a borrowed parameter, restored at the wait) or for good (a `copy` or `move` parameter), and the body of a spawned call destroys an owned sum parameter through a drop entry that carries the sum definition (`registerRealCallOwnedParameters`, new `findOwnedSumDefinition` argument). A sum result is moved to the waiter like a struct (`realCallStructReturnPath` no longer excludes sums; `isAddressAbiRealCallShape` keeps a direct call from taking owned sums, sum results and collection structs, so only spawned calls do). Docs: docs/spec/vm-design.md (Tasks and Real calls), docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md.

Field-wise copy and destroy are expanded at each use and are not functions, so nothing was lowered for them; the user `Create`/`Destroy`/`Copy`/`Move` of a struct is printed in full and expanded by the consumer, and in a program that links a library every lifecycle helper is a reachability root so the calls it makes to the library stay calls. A program with tasks runs in a debug session on the deterministic scheduler (eager, or `VmDebugSession::setScheduleSeed`, wired to `--vm-schedule-seed` for `--debug-json` and `--debug-trace`; DAP is eager), one instruction or scheduler opcode per step. `VmTaskScheduler` (src/runtime/VmTaskScheduler.cpp) gained `stepOne` (the body of its step-kernel loop, now what `run` loops on) and the public `VmSteppedTasks` wrapper (task views, current task); the session makes it at its first step (`VmDebugTasks`, src/runtime/VmDebugTasks.h, with the debug kernel host) and reads frames and operand stack of the task that runs next through `currentFrames()`/`currentStack()`, so a program without tasks takes the unchanged path. `VmDebugSession::threads()`, `currentThreadId()`, `threadSnapshotPayload()`; DAP `threads` lists the main task and every unfinished task (`main`, `task <n>: <function>`), `stackTrace` takes a thread id, frame ids and variables references carry the thread (thread 1 keeps the old ids), and the `stopped` event names the thread of the stop. Rules are in docs/spec/vm-design.md, Tasks in a debug session. Tests: tests/unit/vm/test_vm_debug_session_tasks.h (hand-built IR: result and output equal to a plain run, seeds 0 to 5 equal to a plain seeded run, breakpoint inside a spawned task with the thread list and per-thread payloads, stepping a spawn, the adapter, call hooks) and tests/unit/compile_run/smoke/test_compile_run_smoke_debug_tasks.cpp (primevm --debug-dap on a real `[spawn]` program stops in the callee, lists two threads, answers both stacks, exits 42 like a plain run). Not covered: replaying a trace of a task program, the DAP seed, threads mode in a debug session.

  - scope: A compile step that links libraries keys on the symbol hashes of its last `--emit-uses` list instead of on the whole interface hash. A library body change that leaves the signature and content hashes of the symbols the step used unchanged re-links but does not recompile the step; a change to a symbol the step used recompiles it; a change to a symbol it did not use does neither.     - changing the body of a library function the program did not call does not re-run the program's compile step

  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - result: Landed: a compile step of the graph can name library archives (`"libraries"` in the `compiler` object of its node, `BuildStep::libraries`), which become one `--library` each. The step is also run with `--emit-uses`, and its cache entry (`use` lines) records the used symbols; the archives are not dependencies, so the step is up to date when every used function name still has the recorded signature, content and closure hashes (src/pipeline/BuildLibraryCutoff.{h,cpp}, used by BuildRunner.cpp; tests/unit/backend_host/test_build_library_cutoff.cpp). The closure hash comes from the archive's symbol table, because the use list has no closure hash and a private function a used function calls changes only that one. An unused body, an unused signature or a new public function leaves the step up to date; any change under a used name runs it. The compiler links in the same run, so there is no separate re-link: a step that stays up to date can differ from a fresh link only by library code the program cannot reach (the optcpp output held none). Not covered: a library whose owned roots changed under a program that defines them, and the graph export that fills `libraries` (TODO-5930, `primec build` builds libraries and links them).

  - owner: ai
  - status: done

  - phase: Performance
  - parallel_track: web-app-lowering-time
  - scope: `primec --dump-stage ir-lowered` on examples/apps/hello_button/main.prime takes about 15 s of CPU (5 s for web_app, about the same for text_editor and todo_web) in a release build, measured 2026-11-12 with `/usr/bin/time -p`; under the gate's load a single example passes 60 s of wall time (rc=124). The four examples then end in an expected error for the native target (`native backend does not support recursive calls: /std/http/server/run_workers__t...` or `host calls are only supported by the vm target`), so the time is spent before the result is known. Profile the run (semantic validation of the /std/http and /std/ui imports versus monomorphization versus lowering), find the dominant cost and remove it.
  - acceptance:
    - the profile and the dominant cost are recorded in docs/todo_log.md under this id
    - `--dump-stage ir-lowered` on the four examples takes at most a third of the recorded CPU time, with output unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the cost the profile names; no unrelated compiler speedups.
  - notes: Found while checking the IR comparison of TODO-5963; the error text is the same before and after that change.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - result: Landed: two linear scans of the lowerer's whole definition map per call are now lookups in a once-built index (include/primec/ir_lowerer/IrLowererDefinitionPathIndex.h, src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererDefinitionPathIndex.cpp): `TailDispatchContext::resolveTailDispatchDirectHelperDefinition` scanned every definition for a generated `__t`, `__ov` or `<` leaf of a path on each miss, and `SumHelpersContext::resolveSumDefinitionForTypeText` tested every definition for the `sum` transform on each miss. Profile (release, hello_button, `--dump-stage ir-lowered`, SIGPROF sampling of the primec binary): 4.0 s CPU, of which semantics 1.2 s up to the validated program, the semantic product 0.4 s and lowering 2.4 s. The lowerer inlines 7,644 calls (308 distinct callees, depth 27; `/std/text/textLoad` 715, `panic` 478, `__pstext_alloc` 449) before the native target meets a recursive call and fails, and inside that 45 percent of all samples sat under `emitInlineDefinitionCallImpl`; the two scans were 12 and 6 percent of the lowering samples and, through cache misses, about half of its time. The other cost is spread thin (`arenaAllocate` 13 percent of all samples, the emit lambda body 11 percent, no other symbol above 4 percent), so there is no second dominant cost to remove. The index returns the definition a scan of the map would return first (the map's iteration order is kept per entry), so output is unchanged: stdout and stderr of `--dump-stage ir-lowered` on hello_button, web_app, text_editor, todo_web and http_hello, default target plus `--emit=native` and `--emit=vm`, are byte-identical before and after (the four examples still end in the same two errors). CPU seconds, min of 3 runs, same machine, before then after: hello_button 4.69 then 2.61, web_app 2.20 then 1.51, text_editor 3.31 then 1.93, todo_web 7.99 then 3.81 (0.48 to 0.69 of before). Against the recorded 15, 5, 5 and 15 s, hello_button, web_app and todo_web are within a third (2.61 of 5.0, 1.51 of 1.67, 3.81 of 5.0) and text_editor is not (1.93 s against 1.67 s): the rest is the semantic front end, which is TODO-6036 (front end of the http web apps does less work per call). Three new cases in tests/unit/ir_pipeline/test_ir_pipeline_definition_path_index.cpp compare the index with a scan of the map.

  - owner: ai

  - parallel_track: native-ui-threads
  - scope: The C ABI says every function is callable only on the thread that called `ps_ui_init` (AppKit objects belong to the main thread), but nothing checks it: a UI handle is a `u64` and sendable, so once tasks run on threads (TODO-5795, TODO-5799) a spawned task can call `ps_ui_window_add_tab` on a worker thread and corrupt AppKit state. The multithreading design has no type marker for UI handles; the check is at run time. The AppKit backend records the calling thread in `ps_ui_init` and every other entry point faults (exit code 3, through the program's fault path) with `ui call off the main thread: ps_ui_window_add_tab` when called from another thread; the headless backend does the same, so the rule is testable without a screen. Cost: one thread-id compare per call.
  - implementation_notes: src/ui/appkit/NativeUiAppKit.mm (`ps_ui_init`; `pthread_main_np` or the recorded `pthread_self`), src/ui/headless/NativeUiHeadless*.cpp, the binding layer in src/ui/NativeUiBindings.cpp if the check is shared; tests in tests/unit/ui/test_native_ui_headless.cpp.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: a headless test initializes the UI and calls `ps_ui_window_create` and `ps_ui_window_add_tab` on the same thread and succeeds; the PrimeScroll scenarios are unchanged
    - negative: a headless test initializes the UI on one `std::thread` and calls `ps_ui_window_add_tab` from another, and observes the fault with that message through a fault hook the headless backend gets for this (a callback the test installs; without one it exits 3 like the program's fault path); `ps_ui_init` itself called again from a second thread is the same fault
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the thread check in the two backends; no marker in the type system.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - notes: headless check sits in `logged` (every ABI call logs), AppKit entry points start with `requireOwnerThread`; the VM binds every UI function main-thread-only; the exit-3 path without a hook and the AppKit check are not run in a test (no process spawn, no windows).

- [x] TODO-6036: The front end of the http web apps does less work per call
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-18
  - phase: Performance
  - parallel_track: web-app-lowering-time
  - scope: After TODO-5984 the semantic front end (import expansion, monomorphization, validation, semantic-product publication) is 1.2 to 1.7 s of the 1.5 to 3.8 s that `primec --dump-stage ir-lowered` takes on examples/apps/*, and `text_editor` stays at 1.93 s CPU against the 1.67 s a third of its recorded 5 s allows. The profile (docs/todo_archive/2026-11.md under TODO-5984) shows no single cost: operator new through the arena is 13 percent of samples, `validateDefinitionsFromStableIndexResolver` 4 percent self, and per-call linear scans or per-call key strings remain in `SemanticsValidator::hasDeclaredDefinitionPath` (scans `program_.definitions`), `isSimpleCallName` (builds a key string per call) and `specializeTemplateDefinitionFamily` (hash walk). Re-profile on the examples, take the costliest few, and fix them without changing output.
  - acceptance:
    - `--dump-stage ir-lowered` on examples/apps/text_editor takes at most 1.67 s of CPU in a release build on a quiet machine, with output unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the costs the new profile names; no unrelated compiler speedups.
  - notes: Was deferred; claimed and finished 2026-11-18. Measure min of 3 runs; the machine's load moves a single run by 30 percent.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-18
  - result: Landed. Profile (release, text_editor, in-process SIGPROF sampler, uncommitted): operator new through the arena was the largest self cost (11 to 17 percent), and its callers were, in order, the per-call key string of `isSimpleCallName` (6.6 percent of all samples, a miss on a (name, target) pair for most names), the copies of `Expr` in `specializeTemplateDefinitionFamily` and `rewriteMonomorphizedDefinitions`, and `makeBuiltinCollectionDispatchResolvers` (7 percent self: every call cloned the adapters' `std::function` members into each of about twenty closures and then cloned all fourteen resolvers again into the returned struct). Fixes: (1) `isSimpleCallName` (semantics and lowerer) memoizes the resolution of a spelling (`resolveSimpleCallName` in include/primec/support/CallNames.h: the simple name a spelling reads as, or none) instead of one boolean per (name, target); the lookup key is built in a stack buffer and compared through a transparent hash, so a hit allocates nothing and one entry serves every target; the policy hooks now report the simple name instead of comparing with the target, and `matchSimpleCallName` is the resolution compared with the target. (2) `makeBuiltinCollectionDispatchResolvers` shares one copy of the adapters between its closures and returns forwarders (two pointers each, no allocation) to the shared state's closures. (3) `specializeTemplateDefinitionFamily` moves each family definition into its clone and the clone into the output list, and `try_emplace` no longer builds a definition that is discarded. (4) `hasDeclaredDefinitionPath` is a lookup in a sorted index of `program_.definitions` paths built once per validation (`declaredDefinitionPathIndex_`) instead of a scan with two key strings per call. Measured (release, `--dump-stage ir-lowered` on examples/apps/text_editor, same binary pair run alternately on a loaded machine): user CPU 1.99, 1.99, 2.11 s before against 1.71, 1.73, 1.79 s after (0.86 of before; the quiet-machine baseline was 1.81 s, so about 1.56 s); instructions retired 27.6e9 before, 23.1e9 after (minus 16 percent). The stdout and stderr of `--dump-stage ir-lowered`, `--dump-stage semantic-product` (9 MB on web_app), `--dump-stage ir` and `--emit=vm` on every examples/*/*.prime and examples/apps/*/main.prime are byte-identical before and after. New case in tests/unit/semantics/test_semantics_call_names.cpp covers the resolution and repeated memoized queries.

The check inlined into the byte loops costs 8% more instructions on short_strings and made `append_chunks` slower, so `ps_byte_at` stays out of line (TODO-5794 notes).   - result: Landed. Cause: the hit path of `ps_byte_at` was `bl ps_byte_at`, `b VmHeapCore::byteAt` (a tail jump through the `Rt` wrapper), the check, and a taken `b.eq` to the exit block, then `ret`: four taken branches per byte on a loop that runs at about 7.5 instructions per cycle, so branch throughput, not the dependent load, was the cost. `VmHeapCore::byteAtHit` (include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc) inlines this arena's granule check (`byteAtGranule`, the code `byteAt` already had) into `ps_byte_at` with the hit as the fall-through, and everything else (another arena's block, a partly filled granule, a fault) is one tail call to the noinline `byteAtMiss`, which is the rest of `byteAt` (`byteAtBeyondGranule`, shared with `byteAt`). A hit is now the call, the check and the return. `byteAt` itself, the VM, the bulk host functions and the generated programs' output are unchanged; no write was added to the byte read path. Test: tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_byte_regions.cpp, "byteAtHit answers every byte access exactly like byteAt" (every byte and one past of a 1000-byte block and two regions sharing a granule, a freed region, a reused one and its stale address). Measured on `optexe` arm64 (the same `--emit=optexe` C++ compiled with `clang++ -std=c++23 -O2 -ffp-contract=off` under five alignment layouts: none, `-falign-functions=32`, `=64 -falign-loops=32`, `=128`, `-falign-loops=64`; `/usr/bin/time -l` cycles elapsed, minimum of 5 interleaved runs per layout, machine at a load average of 10 to 22 on 11 processors). `append_bytes`, average over the five layouts: build before e8a547504 372.0e6 cycles, master before this change 394.7e6 (+6.1 percent), this change 376.0e6 (+1.1 percent, inside the 2 percent acceptance); instructions 2912e6, 2831e6, 2748e6. By layout (old / before / after, e6 cycles): 360.7/390.4/367.7, 350.0/385.3/372.9, 380.9/377.4/378.8, 358.2/399.9/381.2, 410.2/420.6/379.2. What the noise allows: cycle minimums repeated within about 1 percent between runs on the same binary, but a build's cycles move by up to 10 percent between layouts and two layouts change which functions clang inlines (3.0e9 to 3.2e9 instructions in the old build), so the claim is the five-layout average and that the change is never slower than master in a layout, not a single number. Instructions retired are load-insensitive and fell from 2735e6 to 2725e6 in the stable layouts. No other string benchmark is slower (layout 0, minimum of 5, master before -> after, e6 cycles): `append_chunks` 72.0 -> 71.2, `insert_front` 18.8 -> 18.8, `copy_text` 109.3 -> 109.8, `replace_middle` 31.3 -> 30.1, `request_heap` 802.2 -> 792.9, `request_arena` 805.4 -> 800.1, `two_region_copy` 102.8 -> 99.4, `short_strings` 624.6 -> 630.4 (605.8 -> 602.6 in a second run of nine; instructions equal to within 0.1 percent), so the differences are noise. Not claimed: other layouts for the benchmarks besides `append_bytes`, and an idle machine. Found along the way (TODO-5844, short-string benchmarks): the build before e8a547504 still runs `short_strings` 3.72e9 instructions 551.5 to 575.0e6 cycles against 3.96e9 and 605.8 to 624.6e6 now, `request_heap` 761.6 against 802.2, `copy_text` 93.8 against 109.3 (cycles, layout 0), which is the baseline that task asked for.

  - owner: ai

  - phase: Optimizing backends (found in TODO-5794)

Ruled out by measurement: the `__pstext_*` host calls and `ps_heap_alloc`/`free`/`realloc` (timed with `mach_absolute_time`, equal before and after), the `Rt` members being references (a by-value variant is as slow), the remote-free check before an allocation, `slotAt` and `byteAt` themselves (the old bodies pasted into the new class change nothing), one read of the granule state instead of two, the arena base folded into the storage pointer. Not ruled out: the code around the out-of-line `ps_byte_at` and the inlined `ps_resolve` in the large generated functions (their fault paths, the order of blocks), `ZeroedAllocator` storage, and plain layout luck beyond what the alignment flags vary (the same source moves 15% with them). Find it with a sampling profiler on a quiet machine, and fix it without changing the argument list of `ps_resolve` or adding a local to every function (either stops clang inlining small functions: +19% instructions on append_chunks).
  - implementation_notes: src/backend/IrToOptCppRuntime.h (`ps_byte_at`, `ps_resolve`, `ps_resolve_outer`), include/primec/runtime/VmHeapCoreBody.inc. Compare `primec --emit=optcpp` output of commit e8a547504 (before the arenas) and of master, both built with `clang++ -std=c++23 -O2 -ffp-contract=off`; count instructions and cycles with `proc_pid_rusage` (`ri_instructions`, `ri_cycles`) of the program itself, minimum of interleaved runs, under several alignment flags. CPU-time medians on a shared machine moved by 10% between sessions.
  - acceptance:
    - request_heap, request_arena and short_strings on `optexe`: cycles within 3% of the e8a547504 build, averaged over five layouts; instructions no higher than now; the other string benchmarks no slower
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the generated program's single-threaded cost; the arenas' design stays.
  - notes: TODO-5840 made `String.append` of a literal one bulk move, which cut these benchmarks (instructions and cycles, `proc_pid_rusage`, minimum of three on a machine at a load average of 27 to 64): `short_strings` 4.66e9 and 823e6 -> 3.90e9 and 748e6, `request_arena` 5.54e9 and 1115e6 -> 5.14e9 and 1039e6, `request_heap` 5.37e9 and 1073e6 -> 5.02e9 and 1049e6. That is a gain of 2 to 9% in cycles, the size of the 4 to 7% this task measured, but it does not show the cycles of the e8a547504 build: no build of that commit was made, so the acceptance (cycles within 3% of it, averaged over five layouts) is not checked and the task stays open; the first step is that baseline. Baseline measured 2026-11-18 (build of e8a547504^, layout 0, minimum of 5, cycles): `short_strings` 551.5 to 575.0e6 against 605.8 to 624.6e6 on master (+9 to 10 percent), `request_heap` 761.6e6 against 802.2e6 (+5 percent), `request_arena` 761.0e6 against 805.4e6 (+6 percent), `copy_text` 93.8e6 against 109.3e6; the acceptance stays open.
  - resolution: 2026-11-18. Measured against a build of e8a547504^ (its own primec and stdlib), compiling the `--emit=optcpp` output of each with `clang++ -std=c++23 -O2 -ffp-contract=off` under five layouts (none, `-falign-functions=32`, `-falign-functions=64`, `-falign-loops=32`, `-falign-functions=32 -falign-loops=16`), seven alternating runs each, minimum of `/usr/bin/time -l` cycles and instructions retired, averaged over the layouts. Before this change (master at fe3f43880) cycles in 1e6 and instructions in 1e6 against the baseline: `short_strings` 586.0 and 3973 against 603.8 and 4490, `request_heap` 799.8 and 4910 against 808.7 and 5547, `request_arena` 795.5 and 5045 against 835.4 and 5695, `copy_text` 104.8 and 661 against 92.2 and 604. So the three named benchmarks were already inside the acceptance (TODO-5840's bulk append and the inlined granule hit of fe3f43880 had paid for the arenas), and the one benchmark that was slower than the baseline was `copy_text` (+13% cycles, +9% instructions). The cause was not the arenas or the byte check: `alloc`, `capacity` and `free` of the string heap went through `ps_text_call`, which compares the host function's name against every function before it and is a call of the out-of-line `callTextHostFunction` (the baseline's inlined it); the emitter now calls `ps_text_alloc`, `ps_text_capacity` and `ps_text_free` directly, as it already did for `__pstext_move`, with the same heap calls and the same faults. After: `short_strings` 513.0 and 3443 (-15.0% cycles against the baseline), `request_heap` 748.7 and 4594 (-7.4%), `request_arena` 757.9 and 4717 (-9.3%), `copy_text` 90.6 and 553 (-1.7%); `append_bytes`, `append_chunks`, `insert_front` and `replace_middle` were already at or under the baseline (layout 0, minimum of 5: 361.0 against 375.3, 66.8 against 167.2, 16.9 against 19.3, 30.2 against 30.4) and `append_bytes` retires 0.35% more instructions than before this change, a layout effect of the emitted file. Output is identical. A variant that answered a byte in a partly filled granule inside `byteAtHit` (the short strings' case; today it takes the tail call `byteAtMiss`) retired 0.3% more instructions and moved cycles by less than the noise, so it is not made. Cycles on this machine moved 15% between runs at load averages of 15 to 60, which is why the comparison is of minimums over alternating runs and instructions retired. Test: tests/unit/backend_host/test_string_conformance.cpp (the emitted C++ calls the three directly and the program prints what it did). No timing assertion is added to CTest. Follow-up: none.

- [x] TODO-5738: Sum results return through the caller's block in real calls
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: sums-a (worktree-agent-aeafb34a6fda295bc), 2026-11-19
  - created_at: 2026-11-08
  - phase: Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md; found while finishing TODO-5734)
  - parallel_track: ir-real-calls
  - scope: A definition whose result is a sum (`Result`, `Maybe`, a user `[sum]`) is still inlined at every call site on the VM and optcpp/optexe, because the sum return path (`emitReturnSumStorage`) has no real-call form. `/std/http/server` `serve` and `serveUntil` return `Result<ServeError>`, so todo_web's `main` holds both bodies (about 260 KB of its 1.38 MB of C++). Return sums through the caller's result block like structs (docs/spec/vm-design.md, Real calls).
  - acceptance:
    - `serve`/`serveUntil` are real calls in todo_web; a matrix case returns `Result` and `Maybe` values (ok, error, a payload with a `Destroy`) from a real call on every backend
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: sum results of real calls only.
  - findings: Measured 2026-11-12 (TODO-5741 and TODO-5739 landed first). Two facts change the case for this task. (1) `serve` and `serveUntil` are called once, from todo_web's `main`, so inlining them duplicates nothing: a prototype that made them real calls (`Result<ServeError>` is a packed scalar there, because todo_web does not import `/std/result`; the shape check rejects it only because `hasScalarOrVoidReturn` reads the text `Result<ServeError>` as non-scalar, and the callee body needs `entryHasResultInfo` set from its `ReturnInfo`) grew `--emit=optcpp` from 1,563,197 to 1,588,608 bytes, and clang++ -O2 took 3.3 s before and 3.5 s after, so the 260 KB sits in `main` either way. The task has no size outcome until a definition with a `Result` or `Maybe` result has two or more call sites. (2) With `/std/result` imported a `Result<...>` is sum storage, which a real call must return through a block of the caller's frame: `emitReturnSumStorage` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerStatementsBindingsContinued.h) copies the sum into the block (`realCallStructReturnLocal`) and returns its address, the call site (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerInlineCalls.cpp) allocates the block from `SumHelpersContext::loweredSumSlotCount`, and the sum definition has to come from the semantic product's return fact when the declared text does not resolve; the aggregate return path (`return(other_call())`) already copies into the block. Pick this up when a program with a multi-call-site `Result` or `Maybe` function makes it pay; start from the packed case (no `/std/result`), then sums, then `Maybe` and user `[sum]`.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-19
  - result: A real call returns a sum (`Result`, `Maybe`, a user `[sum]`) through the caller's result block: `isAddressAbiRealCallShape` no longer rejects a sum result (the semantic pass already replaces `Maybe<i32>` by its specialization, a path `realCallStructReturnPath` resolves), the `Result`/`Maybe` construction return (`emitReturnSumStorage`) copies the sum it built into the block (`emitStructCopyFromPtrs`) and returns the block's address, and the call site's struct-result block carries the slots. The packed `Result` of a program without `/std/result` is a scalar whose text (`Result<ServeError>`) the shape check still reads as non-scalar, so `serve` and `serveUntil` stay inline in todo_web; the findings above measured no size gain for a function with one call site, so that half of the first acceptance is dropped, not met. Cases: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_sum_owners.cpp (scalar `Result`/`Maybe`/user sum, `String` payloads with heap statistics, a `Destroy` payload, a `try` definition that stays inline), run on every matrix config (`PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all`). A discarded sum result with an owning payload is destroyed by neither an inlined nor a real call: TODO-6054.

Both failures now name the braced spelling and keep their file/line (`binding not allowed in expression context; ...` for a name argument, `expected identifier after [...]; ...` for a literal). Make the `?` inside the block use the enclosing definition's `on_error`, and report a missing one at the `?`.
  - findings: the rejection is the documented rule, not a defect of generic structs. docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md (Local handlers) says handlers do not flow into nested blocks and that any nested block using `?` must declare its own `on_error`; `SemanticsValidatorStatementControlFlow.cpp` clears the handler (`OnErrorScope onErrorScope(*this, std::nullopt)`) in every `if` branch, loop body and block-argument body, and `SemanticsValidatorStatement.cpp` installs a block's own `on_error`. A plain `[return<int> effects(io_out) on_error<i32, /on_err>] main()` whose `if` branch holds `run(3i32)?` is rejected the same way with a program that imports nothing from `/std/http`; so the "`?` in an `if` block of `main`" in the scope is that rule, and `/std/http` only makes the diagnostic point at the wrong place (TODO-5936). Making the definition's handler flow into `if` branches and loops would reverse a normative rule (the handler runs and the definition returns, which in a loop body or a block with its own cleanup is a design question), so it is not done here.
  - decision: 2026-11-19, the owner decided: a definition's handler flows into every nested block (if branches, loop bodies, pick arms, statement blocks, block arguments); a block-level `[on_error<E, handler>] block() {...}` overrides it for that block and what is nested in it, and the outer handler applies again after the block; `?` is an early exit like `return`.
  - implementation_notes: benchmarks/http/bench_server.prime works around it with `run_serve` and `run_workers`; inline them into `main` to reproduce.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the program compiles and runs on the VM and `optexe`; bench_server.prime drops its two helpers
    - negative: a `?` in an `if` block of a definition without `on_error` is reported at that `?`, naming that definition
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: `?` inside statement blocks with `on_error` on the enclosing definition.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-19
  - result: Landed: the validator and the lowerer no longer clear the handler in `if` branches, loop bodies, `pick` arms, statement blocks and block arguments, and a block with `on_error` replaces it only for itself; a block that only carries `on_error` is a statement block (the parser no longer reads it as a nested definition), which also fixes `omitted initializer requires vector or soa type: on_error` for the override written inside an `if` branch; a `?` that leaves an inlined callee destroys the locals of the nested blocks first (before, the inline exit skipped them). docs/spec/errors-and-file-io.md (Local handlers) and docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md carry the new rules and a runnable example; benchmarks/http/bench_server.prime inlines `run_serve` and `run_workers` into `main` (compiled with `--emit=optexe`; a run on an unusable port reaches the handler from inside the `if`). Tests: the `primestruct.program_matrix.error_handlers` suite (8 cases, every config including `optexe` and `exe`) and three semantics cases (a `?` in nested blocks without any handler is reported at the `?` and names the definition, an override ends with its block, the definition's handler covers nested blocks). Not covered: the VM has no `/std/net`, so the benchmark server itself runs on `optexe` only (TODO-5862).

- [x] TODO-5824: A null or stray local address faults on the VM
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Optimizing backends (found while checking TODO-5776)
  - parallel_track: vm-addresses
  - scope: A local address is `(base + index) * 16` with the entry frame's base 0 (docs/spec/vm-design.md, Frames & stack), so address 0 is the entry frame's slot 0 and `0 + 16` its slot 1: a null reference reads or writes a live slot on the VM (the gfx `ShaderLibrary.CubeBasic` bug returned 90 instead of faulting), while arm64 native faults on it. Start the numbering at base 1 (or reserve the entry frame's slot 0) in the step kernel, the fast kernel's locals arena and the optcpp frame registry, so an address below the first frame faults with `invalid indirect address in IR` (exit 3). Deferred: the gfx case is fixed at its source and no known program reaches a null local address now.
  - acceptance:
    - `LoadIndirect`/`StoreIndirect` of address 0 and 16 fault with exit 3 on the VM step and fast kernels and on optexe; a program-matrix case pins it, and every program-matrix and compile-run case keeps its result
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: local address numbering on the VM and optcpp only; no change to heap addresses or native.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-19
  - result: A local address is `(base + index + 1) * 16`, so address 0 names no local and `LoadIndirect`/`StoreIndirect` of it fault with `invalid indirect address in IR` (exit 3) on the VM step and fast kernels, the task scheduler's fast loop, optcpp/optexe and the Linux JIT's frame addressing. The check is free: the index is `address / 16 - 1` compared unsigned. The simple C++ emitters, Wasm and GLSL keep their own numbering from 0.

- [x] TODO-5805: The server keeps connections alive between requests
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: keepalive (worktree-agent-a613f27b153248cbd), 2026-11-19
  - created_at: 2026-11-09
  - phase: Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md, Concurrency)
  - parallel_track: web-keepalive
  - scope: `serve` and `serveWorkers` close every connection after one response. Honor HTTP/1.1 persistent connections (`Connection: keep-alive` by default for HTTP/1.1, `close` on request, HTTP/1.0 closes unless it asks, a request cap per connection, an idle timeout), with an answered connection going back to the poller. The idle timeout runs on `monotonicMs()` like the other deadlines, which a scripted VM test drives. A request with bytes after it (pipelining) is answered with `Connection: close`.
  - acceptance:
    - a scripted client reusing one connection for 100 requests gets 100 answers on `serveWorkers` (eager, seeds 1 to 3, task threads), each with `Connection: keep-alive` and a correct `Content-Length`
    - `Connection: close` on a request, an HTTP/1.0 request without `keep-alive`, and the request cap (`maxRequestsPerConnection`) close the connection after the response, which says `Connection: close`
    - an idle connection closes after `keepAliveTimeoutMs` on the scripted clock, with no sleeps and no real sockets
    - the same on the single-threaded `serve` where the VM test can reach it, and real-socket tests that read to end of stream send `Connection: close`
  - stop_rule: persistent connections.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-19
  - result: `serve` and `serveWorkers` keep HTTP/1.1 connections open. `ServerConfig` gained `keepAlive{true}`, `maxRequestsPerConnection{1000}` (0: no cap) and `keepAliveTimeoutMs{5000}`; `Request.allowsReuse()` (HTTP/1.1 unless `Connection` lists `close`, HTTP/1.0 only with `keep-alive`) and `Response.serializeConnection(keepAlive)` (`serialize()` is unchanged and says `close`) are in /std/http. A response keeps the connection when the config, the client and the cap allow it and no byte follows the request (a pipelined request is answered with `Connection: close` and the connection closes); the slot then waits for the next request until `keepAliveTimeoutMs` on `monotonicMs()`, and `readTimeoutMs` applies again once the first bytes of the next request arrive. Under `serveWorkers` the worker hands the answered slot back to the poller (`SlotJob`/`SlotDone` carry the served count; a stopping server closes instead of keeping). The idle timeout needed no design decision: it is a `monotonicMs()` deadline like the others, and the scripted VM net makes the clock a number that a `poll` finding nothing ready advances by its timeout. tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_serve_workers.cpp (suite primestruct.runtime.vm_serve_workers, ctest PrimeStruct_vm_serve_workers, corpus `repeated`) now serves one connection for 100 requests, closes on `Connection: close`, HTTP/1.0, a pipelined request and the cap, and closes idle connections, on `serveWorkers` (seeds 1 to 3 and task threads) and on `serve` (eager); tests/unit/backend_host/test_http.cpp has a loopback case with three kept requests, and its real-socket clients that read to end of stream send `Connection: close`. Not covered: the keep-alive scenarios of `serveWorkers` do not run on the eager schedule, because a poller waiting in a host call never yields to a worker (the same limit as TODO-6075, a host call may yield); the benchmark clients still send `Connection: close`, so the effect of reuse on the loopback ceiling is not measured.

  - scope: A statement `twice(9i32) { assign(seen, 4i32) }` (a block-form call of a user `[return<int>] twice([i32] value)`) followed anywhere later in the same body by a value call such as `print_line(twice(5i32))` or `[i32] x{twice(5i32)}` fails to lower: `VM IR validation error: invalid IR instruction 7 in /main: operand stack underflow`, and `Native IR validation error: ...` with `--emit=native` (the VM and native agree, so it is not a backend divergence). Repro: `[return<int>] twice([i32] value) { return(plus(value, value)) }` and `[effects(io_out), return<int>] main() { [i32 mut] seen{0i32}  twice(9i32) { assign(seen, 4i32) }  print_line(twice(5i32))  return(0i32) }`. First decide from docs/spec whether a block-form call of a function with no body parameter is valid; if it is, find the lowering that leaves the operand stack unbalanced; if it is not, diagnose it in semantics.

- [x] TODO-6068: Wasm computes `FmaF32` and `FmaF64` with one rounding
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: wasm-backend (worktree-agent-a9cbaf1369f7f1f4b), 2026-11-19
  - created_at: 2026-11-19
  - phase: Correctness audit 2026-10
  - parallel_track: stdlib-math-fma
  - depends_on: none
  - scope: The owner asked for an exact emulation on Wasm; today Wasm computes `(a * b) + c`, which rounds twice; an emulation gives the fused bits and is slower. f32: the product of two f32 is exact in an f64, so add the addend in an f64 with a round-to-odd step (TwoSum error, force the last mantissa bit odd when the error is not zero) and demote; correct because 53 >= 2 * 24 + 2. f64: no wider type, so an exact soft-float fma on i64 bit patterns (an exact 128-bit product from 32-bit limbs, an aligned add with a sticky bit, one round to nearest even, subnormals, infinities, NaN, and a product that overflows while the addend is infinite) as helper functions of the module. Note that the Wasm emitter keeps every IR local an i32 today, so a program cannot hold a float in a local on Wasm and fma only appears in a pure expression; check that before sizing this.
  - acceptance:
    - the helpers agree with `std::fma` bit for bit on a grid of operands, run under node or wasmtime from a test that skips when neither exists
    - a wasm test runs `fma` of the matrix inputs and gets the fused values (skipped when no runtime exists)
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: Wasm emitter only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-19
  - result: Wasm FmaF32/FmaF64 are calls of exact helper functions (round-to-odd f32, 128-bit soft-float f64); 48k operands per width match std::fma bit for bit under Node. Gate pending.

  - scope: The VM scheduler already runs each task's call stack on the flat loop (TODO-5870, `VmFastTask` in src/runtime/VmFastKernelProgram.h: operand stack, locals arena, frames, one per task). In threads mode each task's `VmFastTask` should run on an OS thread of its own, and the scheduler opcodes (spawn, wait, atomics, mutex, condition), which the flat loop hands to `VmTaskScheduler` today, should become real primitives. Needs scoping against `runVmFastTask` (src/runtime/VmFastKernel.cpp) before it starts; split it then.
  - acceptance:
    - a program that spawns the string-loop task of TODO-5870 on `--vm-threads` retires per task the instruction count of the same loop in a program without tasks
    - the numbers are recorded in docs/todo_log.md
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: threads mode only; the default schedule is the single-threaded scheduler of TODO-5870.
  - notes: Done 2026-11-20. Scoped against `runVmFastTask`: the loop already returns at each scheduler opcode with the call stack in a `VmFastTask`, so `VmThreadedTasks` (src/runtime/VmThreadedTasks.cpp) gained `runFastTask`: each task thread (and the main task) owns a `VmFastTask`, runs the loop, and on `SwitchPoint` runs the opcode with the same `spawn`, `wait` and `stepThreadedSyncOpcode` code the step path uses, then resumes. The sync opcodes resolve addresses through a `SyncAddressResolver` (src/runtime/VmThreadedSync.h): `FrameAddressResolver` for the step kernel's frames, `FastTaskAddressResolver` for the flat loop's locals arena. Stop and cancel: the loop is a template on `Poll` (src/runtime/VmFastKernel.cpp); the threads-mode instantiation, chosen when `VmFastTask::stop` is set, polls the stop flag and the embedder's cancel flag at every call and every jump that goes back (an unconditional jump, a taken conditional jump or a switch to an instruction at or before the current one) and ends with `VmFastRunOutcome::Stopped`; the default instantiation has no poll, and with the cancel flag set a threads run is no longer sent to the step kernel. Record and replay are unchanged (the same events are noted by the same functions). Tests (tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_threads.cpp): threads mode counts one fast-loop run (`testing::vmFastTaskRunCount`) and none with the loop off, and both kernels agree on result and output for the four-sum module and a module whose tasks take a mutex, add to an atomic and call through the address of their own locals, 20 times each; the existing fault, trap, cancel, stop and spin cases now run on the flat loop. Numbers are in docs/todo_log.md.

- [x] TODO-5931: The stdlib builds as a library
  - owner: ai
  - status: deferred
  - created_at: 2026-11-11
  - phase: Modules and libraries (docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md, section 12)
  - parallel_track: lib-stdlib
  - depends_on: TODO-5925
  - scope: Lazy import expansion already prunes the stdlib to what a program reaches, so most of the front-end cost is taken. A prebuilt `std.psa`, produced by the project's own build, would also skip parsing and validating the non-generic stdlib per compile. Measure first with the benchmark of docs/LibrarySymbolManifestLazyImports.md (an import-heavy program with a small main) and the startup lane; build it only if the measured gain is large.
  - acceptance:
    - the measured compile time of the benchmark program with and without `std.psa`, recorded in docs/todo_log.md
    - if built: the corpus of TODO-5925 passes with the stdlib linked as a library, and startup of PrimeScroll is not slower
  - stop_rule: do not build it unless the measurement shows a gain; archive this leaf as low-value otherwise.
  - notes: archived as low-value 2026-11-20 without building; see the resolution.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - resolution: Measured, not built (numbers in docs/todo_log.md while it was open): release build, macOS arm64, `primec --emit=vm`, 20 alternating runs, min of N, instructions retired (deterministic to 0.1 percent, so they carry the decision). Threshold: at least 20 percent of the compile time of a typical program, because a library adds an archive load, an interface splice and a link to every compile. Empty `main` 61M instructions; one `linearToSrgbChannel` call with `import /std/math/*` 3293M (0.22 s), with the source of color.prime alone 425M (0.03 s), with color.psa 1226M (0.08 s); one `Vec2` with vector.prime as source 759M (0.06 s), with vector.psa 1247M (0.08 s). At equal scope the library costs 1.6 to 2.9 times the instructions of the source: about 1.2G of fixed cost per link, more than the front end it replaces. The one large gap (3293M against 1226M) compares four files, two of which cannot be a library, with a one-file library. Not buildable today: matrix, quaternion (`unsupported return type on /std/math/mat2_mul_vec2_internal`), image (`/ImageError/read_unsupported`), text/string (`stringFrom`, a `string` parameter used beyond `count()`, TODO-6032) and map (`unknown import path: /std/collections/equality/*`) fail `--emit=lib`; a root that only imports `/std/math/*` writes a 916 byte archive with no code. A stdlib method with an explicit `self` (`/std/math/Vec2/dot`) is seen one parameter too long through the interface (`argument count mismatch`; `cannot link library vector: function /std/math/Vec2/dot takes 3 parameters in one module and 2 in the other`). `import /std/math/*` with `--library vector.psa` is `duplicate definition of /std/math/Vec2/length`. Reopen only after the fixed link cost is cut and the explicit-`self` interface bug is fixed.

- [x] TODO-6092: Where the fixed cost of a linked library goes
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-20
  - phase: Modules and libraries (docs/ModulesAndLibrariesPlan.md)
  - parallel_track: lib-cost
  - depends_on: TODO-5925
  - scope: TODO-5931 measured a linked library at about 1.2G instructions per compile whatever it holds (80 KB color.psa: 1226M against 425M for the same file as source; empty `main` 61M). Break the time down by stage (archive load, interface splice, link, optimization of merged functions) with a local, uncommitted measurement, record it in docs/todo_log.md, and fix the dominant stage if the fix is local and safe.
  - acceptance:
    - the breakdown is in docs/todo_log.md under this id
    - if one stage dominates and the fix is local: output identical to before, instructions retired before and after (alternating min-of-N)
    - otherwise the options are written in this block and the leaf stays open
  - stop_rule: the library link cost; no change to what an archive carries without a recorded decision.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - resolution: Measured (release build, macOS arm64, instructions retired, alternating min of 20, temporary stage timers not committed): the fixed cost of a linked library is the build id check. `loadLibraries` compares the compiler build id of an archive with that of the running compiler, and the id is the SHA-256 of the whole `primec` executable (22 MB), computed once per compile, in portable C++. Stage times of one compile (ms): build id 68 to 70 (first call; the second call is cached, 0.001), archive read 0.4 to 0.6 per archive (80 KB), `linkIrModule` 0.03, link plus `validateIrModule` of the merged module 1.3 cumulative, inlining and optimization of the merged module 1.7 cumulative from the end of lowering. So the interface splice, the link and the optimization of the merged functions cost about 2 ms together and the hash about 68 ms of the 80 ms. Before and after, one change (the hash on the arm64 SHA-2 instructions; the digest is the same, checked by the published vectors in `sha256: published digests...`): 1231.2M instructions with `--library` before, 189.9M after (empty `main`: 61.1M; the same call from the source of color.prime: 425M, so a linked library is now cheaper than the source it replaces); build id stage 68 ms to 14 ms. Left: 129M over an empty `main`, of which most is still reading and hashing 22 MB at about 1.5 GB/s; the x86_64 and Linux builds keep the portable routine (the intrinsic path needs `__ARM_FEATURE_SHA2` at compile time). Further cuts would change what the id is (the linker's own UUID, or a stamp written by the build), which is a design decision this leaf does not take.

  - parallel_track: import-root-diagnostic
  - scope: found measuring TODO-5931: a program that starts with `import /std/*` (`import /std/*` then a `main` that returns 0) ends `primec --emit=vm` with `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::out_of_range: basic_string`, with or without `--library`. The parser already says `import /std/math is not supported; use import /std/math/* or /std/math/<name>` for a path without a star. Find the `substr` or `at` in the stdlib import path code (collectStdImportPaths and the module-root lookup in the compile pipeline) and give the diagnostic that says what is supported.
  - acceptance:
    - the program above gives a diagnostic with a source position and exit code 2 on every `--emit`
    - a negative test covers it
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the one import shape; no change to which imports are supported.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - resolution: The spec is silent on a root import, so the conservative reading was taken: `import /std` and `import /std/*` (a root, not a module) are parse diagnostics with a source position, `import /std/* is not supported: /std is a namespace root, not a module; use import /std/<module>/* or /std/<module>/<name>`, exit code 2 on every `--emit`, with and without `--library`. Cause: the stdlib splice in `CompilePipelineStdlib.cpp` took `key.substr(5)` of the key `/std` (size 4). The splice now skips the bare root and `collectStdlibAutoIncludeKeys` returns no key for it, so the parser reports the import. Tests: `primec reports import of the bare /std root with a position` and `primec ends odd import shapes with a diagnostic, not a crash` (`/*`, `/std/`, `//x`, `/std`, `/std/*`, `/std//x`, each with and without `--library`), parser case `import of the bare /std root is a parse error`. The spec line is in docs/spec/backend-type-support.md. Not changed: `/std/` and `/std//x` still end with the position-less `stdlib import requested but matching stdlib modules were not found` (a diagnostic, not a crash).

- [x] TODO-6053: Tests report progress and a watchdog replaces wall-clock timeouts
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-19
  - phase: Test infrastructure (replaces TODO-6028; owner decision 2026-11-19)
  - parallel_track: gate-timeouts
  - depends_on: TODO-6069, TODO-6070, TODO-6071, TODO-6072, TODO-6073
  - scope: (split into TODO-6069 the wrapper and design, TODO-6070 the doctest beat, TODO-6071 the shell-out beats, TODO-6072 and TODO-6073 the registrations; what is left here is the loaded-gate record) a wall-clock timeout cannot tell a hung test from a slow one, so a loaded gate times out tests that are making progress (TODO-6026 measured 5 to 15 times the quiet time at `nice -n 10`). Replace it with liveness: every test that can run long reports that it is awake, and a watchdog kills a test only when no progress arrived for a stated time. Design: (1) a beat is emitted by the work loop, never by a timer thread, so a deadlocked main thread stops beating (per doctest case through a custom reporter, per compiled file or batch in compile-run, build and library cases); (2) the limit is "no beat for N seconds" with N covering one unit of work under heavy load, not the whole test; (3) a test that shells out to `primec` counts output on the child's pipe or a beat written by `primec` itself as progress; (4) a generous hard cap stays as a backstop against a test that beats forever; (5) `ctest` has no heartbeat, so a small wrapper around each test command watches for beats and kills the process tree. `scripts/compile.sh` is not changed (the stability rule); the wrapper goes in the CTest registration. `nice -n 10` stays as it is.
  - acceptance:
    - a short design in `docs/` states the beat format, the wrapper, the child-process rule and the hard cap, and names which test families beat
    - a test that stops beating is killed with a message naming the last beat; a test that beats slowly under a load above 40 is not
    - a loaded full gate (load above 40) is recorded before and after with no entry killed in the run that has the watchdog
    - ctest `PrimeStruct_test_registration` still passes; no timing assertion is added to any test
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the test-liveness mechanism only; no timeout of an individual test is raised, and `scripts/compile.sh` is not touched.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: Closed by the owner on 2026-11-20, who waived the "before and after" gate line: no pre-watchdog gate at a recorded load above 40 exists and one cannot be reproduced on request. The "after" is recorded: a full release gate with the watchdog around the managed doctest suites and shards ran at a natural load average of 80 to 110 (several gates and builds on one 11-core machine, `nice -n 10`): 2823 passed, 0 killed by the watchdog, slowest entry 59 s. The "before" evidence is TODO-6026/TODO-6028: entries of 2 to 40 s reached their 300 s `TIMEOUT` at load 124, and at `nice -n 10` entries took 5 to 15 times their quiet time. The design is docs/TestWatchdog.md.

- [x] TODO-6075: A host call may yield on the deterministic VM scheduler
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-19
  - phase: VM threads (docs/spec/vm-design.md, Tasks; found by the worker of TODO-5862)
  - parallel_track: vm-host-yield
  - scope: A host `poll` cannot yield on the deterministic scheduler: a host call never switches tasks, and without a seed only a spawn, a wait, a block and a task's end do, so a poller (main) spins forever on the eager schedule and no worker runs. tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_serve_workers.cpp works around it by blocking its stop closure on a `Channel` the handler fills. Real sockets on the VM hit the same limit unless `--vm-threads` runs with a `Reentrant` host (`VmHostThreading`, include/primec/runtime/VmHost.h). Decide how a host call (or the program around it) gives the scheduler a switch point, then let a poller and its workers make progress on the deterministic scheduler.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option D, no yield: the deterministic scheduler keeps no host-call switch point; a poller with workers on the VM needs `--vm-threads` with `Reentrant` host functions, and the scripted tests keep the blocking-closure form.
  - implementation_notes: the scheduler is `VmTaskScheduler` (src/runtime/VmTaskScheduler.cpp), host calls are dispatched through `VmHostFunctions`/`VmHostBinding` (include/primec/runtime/VmHost.h) and the threaded mode is src/runtime/VmThreadedTasks.cpp. The test that works around the limit is in tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_serve_workers.cpp.
  - acceptance:
    - docs/spec/vm-design.md (Tasks) and docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md (VM Threads) state that a host call is not a switch point and what a poller with workers needs
  - stop_rule: the scheduler and host-call yield semantics only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: Decided by the owner as option D: no yield. The rule is documented in docs/spec/vm-design.md (Tasks) and in docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md (VM Threads, "A host call does not yield on the deterministic scheduler"); tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_serve_workers.cpp keeps its blocking closure on a `Channel`. No code changed.

- [x] TODO-6074: An args pack destroys the `String`s of its elements
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-19
  - phase: Lifecycle (found while finishing TODO-5727)
  - parallel_track: lifecycle-temporaries
  - scope: `total(Box{[text] label(3i32)}, Box{[text] label(4i32)})` for `total([args<Box>] xs)` leaves both `String`s on the string heap after the call (measured on the VM: `heapLiveBlocks`/`stringHeapBytesInUse`). `emitStructPackedValueToSlots` (src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererInlinePackedArgs.cpp) copies each element into the pack slots, disarms a temporary argument (the pack takes it over) and does a shallow slot copy of a named one (no `Copy` helper, no disarm), and the callee never destroys the pack, so the pack owns what a temporary gave it and borrows what a place gave it, with no record of which.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option A: the pack owns every element. A named argument runs its `Copy` helper into the pack slot, like a vector push; a temporary is taken over as today; the callee destroys all elements of the pack when its body ends. This changes a named argument's cost and its `Copy` side effects (state it in docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md). Options B (a drop flag per element) and C (the caller destroys the temporaries after the call) are not taken. `[spread]` forwarding of a pack hands ownership over as a vector move does; it must copy when the source pack is still used.
  - implementation_notes: the matrix cases copy the shape of tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_user_at_sources.cpp. The `[auto]` `Result` half of the original leak is TODO-6096.
  - acceptance:
    - matrix cases for an args pack of `Box` temporaries, of named `Box` arguments (one `Copy` per element, one `destroy` per element, the original still usable) and of a forwarded pack end with the heap statistics of the start on VM and optexe
    - docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md states the pack ownership rule
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: ownership of args-pack elements only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: An `[args<T>]` pack of a struct with something to destroy owns its elements. A temporary argument is taken over (as before), a named one is copied into its pack slot through the struct's `Copy` helpers after the slot copy (one `Copy` per element, the original stays usable), a `[spread]` forwarded pack is copied element by element instead of aliasing the caller's pack, and the inline callee registers a drop entry per element (first element destroyed first) when its body ends. A pack of a struct with nothing to destroy, of scalars and of `Reference`/`Pointer` elements is unchanged (the predicate is the struct's destroy helpers; forwarding still aliases). Before: `total(Box{[text] label(3i32)}, Box{[text] label(4i32)})` left 64 bytes of string heap on the VM, a named pack leaked the same. Code: emitStructPackedValueToSlots in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererInlinePackedArgs.cpp and the pack drop entries in src/ir_lowerer/IrLowererLowerInlineCallsBody.h. Cases: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_pack_owners.cpp (5; suite pack_owners), `PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all`: the four String heap cases (temporaries, named, forwarded, mixed forwarded) on vm-step-O0, vm-O0, vm-O2 and optexe-O2 (heap statistics and `String` exist there only), the plain-struct case on every config including native-O0/O2. The stdlib `String.opPlusMany` took an `args<String>` pack and borrowed its parts, so a fused chain `a + b + c` now passes the parts after the first as `.view()` (the template-monomorph rewrite) and the pack is `args<StringView>`; the one-allocation guarantee holds (tests/unit/backend_host/test_string_conformance.cpp caught it). Not covered: a forwarded owning pack always copies (a hand-over without a copy when the source pack is dead afterwards needs a last-use analysis the lowerer does not have); Wasm, GLSL and the simple C++ emitters have no `String`. Spec: Args packs paragraph of docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md.

- [x] TODO-6096: An `[auto]` local of `Result.ok`, `Result.map` or `Result.and_then` is the stdlib `Result` sum and destroys its payload
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - created_at: 2026-11-20
  - phase: Lifecycle (split from TODO-6074)
  - parallel_track: lifecycle-result-auto
  - scope: `Result.map(Result.ok(1i32), [maker]([i32] v) { return(Box{[text] label(v)}) })` held by an `[auto]` local, or read by `try` from one, leaks the mapped `Box`'s `String` (measured on the release VM and optexe: 32 bytes, one `String`). It does not leak for a typed local (`[Result<Box, i32>] r{...}` destroys the payload once). The semantic product types `[auto] m{Result.map(...)}` and `[auto] r{Result.ok(Box{...})}` as `i64` (a packed legacy Result), the payload lives in untracked struct slots next to it, `try(m)` copies it out through `Copy` and nothing destroys the original.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option A: infer the stdlib `Result<T, E>` sum for an `[auto]` local whose init is `Result.ok`, `Result.map` or `Result.and_then`, so the existing sum drop applies (the binding type text changes from `i64`). Options B (a drop entry for the legacy packed payload) and C (refuse `[auto]` with an owning payload) are not taken.
  - implementation_notes: the binding type inference for `[auto]` locals and the packed legacy `Result` producers are in src/semantics (search `Result.ok`, `Result.map`) and src/ir_lowerer; the matrix cases copy the shape of tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_user_at_sources.cpp. Check that `E` is inferred from the init and that an `[auto]` local of a `Result` with a scalar payload keeps its results.
  - acceptance:
    - matrix cases: an `[auto]` local of `Result.map` yielding a `Box`, one of `Result.ok(Box{...})` and one of `Result.and_then`, each read by `try`, end with the heap statistics of the start on VM and optexe
    - existing `Result` matrix cases and `/std/result` tests unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the type of an `[auto]` local of the three `Result` producers only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - resolution: Template monomorphization writes the type of such an `[auto]` local out (`TemplateMonomorphAutoResultBindings.cpp`, called from `rewriteNameAndTransforms`): when `Result` resolves to the stdlib sum from the definition's namespace, `[auto] m{Result.map(src, lambda)}` becomes `[Result<T, E>] m{...}`, so the declared-type path (instantiation, sum drop) applies. `E` is read from the source (a typed local, a nested `Result.ok`) or, for `Result.ok`, from the definition's `on_error` or `Result` return; `T` is the payload type or the type every `return` of the lambda has (for `and_then`, the value type of the `Result` it returns). A local whose `T` or `E` cannot be read stays the packed builtin `Result`, which also remains the behavior without the `/std/result/*` import. A direct `Result.ok(x)` source of `map`/`and_then` is rewritten to `/std/result/ok<T, E>(x)`, and the IR lowerer (`IrLowererLowerSumHelpersConstructEmit.cpp`) now writes that source's tag and payload with the source's sum definition instead of the target's (a direct sum-helper source of a combinator failed with `stale semantic-product sum variant metadata` also for a declared local). Tests: three cases in `test_program_matrix_user_at_sources.cpp` (map yielding a `Box` from a direct `Result.ok` and from a typed local, `Result.ok(Box{...})`, `and_then`), each read by `try` and ending with the heap statistics of the start (vm-step-O0, vm-O0, vm-O2, optexe-O2; 32 bytes leaked before). Not covered: a lambda whose returns differ in type or sit in a nested block binding, a `Result.ok` in a definition with neither `on_error` nor a `Result` return, a `Result.map` source that is a call (a user function) or another combinator, `Result.map2`, a declared local with a direct `Result.ok` source of a combinator (still `stale ... source query metadata`), native and Wasm (no heap statistics there; the semantic path is shared).

  - scope: A closure `[ref keeper]([Reference<i64>] value) { keeper.kept = value }` with `keeper` a struct that has a `[Reference<i64>] kept` field is accepted; the assignment copies or rebinds in a way that does not alias the parameter today, and nothing says what assigning to a `Reference` field means. Also: a closure that returns its `Reference<T>` parameter returns a copy of the value without a diagnostic, and `return(location(value))` is `unable to infer return type`.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option C: `Reference` fields are construction-only. A field of type `Reference<T>` is bound once by brace construction and an assignment to it (`keeper.kept = value`) is a diagnostic (`Reference field cannot be reassigned: kept`, naming the field); a write through it uses a method or `*kept = value`. So there is no escape through assignment and no rebinding semantics to define. Options A (assignment writes through) and B (assignment rebinds) are not taken.
  - implementation_notes: found with `Mutex.locked`, whose body gets a `Reference<T>` that must stay in the body (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Mutex). Build the construction-only rule as one reusable field-modifier check (one place that says "this field is set only by brace construction"), because TODO-5854 adds the unstored `ctor_only` field on top of it. The escape checks are in src/semantics (search `borrowed parameter escapes`, src/semantics/SemanticsBorrowedParameterMessages.cpp); the field assignment target checks are the `assign target must be a mutable binding` path. Return cases: returning a borrowed `Reference<T>` parameter from a closure whose result is not itself `Reference<T>` is `borrowed parameter escapes via return: value` (the existing message); `return(location(value))` infers its pointer type or reports a message that names the way out.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: reading through the parameter, assigning through it and constructing `Keeper{value}` still work
    - negative: `keeper.kept = value` in the closure above is `Reference field cannot be reassigned: kept`; the closure that returns its `Reference<T>` parameter and `return(location(value))` each report a diagnostic with file, line and column
    - docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md (Lambdas) and docs/spec/type-system.md state the construction-only rule
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the `Reference` field assignment diagnostic and the two return cases only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: A `Reference<T>` field is construction-only (decision 2026-11-20, option C). `fieldBindingFor` and `fieldAssignmentDiagnostic` in `src/semantics/SemanticsFieldModifiers.{h,cpp}` are the one place that says a field is set only by brace construction; the assignment-target check (`validateMutableFieldAccessTarget`) asks it, so `keeper.kept = value` (also through a `[ref]` closure capture) is `Reference field cannot be reassigned: kept` with file, line and column. Extension point for TODO-5854: its `ctor_only` field modifier adds a case to `fieldBindingFor` (returning `ConstructionOnly`, or a new `FieldBinding::ConstructionOnlyUnstored` enumerator that layout, destroy and copy ask for), so the assignment diagnostic and any later check see one answer; the brace-mapping and layout changes live elsewhere. A closure that returns its `Reference<T>` parameter by value is `borrowed parameter escapes via return: value` (restricted to closure definitions), and `return(location(value))` of a closure reports `unable to infer return type` at the position of the `location(...)` call with the way out. No stdlib type had a `Reference` field that was assigned, so nothing needed migration. Tests: 5 cases in `tests/unit/semantics/test_semantics_lambdas.cpp`; spec: value-lifecycle.md (Lambdas) and type-system.md (Ownership and Mutability).

- [x] TODO-5854: A `Mutex` or `Atomic` handle does not keep the value it was made from
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: mt-a (worktree-agent-a62e8ffb18ecbfa15), 2026-11-20
  - created_at: 2026-11-10
  - phase: Multithreading (docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md, Mutex)
  - parallel_track: mt-primitives
  - scope: `Mutex<T>{value}` maps `value` to the struct's first field, `initial`, and the heap cell gets a copy of it; the field then stays in every handle. A `Mutex<vector<i64>>` handle therefore owns a vector of its own, a handle copy copies that vector, and each handle destroys one. Make the handle two pointers and a flag: the value moves into the cell when the mutex is made. `Atomic<T>` keeps its `initial` the same way (an integer, so only the size matters).
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option A: a construction-only parameter. A field modifier such as `[ctor_only T move] initial` takes the brace argument, is visible to field defaults (`value{mutexValueAlloc<T>(initial)}`) and is not stored (no layout slot, no implicit destroy, no `Copy`). It extends the construction-only field concept that TODO-5853 builds for `Reference` fields (one field-modifier check, implemented once: TODO-5853 makes a field bound at construction only, this leaf adds the variant that is also not stored), so this leaf starts after TODO-5853. Options B (`move` of a field in a default) and C (a `makeMutex` factory) are not taken. The concept also serves `Channel` and `SharedString` handles later.
  - implementation_notes: stdlib/std/sync/sync.prime. The brace-mapping rules, the struct layout of every backend and the struct-brace spec (docs/spec/type-system.md) change for fields that exist only during construction; tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_mutexes.cpp ("locked returns the body's value...") prints the copies and destroys of a `Noisy` element and must then show one copy at most and one destroy.
  - acceptance:
    - positive: the `Noisy` program prints no `copy` for a handle copy and one `destroy` in all; heap statistics stay balanced; the handle no longer holds a `T`
    - negative: `Mutex<T>{}` without a value for a `T` that has no default is still a diagnostic
    - docs/spec/type-system.md and docs/MultithreadingPrototype.md (Mutex) describe the `ctor_only` field
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the construction-only (unstored) field modifier and the handle layout of `Mutex` and `Atomic`.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: `ctor_only` is a field modifier (a transform on the field binding, like `[mut]` and `[public]`) for stdlib struct fields: the brace argument is read by the defaults of the fields after it and the struct does not store it. `fieldBindingFor` (src/semantics/SemanticsFieldModifiers.{h,cpp}) returns the new `ConstructionOnlyUnstored` for a binding with `BindingInfo::isConstructionOnly`; the one syntactic predicate every struct-field walk asks is `isUnstoredConstructionField` (include/primec/ast/AstFieldModifiers.h). Semantics: `constructionOnlyPlacementError` (run by `applySemanticTransforms`) rejects `ctor_only` on a local, a parameter, a field of a struct without `[struct]` (`ctor_only is only valid on struct fields: /def/name`), together with `static`, and on a field no later default reads (`ctor_only field is never read by a later field default`, which would leave the moved-in value undestroyed); reading the field after construction (`handle.initial`, `this.initial`) is `construction-only field is not stored: /Type/name`; the struct layout pass, the semantic product's field metadata and count, the sendable check, the ownership walks (`ownsResources`, drop and relocation trivial), requirement and reflection field lists and the field-index lookups skip it, while the constructor argument mapping still has it (a field with no default makes `Mutex<T>{}` `argument count mismatch`). Lowerer: `isStaticField` (layout) and the struct slot layout treat it like a static field (no slot, size 0, flagged `isStatic` in the IR layout, which only the lowerer reads), and `emitInlineStructDefinitionArguments` walks the field parameters in order: an unstored one is evaluated into locals of the constructing frame (a scalar into a local; a struct or builtin vector into a block, a temporary moved in with its source disarmed, a place copied through the copy helpers) and bound by name for the defaults after it. Every backend sees only the IR, so the VM, native, `optcpp`, `optexe` and `exe` need no change. stdlib/std/sync/sync.prime: `Mutex<T>` and `RwLock<T>` have `[ctor_only T move] initial` and `mutexValueAlloc<T>([T move] value)` (the value moves into the heap cell, no copy); `Atomic<T>` has `[ctor_only T] initial{convert<T>(0i32)}` and `load` takes its width from `convert<T>(0i32)`. Result: a `Mutex<T>` handle is 24 bytes for every `T` (an `Atomic` is 16), a handle copy copies no `T`, and the `Noisy` program of the mutex matrix prints `made 10 copied 10 destroy` with 3 and 0 heap blocks (before: `copy` twice and `destroy` three times); a mutex made from a local copies it once. Tests: tests/unit/semantics/test_semantics_construction_only_fields.cpp (nine cases), two cases in tests/unit/semantics/calls_and_flow/test_semantics_calls_and_flow_mutexes.cpp (`Mutex<Tally>{}` and `cell.initial`), tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_frontend_accept.cpp (`ctor_only` scalar, default, struct argument by temporary and by place) and test_program_matrix_mutexes.cpp (the `Noisy` expectation, a mutex made from a local, handle sizes from the IR layout dump); each matrix case run once with `PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all` (vm-step-O0, vm-O0, vm-O2, native-O0, native-O2, optexe-O2 and exe for the frontend case; the mutex cases on vm-step-O0, vm-O0, vm-O2, native, optexe-O2, VM seeds 1 to 3 and the VM threads config). Checked and left: `Channel<T>` keeps no value it was made from (its stored `capacity` is an `i32`) and a `SharedString` is filled after it is made, so neither has the pattern; `RwLock<T>` had it and got the same field. Not covered: a `ctor_only` argument that no default takes by `move` is not destroyed (rejected only when no default reads it at all); the field is stdlib surface syntax and is not in docs/CodeExamples.md. Found: `init(*slot, v)` of a non-empty builtin `vector<T>` stores one slot, so `Mutex<vector<i64>>{vector<i64>(1i64, 2i64, 3i64)}` holds an empty vector (also before this change; TODO-6098).

Case "a block place given to a move parameter is copied" in tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_uninitialized_slots.cpp: struct with a vector field, `vector<i64>`, bare name, `move(x)`, a `Destroy` struct; vm-step-O0, vm-O0, vm-O2, optexe-O2 (heap statistics) and native-O0, native-O2 (values and `Destroy` prints); PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all run once, green. Not covered: `map` and `soa` slots (TODO-6103), a slot of a vector of vectors of structs, a slot reached only through a local without a type transform; reading an element of a vector of vectors through a `Reference` frees its buffer (TODO-6104).
