- [x] TODO-5956: Native string arenas and the remaining string heap statistics
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: string-arenas (worktree agent-ad3f1a3afe8d1ebc3), 2026-11-20
  - created_at: 2026-11-12
  - phase: Native PrimeScroll (docs/NativeUiPlan.md; follows TODO-5586)
  - parallel_track: native-backend-strings
  - scope: The arm64 native backend answers `__pstext_stat` for chunks, bytes in use, large blocks and bytes, and blocks handed out, and `__pstext_set_limit` over the bytes of live text blocks, but `stringHeapBytesFree()` and `heapLiveBlocks()` (statistics 2 and 8) stop the program with "string heap statistic is not available on the native backend", and `StringArena` (`__pstext_arena_begin` and `_end`) is rejected at validation ("string arenas are not available on the native backend yet"). The limit counts live text-block bytes where the VM counts the bytes of its chunk regions, so a program that sits close to a limit can differ. Count the slot heap's live blocks and the free blocks' bytes in the pool, and give arenas a bump region in the data segment's state.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option A: native-defined statistics, not the VM's figures. Statistic 2 (`stringHeapBytesFree()`) is the bytes of freed text blocks on the pool's free lists (a counter in `emitTextFree` and in the reuse path of the pool alloc). Statistic 8 (`heapLiveBlocks()`) is the live slot-magic blocks, a counter in the heap routines gated by `textStats_` (one global atomic counter, so a threaded program counts all threads where the VM's `liveSlotAllocationCount` is per thread heap). Arenas are bump regions mapped per arena and linked from the data segment's state (statistics 6 and 7 answered), `__pstext_arena_end` unmaps nothing that a later use could trip over silently: keep the regions mapped and fill the header of freed arena text with the free magic, so text used after its arena ended hits the existing double-free style message (exit 3) rather than SIGSEGV; the limit counts text-block bytes. No startup cost for a program that does not use the figures. Option B (a second allocator mirroring `VmTextHeap`) and option C (keep faulting) are not taken.
  - implementation_notes: the native heap is one shared slot pool (256 KiB chunks, size classes shared by all blocks) while the VM's text heap is per-size-class chunks (4 KiB first chunk, doubling to 256 KiB, free chunks returned beyond a 1 MiB cap), so `chunks` and absolute `bytesFree` differ even today. The tests print relations and deltas (a figure after minus before, balanced to zero, `live` goes up by one per live block), never absolute `chunks` or `bytesFree`. docs/spec/vm-design.md (or the native backend spec) lists the differences between the VM's and the native figures.
  - acceptance:
    - `stringMemory()`, `heapLiveBlocks()` and a `StringArena` program (the programs of `tests/unit/runtime/test_vm_heap_arenas.cpp`, rewritten to print relations and deltas) run through `--emit=native` with the VM's output
    - text used after its arena ended reports the free-magic double-free message and exit 3 on native
    - the spec lists the differences in the figures
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the native string heap's arenas and the two statistics only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: The arm64 native backend answers every string heap statistic and runs `StringArena`. Statistic 2 is the class bytes of freed pool blocks (counted in the pool's free and reuse paths), statistic 8 the live slot blocks (HeapAlloc and its free, one atomic counter for all threads), 6 and 7 the open arenas and their text bytes. An arena is a chain of 256 KiB regions (`NativeEmitterInternalsArm64Arena.h`) with a bump pointer, linked from the data segment's state; ending it writes the free magic into its blocks (a later free is the double-free message, exit 3), and its standard regions go on a free list the next arena reuses. The figures that differ from the VM's are in docs/spec/strings-and-views.md. Tests: tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_string_arenas.cpp (6 cases on the VM configs, optexe and native), and the heap-statistics matrix helpers of early_returns, sum_owners, pick_values and vector_owners now run native too. Found and filed: TODO-6117 (stale arena text is read and written silently), TODO-6118 (larger regions never unmapped), TODO-6119 (arenas of a module with tasks only count).

- [x] TODO-6115: A `Function` field of a lambda parameter cannot be called: `b.f(x)` is `unknown method`
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: lambda-field (worktree-agent-aea48cb30770b2538), 2026-11-20
  - created_at: 2026-11-20
  - phase: Function values (docs/spec/value-lifecycle.md; found with TODO-6113)
  - parallel_track: lambda-function-field-call
  - scope: `[struct] Box() { [Function<i32, i32> mut] f{} [i32] base{0i32} }` and `run<Body>([Body mut] body, [Box] box) { return(body(box)) }`; `run([]([Box] b) { return(b.f(b.base)) }, b0)` reports `unknown method: /Box/f [PSC1005]`, while `read_it([Box] b) { return(b.f(b.base)) }` as a free function compiles and runs (prints 5 for `f` adding one to 4). The `b.f(x)` to `b.f.call(x)` rewrite in `TemplateMonomorphCallableRewrites.cpp` (the field-callable rewrite, around line 140 to 190) resolves the owner of `f` through the locals and parameters it is given, and the parameters of a lambda are not in that scope, so the call stays a method call of `/Box`. The same call with the `RwLock<Box>.read` lambda of TODO-5804 fails the same way.
  - acceptance:
    - the repro prints 5 for a lambda parameter, a lambda parameter that is a `Reference<Box>`, and a lambda nested in a generic `Body` call, with semantics and compile-run tests
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: resolving the owner type of a field call inside a lambda body; whether a read-only `Function` may be called is TODO-6113 and TODO-6116.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: The cause was the namespace of the lifted closure `call` method (`/main__lambda0`), not the lambda's scope: the field-callable rewrite resolved the parameter's bare type `Box` in that struct namespace and found nothing, so `b.f(x)` stayed a method call. `resolveStructTypeVisibleFromMethod` (TemplateMonomorphCallableRewrites.cpp) now continues the search at the namespace that holds the closure struct, as `importedStructPath` does. Tests: semantics (by value, `Reference<Box>`, nested in a generic `Body` call) and a compile-run program on every closure config. No mutability check was added or removed (TODO-6113, TODO-6116).

- [x] TODO-6080: A diagnostic column and snippet are those of the source the user wrote, not the text-filtered form
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: filter-offsets (worktree-agent-aea48cb30770b2538), 2026-11-20
  - created_at: 2026-11-19
  - phase: Correctness audit 2026-10 (split from TODO-5520)
  - parallel_track: diagnostics-filtered-columns
  - scope: A semantic error in `[i32] b{a + 2i32 * nope}` prints line 4 column 34 and the snippet `plus(a, multiply(2i32, nope))`; `nope` is at column 22 of the file. The text filters rewrite operators into calls and keep no offset map.
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option (a): the text filter records each rewrite as an edit (original range, filtered range), an offset map from the filtered text back to the user's source, and spans, columns and snippets map back through the edits, so a diagnostic shows the user's text and true columns. The token-aligning heuristic (b) and printing both lines (c) are not taken.
  - implementation_notes: the filters are in src/text_filter (search the operator and call rewrites); the edit list is carried by the parsed program or its source record so `primec` diagnostics, `--collect-diagnostics` and the semantic product spans use it; imports and stdlib text keep their own maps.
  - acceptance:
    - a diagnostics test asserts file, line, column and the snippet of an error inside an operator expression and a rewritten call, and of an error after a rewritten span on the same line
    - diagnostics of programs without rewrites are unchanged
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: spans and snippets only.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: A text filter run can track where each byte came from: `Text` (src/text_filter/TrackedText.h) is a `std::string` whose slices and appends keep a source offset per byte, so the offset map falls out of the rewrites with no per-rewrite bookkeeping (a byte a rewrite wrote, such as the `plus(` of `a + b`, is marked synthesized and maps to the next copied byte, so a rewritten call reports the start of its expression). `TextFilterPipeline::applyWithOrigins` returns the origins and `TextFilterOffsetMap` maps a filtered line and column to the source's. `ExpandedSource::textFilterOptions` (set after the transform stage) lets the source location mapper build the map on the first diagnostic by running the filters again with tracking, an error path only, and map the spans of every diagnostic through it before it looks for the source unit (the instruction source ranges of the lowerer keep the plain lookup, so a program that compiles never builds the map; startup of `primevm` on a stdlib-importing program measured +0.55 percent instructions retired, a small program +0.1 percent); the CLI cuts the snippet from the expanded source. The normal run tracks nothing (one branch per write). Decided against per-rewrite edit records: the origin of every copied byte is the same map without a bookkeeping call at each of the roughly 70 rewrite sites. Not covered: positions in `--dump-stage` output and the semantic product stay those of the filtered text; the columns of the IR source map the debugger reports are TODO-6121 (rewritten expressions); the snippet of a diagnostic in an imported file is TODO-6120.

- [x] TODO-5718: All values of a repeated parameter and decoded path parameters
  - owner: ai
  - status: done
  - claimed_by: web-params-a (worktree-agent-ab18fa13ddf892207), 2026-11-20
  - created_at: 2026-11-07
  - phase: Web apps (docs/WebAppsPlan.md; found by TODO-5702 and TODO-5703)
  - parallel_track: web-params
  - scope: `queryParam` and `formParam` give the first of repeated parameters (`?tag=a&tag=b`), so a form with checkboxes or a multi-select cannot read every value; and `pathParam` returns the segment as sent, so `/files/a%20b` gives `a%20b`.
  - decision: 2026-11-20. (1) All values of a name: count plus index, like the header accessors: `queryParamCount(name) -> i32` and `queryParamAt(name, index) -> String`, and the same for `formParam` (`formParamCount`, `formParamAt`); each call rescans the text, nothing is allocated beyond the returned String, an out-of-range index gives an empty String. A `vector<String>` form is not taken. (2) Path segments: `pathParamDecoded(name) -> String` decodes only `%XX` and leaves `+` alone (a `+` in a path is a literal plus, RFC 3986; option b); a `%` not followed by two hex digits, or bytes that are not UTF-8 after decoding, gives an empty String; `pathParam` still tells a missing segment, so no `hasPathParam` is needed. `queryParam` and `formParam` keep their decoding (`+` is a space).
  - acceptance:
    - VM and optexe tests: three values of a repeated query and form parameter in order through the count and index accessors, an out-of-range index, a `%20` and a kept `+` in `pathParamDecoded`, a malformed `%` and a non-UTF-8 segment (empty String)
    - docs/spec/stdlib-reference.md and docs/WebAppsPlan.md updated
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: repeated values and decoded path segments only; no typed parameters, no multipart.
  - finished_at: 2026-11-20
  - result: `Request` has `queryParamCount`/`queryParamAt`, `formParamCount`/`formParamAt` (count and index, each call rescans, out-of-range index gives an empty String) and `pathParamDecoded` (decodes `%XX` only, `+` stays; malformed `%` or non-UTF-8 gives an empty String). `urlencoded_pair` is now `urlencoded_pair_at(text, name, 0)`, and `percent_byte_at` is the byte decoder without the plus rule. Test: tests/fixtures/http/repeated_params.prime on the VM and through optexe.

- [x] TODO-6090: The program matrix runs the programs Wasm supports on a Wasm config
  - owner: ai

  - phase: Correctness audit 2026-10
  - parallel_track: wasm-matrix
  - depends_on: TODO-5744 (done)
  - scope: `PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS` (tests/unit/program_matrix/program_matrix.h) has no Wasm config. A survey (every raw-string program of tests/unit/program_matrix/test_program_matrix_*.cpp compiled with `--emit=wasm --wasm-profile wasi` and run under node, 365 programs, 2026-11-20) found 47 that already print and exit as the VM does (27 of control, 6 optimizer, 5 shared_programs, 4 user_shadows, 1 each of conversions, frontend_accept, parameter_modes, runtime_faults, struct_methods), 2 that only differ because the runner reads the result of a `void` main, and 316 that do not compile for Wasm (about 200 `unsupported opcode for wasm target`, 23 `unsupported effect mask bits`, 19 atomics, 18 channels, the rest frontend errors of programs that need a flag or are fragments).
  - decision: 2026-11-20, option (a): the Wasm config is slow and opt-in (`PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all`) and runs only the cases that list it in `onlyConfigs` (about 47 annotations, so a backend gap stays visible as the absence of the annotation). Options (b) (about 316 `skipConfigs`) and (c) (`wasmUnsupported`) are not taken. The config adds `Backend::Wasm` to `ExecutionConfig` and `runConfigUnnormalized`: `primec --emit=wasm --wasm-profile wasi ... -o x.wasm`, then `node` with a runner like `WasmNodeRunner` in tests/unit/compile_run/smoke/test_compile_run_smoke_wasm_node.cpp; a `void` main is exit code 0; a Wasm trap is a fault outcome (exit 3 under WASI once TODO-5744 lands, which this leaf depends on); a machine without node skips the config with a message (`hasNode`).
  - acceptance:
    - the Wasm config runs the cases that list it in `onlyConfigs` (the 47 programs of the survey) and agrees with the VM on stdout and exit code, a trap as the fault outcome
    - a machine without node skips the config with a message
    - full release gate green
  - stop_rule: the config and its annotations only; opcode gaps found by it (heap, strings, atomics, channels) are separate leaves.
  - notes: a matrix helper such as `check()` that returns an `if` expression could not run on Wasm until TODO-6089 (a value-yielding `if`) was fixed.
  - result: The program matrix has a Wasm config, `wasm-wasi` (`Backend::Wasm` in tests/unit/program_matrix/program_matrix.h): `primec --emit=wasm --wasm-profile wasi`, then the module runs under node (`WasmNodeRunner`: WASI `fd_write` for stdout, `proc_exit` as the exit code, the result of `main` modulo 256 otherwise, a `void` main is 0). It is opt-in: the config has `optIn`, so neither the default set nor `PRIMESTRUCT_MATRIX_CONFIGS=all` runs it; a case runs it when it lists `wasm-wasi` in the new `ProgramCase::extraConfigs` (run in addition to the default set, also for a case that has `onlyConfigs`). The block named `onlyConfigs`, but that would have dropped the VM, native and C++ configs the program must still agree with, so the listing is a separate field. It checks stdout and the exit code against the oracle (or the case's expectation); stderr is not compared. A machine without node prints `SKIP: node is unavailable; wasm-wasi did not run <program>` and runs the case's other configs. The task helper skips opt-in configs (it built its list from `allConfigs()`). A survey of every program of the matrix (511 `runProgramMatrix` calls, 2026-11-20, run on `vm-O2` and `wasm-wasi`) found 56 that agree: 29 of control, 6 conversions, 6 of the optimizer, 5 shared_programs, 4 user_shadows, 2 math (`atan2`, `fma`), and one each of frontend_accept, parameter_modes, runtime_faults, struct_methods; those 56 list `wasm-wasi`. The other 455 stay visible as the absence of the entry: 369 `unsupported opcode for wasm target` (TODO-6124), 32 `unsupported effect mask bits`, 18 atomics, 16 channels (TODO-6128), 2 u8 conversions, 1 host call, 1 `/std/gfx` (TODO-6127), 2 `unsupported control-flow pattern` (TODO-6126), 3 integer divisions by zero that end in a raw wasm trap instead of `proc_exit(3)` (TODO-6125), and about 11 negative or fragment programs that do not compile on any backend. Cost: the 56 programs add one `primec` and one node run each (about 0.15 s per program) to cases that already run three to seven configs. Spec: the header comment of program_matrix.h. Not covered: wasmtime (not installed), the browser profile (a trap is its fault outcome and has its own tests in tests/unit/compile_run/smoke/test_compile_run_smoke_wasm_node.cpp), Linux and x86_64 hosts (the run was on macOS arm64).
